fields.name: amount_pop_value
fields.doc:
Estimated-Order-Value pop over the amount input (V1
`OptionTradePanelPresenter.inputCalAmountPop` →
`OptionsTradeInputUtils.getProbablyValue`): "≈ {fiat symbol}{value}"
as a `DisplayString` (locale grouping applied by Kotlin resolve).
`Simple("")` when price/amount empty or the derive is not applicable.
Producer: `on_price_changed` / `on_amount_changed` / `on_percent_changed`
via `OptionLimitOrderManager.evaluate_*_change`.

fields.name: cached_index_ticker
fields.doc:
Underlying index price for the tapped strike's `uly` (V1 indexTicker,
sourced from `TradePageDataRepository.indexTickerItemLiveData.value?.price`).
The option bottom-sheet is per-strike and the shared main-page session's
`InstContext` is NOT on this strike, so the estimated-value derive cannot
read the index off the session/`new_minimal` context (no IndexPrice data
source). Producer: `fetch_option_instrument_detail` (async, keyed by the
fetched `detail.uly`). Consumed by `recompute_amount_pop` as the index
override so the "≈ value" pop shows while typing. Empty until it lands.

fields.name: cached_ct_mult
fields.doc:
Option contract fields for the tapped strike, cached from the per-strike
`fetch_option_instrument_detail` fetch. The shared session / option biz
`get_biz_info_for_id(inst_id)` frequently MISSES the tapped strike (the
whole reason `fetch_option_instrument_detail` exists), so the per-keystroke
est-value pop derive cannot rely on the biz map for `ct_mult` / `ct_val_ccy`
/ `ct_type` — a miss yields `OptionInstrument::default()` (empty ct_mult →
wrong coin_amt; empty ct_type → CM misclassified). Cache them here so
`recompute_amount_pop_on_handle` builds an accurate InstContext (V1
`getProbablyValue` reads these off `getBizInfoForId`, which on the main
page DOES have the strike). Empty until the detail fetch lands.

fields.name: amount_unit_symbol
fields.doc:
Amount-input unit chip token (V1 setAmtUnit): the Zhang CDKey
`pr_options_footer_switch_amount`, or the instrument coin symbol when
the user's option trade-unit setting is COIN. Kotlin resolves via
`resolveCdKey`. Producer: `recompute_amount_unit_display` (instrument
landing + `refresh_amount_unit`). Empty until the instrument lands.

fields.name: amount_unit_options
fields.doc:
Selectable amount-unit rows for the pure unit-switch bottom sheet (V2 of
the OKTradeCore-bound `TradeUnitContractAndOptionBottomSheet`). Option has
exactly two rows — COIN (label = instrument coin symbol, V1
`isShowDetailedCoin=true` used by the option panel) and CONTRACT (CDKey
`pr_options_footer_switch_amount` = Zhang/contract). `is_selected` reflects the live
option trade-unit setting. Native renders the sheet purely from this list
(B1: no OKTradeCore / BizInstrument). Producer:
`recompute_amount_unit_display` (instrument landing + `refresh_amount_unit`
+ `on_amount_unit_changed`). Empty until the instrument lands.

fields.name: amount_digit
fields.doc:
Unit-aware amount precision (V1 `OkOptionBiz.getAmountDigit`):
contract unit -> `sheetDig` (integer Zhang), coin unit -> `contractDig`
(coin decimals). Producer: `recompute_amount_unit_display`. Native consumes
this for both units; zero is a valid integer-only precision and must not be
replaced by a lotSz/quote-digit fallback. 0 until the instrument lands.

fields.name: price_prefill_done
fields.doc:
One-shot latch for the ticker auto-prefill. V1 `loadInitTicker` fills the
price input exactly ONCE on sheet entry; after that the field is the
user's to edit. Set true the first time the ticker seeds a price, so a
user who CLEARS the price is not re-seeded by the next streaming tick
(the bare `price.is_empty()` guard alone refills on every empty tick).

fields.name: displayed_avail_balance
fields.doc:
Final max-available values for the UI. Unlike `max_avail`, which keeps
raw Zhang/margin values for seekbar calculations, this record already
applies the legacy option precision and rounding rules.

fields.name: available_unit_symbol
fields.doc:
Unit paired with `displayed_avail_balance.available` (option margin
symbol, e.g. BTC or USDC).

fields.name: max_buy_sell_unit_symbol
fields.doc:
Unit paired with the displayed max-buy/max-sell values. PM-cross uses
the margin symbol; standard accounts use the selected option amount unit.

fields.name: price_tick_error
fields.doc:
Price tick-size hint marker for the inline price-input error (V1
`OptionLimitTradePanelPresenter.priceChangeListener` →
`TradeInputUtils.getPriceTickSizeMsg`). Empty = no hint. Non-empty format:
`"tick_size|{multiple}|{number}"` (mirrors multi-leg `low_amount_error`),
where `{multiple}` = instrument tick size and `{number}` = the auto-adjusted
price. Kotlin resolves it into `pr_trade_text_tick_size_hint`. Derived on
every `on_price_changed` (see `validate::derive_price_tick_size_msg`).

fields.name: amount_lot_error
fields.doc:
[BugOptLimitAmtLot] Amount lot-size hint for the inline amount-input error
(V1 `OptionLimitTradePanelPresenter.amountChangeListener` →
`TradeInputUtils.getAmtTickSizeMsg`). Mirror of the advanced sibling
(`OptionAdvancedState.amount_lot_error` / `amount_lot_corrected`).
`amount_lot_error` = the lot-size multiple (e.g. "0.01" coin / "1" Zhang),
`amount_lot_corrected` = the snapped amount; BOTH empty when the amount is
lot-aligned / empty. Kotlin resolves them into `pr_trade_text_tick_size_hint`
(element [1] = auto-fill value). Derived unit-aware (coin/contract) via the
manager on every `on_amount_changed`.

amount-percent seekbar for PM-unique accounts (V1

Projected from `PureOptionLimitInteractorArgs.subtype` at init; drives
the price-field split (px / pxUsd / pxVol, with UM USD orders routed to px)
and tickSize-skip for IV.

fields.name: multiple_price
fields.doc:
Canonical BE-converted multiple-price (px / pxUsd / pxVol) for the
CURRENT price input. Producer: `convert_prices` effect →
`OptionLimitOrderManager::convert_price`. Consumers are request,
precheck, max-available, and estimated-value derivations; the renderer
intentionally uses `published_multiple_price` instead. Empty for
BASIC_LIMIT (no conversion needed — the raw input IS the px).

fields.name: px_vol_display
fields.doc:
Display-formatted IV equivalent for the multiple-price row (V1
`OptionPriceUtils.formatIvPrice`: `pxVol × 100`, DOWN-rounded to
`DEFAULT_IV_DIGIT` (1) decimals, rendered as a percent). `multiple_price.px_vol`
stays the RAW BE ratio (needed verbatim for the order request `pxVol`), so
the human-readable "297.4%" lives in this separate field. Emitted as
`DisplayString::Percent` (already ×100-scaled value) so Kotlin only ICU-
formats + appends "%". Producer: `convert_prices`; empty/`Simple("")` when
no conversion / px_vol blank.

fields.name: published_multiple_price
fields.doc:
Last successfully published equivalent-price projection for the UI.
Unlike `multiple_price`, this display-only snapshot may remain visible
while a newer non-empty input is being converted. Submit, precheck,
max-available, and estimated-value logic must never consume this field.

fields.name: published_px_vol_display
fields.doc: Display-only IV companion of `published_multiple_price`.

fields.name: price_digit
fields.doc:
Price-input decimal precision for the CURRENT subtype. Producer:
`recompute_price_display_derives` (BASIC = decimals(tick_sz),
TRACKING_IV = 1, TRACKING_USD = 2). Consumer: RenderExt
`setDigitalPrecision`. 0 until instrument resolves.

fields.name: price_unit
fields.doc:
Price-input unit label for the CURRENT subtype. Producer:
`recompute_price_display_derives` (BASIC = quote_ccy, TRACKING_IV = "%",
TRACKING_USD = "USD"). Consumer: RenderExt `setInputUnit`. Instrument-
aware for BASIC, so emitted from Rust rather than derived in native.

fields.name: max_avail_tip_type
fields.doc:
Max-available tooltip type for the max-buy/max-sell labels. Mirrors V1
`OptionTradePanelPresenter.updateMaxBuySellTip`: Cross + account-level /
auto-loan decide whether the buy (and, for cross-multi-no-borrow, the
sell) label shows the help-text underline + click popup. Written at both
instrument-commit sites in `option_limit_interactor.rs` alongside
`resolved_td_mode`; `Isolated`/`None` = no tip.

fields.name: precheck_resp
fields.doc:
Raw pre-check resp snapshot from the LAST successful `precheck_order`
call. Producer: `precheck_order` action (interactor) — written from the
`OrderPreCheckResp` returned by `LimitOrderManager::pre_check_order` on
`is_success`. Consumer: `orchestration::confirm::b016_get_order_confirm_data`
— the margin MMR / before-after / cost confirm rows are sourced from
THIS field (server convention), NOT the local `calculate_margin_mode_margin_info`
guess. `None` until the first successful precheck (b016 then falls back
to the local cost guess for backward compat).

fields.name: has_position_for_inst

Whether the account holds an OPTION position on the CURRENT instrument.

[BugOptSimpleSellGate] Sole consumer is the simple-account sell gate
(`check_sell_permission`, V1 `OptionTradePanelPresenter.simpleOptionSell`
→ `checkOptionPosition`): on a simple account (L1) selling is only allowed

monolith `OptionLimitInteractor.start_position_subscription`).

doc:
Round 19 NF-5 (2026-05-21) · Available-balance label kind.

V1 reference: `AbsSpotTradePanelPresenter.kt:847-860` selects between
two i18n keys for the available row title based on a 3-AND branch:
```text
if (currentAccountHasMultipleAttr() &&
currentMarginMode == MGN_ISOLATED &&
isMarginOrSpotReduceOnly() != true) {
text = R.string.pr_margin_title_margin_available  // "Margin avail."
} else {
text = com.okinc.tradeuilib.R.string.pr_trade_text_avail // "Avail."
}
```

Kotlin RenderExt reads this enum and chooses the right resource id.
Producer: `orchestration::borrow::derive_available_label_kind` (called
from `recompute_borrow_derives`). The two new input mirrors
(`is_iso_margin_spot_mode`, `is_margin_or_spot_reduce_only`) default
`false` until the host bridge wires the producer chain — until then
the derive returns `Default` and the Kotlin path is unchanged
(`pr_trade_text_avail`). This is structurally safe — same visible text
as today; switch only fires after producer lands
(EMIT_PENDING(T-AVAILABLE-LABEL-MARGIN-MODE-PRODUCER)).

name: get_display_title
doc:
Pre-formatted header subtitle title for the adjust-margin sheet.

Replaces the Native `TradeTitleUtils.getTitleByIdAndType(inst.getInstId(),
inst.getInstType(), false)` call in `RustAdjustMarginBottomSheet.kt:154-155`
(Native passed `getInstId()` + `getInstType()` scalar getters into the
title util — two A2 reads). `format_trade_title` uses the default options
(simple=false, swap suffix Short), exactly matching the Native third-arg
`false` (= `isSimple=false`, default `swapWithSuffix=true`). Native
resolves the `CTTradeTitle` CDKey segments and joins them.

Exposed as a synchronous getter (not via the async `Loaded { details }`
VO) because the subtitle renders at sheet open, before the first
`query_initial` result arrives — same lifecycle slot as the existing
`get_inst_id` / `get_inst_type` getters it supersedes.

doc:
Initialization parameters for the unified facade, sealed by scenario.

All 7 variants ship full payload parameters as of Phase 1.5 — Native
callers must build the concrete variant matching their scenario (no unit
placeholders remain). Adding fields to a variant is additive and safe;
removing or reshaping fields is a breaking change.

name: build_attach_sync
doc: Build attach params synchronously. Returns empty vec if manager not ready.

name: on_hidden
doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase).

Distinct from `on_pause`: the Pure host swaps StrategyType panels via
show/hide keep-alive (NOT re-inflate), so a hidden panel does NOT get
Activity-level `onPause`. Native, by contrast, re-inflates a fresh
Fragment per StrategyType, so it shows a blank draft on every order-type
switch. Amount lives in Rust state and survives hide/show, so to mirror
native we clear the input draft (amount + probably/total + seekbar) ONLY
on this hide transition — NOT on `on_pause` (which also fires on app
backgrounding, where native preserves the typed amount).

Kotlin routing: `PureSpotAdvancedLimitFragment.onHiddenChanged(hidden=true)`
calls `on_pause()` (max_avail reset) AND `on_hidden()` (draft clear);
`Fragment.onPause()` (backgrounding) calls only `on_pause()`.

Keeps `price` intact (sibling parity: post-submit + side-switch resets
keep the limit price). Additive action — forward-compatible; existing
bindings that never call it are unaffected.

name: PureAdvancedLoadState

name: query_inline_tpsl_projection
doc:
Query trade-panel TPSL preview echo rows (Trailing / Multi).
Returns empty vec for OCO — Kotlin's renderAdvanceEcho handles that path.
V1 parity: TPSLConfig.getDisplayInfo() (TPSLConfig.kt:223-270).
Thin wrapper — all derivation in orchestration::tpsl_echo.
Single-source close-path projection (Phase 1, H5). Replaces the
Kotlin 3-branch decision in `renderEchoRowsFromBinder`: the echo-rows
mode, the OCO-echo gate and the per-leg ByPrice blank gate all derive
HERE from the kernel, so cancel-vs-confirm-vs-clear needs no
Kotlin-side guessing (the close paths are indistinguishable there).
Byte-parity with the retired Kotlin gate: kind is the kernel
`tp/sl_strategy_kind` (the Bug-X routing authority the Kotlin mirror
tracked) and emptiness is `compute()`'s `*_trigger_px_api` (the same
source `currentOcoPrefill` read).

retype to DisplayString — those callers parse it numerically.

fields.name: trade_quote_ccy_list

Tradable quote-ccy options for the bound instrument (e.g.
`["USDT", "USDC"]` for a dual-quote USDⓈ pair, empty for a
single-quote pair like BTC-USDT). Sourced from the parent session's
instrument sub-record on every InstrumentChanged / bind

name: sync_order_type_epoch
doc:
Order-type switch epoch sync (Native destroy+recreate parity). Native
rebuilds the whole trade-panel fragment on an order-type change (orderType
is part of `FutureOrderCache` cacheKey), so the attached TP/SL starts
fresh (unchecked + empty). V2 is keep-alive, so the panel + this attached
child survive the switch. The Kotlin host polls this once on the panel's
visible/render tick (same timing as the panel interactor's own
`maybe_reset_on_order_type_switch`); it compares the session order-type
generation with the last-seen value:
- sentinel `u64::MAX` (first sync) -> adopt WITHOUT clearing (deeplink-
preset attach is preserved);
- unchanged -> no-op (④ hide/show re-visit preserves the attach);
- changed -> `reset_after_order` (keep the checkbox CHECKED + the simple
by-rate value, clear by-price / advanced) + return `true` so the host
runs `resetTpslAfterOrderSuccess` (box handling, NO uncheck). Native
rebuilds the fragment which re-reads the per-instType checkbox SP + the
global by-rate SP, so an order-type switch is NOT an uncheck / full wipe
(corrected 2026-07-31; earlier `clear_all_tpsl` + uncheck was wrong).
Returns `true` at most once per real order-type switch.

(`../../spot/market/pure/spot_market_interactor.rs:437`).

No parent session (`Weak::new()`): the session-reading subscriptions
(`spawn_session_subscription` / `spawn_cool_state_subscription`) short-
circuit on their `session.upgrade() == None` guard, and
`spawn_side_subscription` no-ops on `side_rx == None`. The manager is
seeded with a default swap instrument (same fallback `new_with_session`
uses when the session has no instrument). The host sends only identity;
Rust resolves the real snapshot and retries when the cache loads late.

doc:
Semantic color tone for a leverage input section's value + unit.

Rust emits **intent only** — the dual long side is `Up`, the dual short side
is `Down`, every other scenario is `Neutral`. Native maps the tone to a

name: PureTransferPrefill
doc:
§12 formula (b) · transfer entry pre-fill snapshot (Rust-resolved).

Holds **all** data Native needs to launch the Transfer Activity:
- `currency` already contains the V1 fallback (`OrderShowUtils.getSpotTransferSymbol`
equivalent) — empty input ccy → quote_symbol (BUY) or base_symbol (SELL).
- `amount` follows V1 `InsufficientBalanceUtil.getInputCcyAmount` —
LIMIT BUY = probably_value, LIMIT SELL = amount/sz.
- `currency_id` is the integer ID required by `FundTransInTradingPageUseCase`,
resolved via `CTRSTrade::instance().coin_wrapper()?.get_coin_by_symbol`
— Native receives a ready int (0 = not-found / coins-not-loaded).
- `is_new_coin_blocked` mirrors V1 `CommonUtil.isNewCoinOnLineAndNotWhiter` —
when true, click should toast `pr_trade_transfer_toast_unavailable_notlist`
instead of launching Transfer.

Single source of truth (R-ARCH-3): derived inside Rust orchestration at every
state mutation that affects (side / instrument / probably_value / amount /
trade_quote_ccy / is_new_coin_disabled). Native never recomputes; it only
reads this struct via state push or consumes the matching UxEvent payload.

Written via `set_input_amount` from the `onAmountInputChanged` hook in the Kotlin

recompute always uses the session last price as the deal price (KB45 Behavior 1).

Raw trade-unit code of the amount input ("0"=coin / "1"=zhang / "2"=settle-ccy /
"3"=lot, KB37). Persisted so the cost recompute can convert the unit-denominated
`input_amount` into zhang via the #60a dispatch. Writers: `on_amount_unit_changed`
+ `update_instrument_snapshot` / `project_session_instrument_into_state` (default
unit on bind). Consumer: `recompute_input_cost` (R-MIG-167).

fields.name: is_tpsl_supported

panel; forced false for the K-line quick-order compact panel (mirror of

`!is_quick_order`.

native-layer A1 — the compact fragment reads it, never infers it. Gates
inline TP/SL (`is_tpsl_supported = !is_quick_order`). Mirror of spot
`PureSpotMarketState`'s quick-order classification.

fields.name: tpsl_market_price

NOTE: this collapses OFF and PENDING to `false` -- it is only for the
asset-row tag and MUST NOT be used to drive the first-entry guide /
page routing. Use `auto_earn_state` for that.

fields.name: auto_earn_state
fields.doc:
Real 3-state auto-earn status for this asset, mirroring native
`AssetsListItemBinder.getEarnStatus()`. Carries the raw `AutoEarnState`
string value ("off" / "pending" / "active"; empty only in the
not-supported fall-through, which native `jumpToAutoEarn` treats as OFF).
Kotlin maps this 1:1 onto `com.okinc.unify_trade.utils.AutoEarnState` and
passes it to `TradeAssetsUtils.jumpToAutoEarn`:
OFF     -> first-entry guide + AutoEarnPageType.OPEN
PENDING -> no guide + AutoEarnPageType.OPENED
ACTIVE  -> no guide + AutoEarnPageType.OPENED
Unlike `is_auto_earn_active` (row tag), this does NOT collapse PENDING to
OFF, so a first-time PENDING user correctly skips the guide.

fields.name: is_flash_icon_active
fields.doc:
Whether the flash (quick) icon is active for this asset's auto-lend row.
Mirrors native `ConvertAssetsData.isShowFlashIcon()` (ConvertAssetsData.kt:529):
`(supportAutoLend && autoLendStatus in {pending, active})
&& (supportAutoStaking && autoStakingStatus in {pending, active})`.
NOTE: this differs from `is_auto_earn_active` (which is OR + active-only):
flash icon is AND of BOTH legs and each leg is PENDING-OR-ACTIVE.

fields.name: is_support_auto_earn
fields.doc:
Whether the currency supports auto earn (drives "{CCY} Rewards" vs "Auto Earn" button text).
When true, the button text should be "{CCY} Rewards"; when false, "Auto Earn".

fields.name: earn_type
fields.doc:
Auto-earn type for this asset, used to route to the correct AutoEarnActivity page.
"1" = Lend only, "2" = Staking only, "3" = Lend + Staking.
Empty string when auto-earn is not supported.

fields.name: is_equity_positive
fields.doc:

Used to determine default trade direction for TP/SL and Buy/Sell actions:
true (eq > 0) → default SELL direction, false → default BUY direction.

fields.name: default_buy
fields.doc:
Default Buy/Sell direction for the asset Buy/Sell sheet.

`= !is_equity_positive` (eq <= 0 → default BUY, eq > 0 → default SELL).
Mirrors Kotlin `PureAssetBuySellBottomSheet.newInstance(defaultBuy = !vo.isEquityPositive)`.
Computed in Rust so the native layer reads a ready value.

fields.name: cost_price
fields.doc:
Cost price selected for the asset Buy/Sell sheet (raw, unformatted).

Mirrors Kotlin `getCostPrice(openAvgPx, accAvgPx)` with the call-site
defaults `isFormat=false, isFormatToLocal=false`:
- `CostPriceConfig.isAverageCostPrice()` (spotAverageConfig == 0 → AvgCost):
if `open_avg_px` is empty → `"--"`, otherwise the raw `open_avg_px`.
- otherwise (TotalCost): if `acc_avg_px` is empty → `"--"`, otherwise the
raw `acc_avg_px`.

Note: the `isFormatToLocal=true` USD→local-fiat formatting branch of
`getCostPrice` is NOT mirrored here — the Buy/Sell call site passes
`isFormatToLocal=false`, so only the raw selection applies. If a locale
formatting variant is ever needed it must stay on the native layer
(USDToLocalConvertor + fiat symbol formatting).

fields.name: reminder_state
fields.doc:
Reminder warning state — drives `OKReminder(STYLE_WARNING)` visibility and message.
`None` = hide reminder bar. Mirrors Kotlin `AssetsListItemBinder.handleReminder()`.

fields.name: open_avg_px
fields.doc:
Open average price in USD (from account balance).
Used when CostPriceConfig.isAverageCostPrice() == false (open price mode).

fields.name: acc_avg_px
fields.doc:
Accumulated average price in USD (from account balance).
Used when CostPriceConfig.isAverageCostPrice() == true (average cost mode).

fields.name: is_navigable
fields.doc:
Whether this asset is navigable to a trade page.
true = has a tradeable SPOT pair AND is not a stablecoin → show arrow + click.
false = stablecoin or no SPOT pair → hide arrow.
Mirrors Kotlin AssetsListItemBinder: `bizInstrument != null && !isStableCoin(name)`.

fields.name: show_share
fields.doc:
Whether to show the share icon for this asset item.

Mirrors Kotlin AssetsListItemBinder:
`isSupportAllInstruments() && isPnlPerNotNullOrEmptyOrBlank() && !isStableCoin()`

Rules:
- account_level != "1" (unified account, supports derivatives)
- has non-empty / non-zero PnL ratio (there's something worth sharing)
- not a stablecoin (is_support_spot_avg_cost == true)

Native: shareIcon.isVisible = showShare

name: bind_instrument
doc:
F1 wave-5 B1 — write just the inst_id slot. Sibling parity:
`spot_advanced_limit_interactor.rs::bind_instrument` (line 1612).
Used by KlineQuick / Amend / panel re-attach to populate the
inst_id before the full snapshot fetch resolves.

DEVICE-FIX (2026-07-07 coin-switch stale unit/ccy): re-project the FULL
instrument snapshot from the session synchronously + re-fetch max-
available (OCO twin of the Single sibling fix). Without this, switching
pair while the panel stays open left base_ccy / unit / button stale
(buy button + max-buy still showed BTC on an ETH panel), because the native
full-snapshot push was removed and the async session event was the SOLE
re-projection path. Also restamps `balance_inst == inst_id` so the percent
seekbar's `compute_amount_by_percent` stops returning empty.

name: update_context_pricing
doc:
Push the parent order's reference price and lever / position-size
hints (used by ByRate + ByProfit). The host passes whatever it has;
any field left `None` keeps the previously-set value.

`open_sz` is the MARGIN position asset (native `positionPrice` =
`mPositionItem.pos`). It is otherwise seeded ONLY at binder CREATE
(`init.open_sz`, :4477); the position-TP/SL binder is cached
(`getOrCreate`) and never re-seeded, so when `positionData.pos` was
empty at create the MARGIN by-price est-profit had no order amount /
`position_asset` and `compute_pnl_display_by_price` returned `None`
("--"). This ADDITIVE, optional param lets the host re-seed `ctx.open_sz`
once the late position size arrives (mirrors the additive `positionLiab`
precedent). Some & non-empty overwrites `ctx.open_sz`; `None` / empty
leaves it untouched, so spot / contract / order-entry callers (which pass
`None`) are unaffected. `order_amount` already falls back to
`ctx.open_sz` and `position_asset = ctx.open_sz` (by_price.rs:1319/1355),
so seeding it here is sufficient for the MARGIN branch to compute.

cache misses (otherwise OKMarket picks the wrong event tab).

`is_login` / `is_support_derivative` so native dispatches by a
single `when(entry)` instead of branching on the raw signals (per
`spec/interactor.md` §A1 / §D — Interactor surfaces decisions, not

doc:
One-shot UI events emitted from header click actions that carry **Rust SSoT
payload**. Native (Kotlin/iOS/Harmony) subscribes via `setUiEventObserver`
and routes each variant to the corresponding dialog / page / sheet
(Android: `RustHeaderNavigator`).

Scope rule (issue 05 ADR — see plan §F audit):
* Every variant **must** carry a Rust-owned payload (`instId` /
`instType` / `marginLevel`). Emitting the full payload atomically at
click-time guarantees parameter consistency vs the alternative of
letting native re-read multiple state fields just before navigation.
* If a future click destination needs **no Rust-owned payload at all**
(neither for the destination nor for tracking), prefer pure Kotlin
`onClick` → navigator call to avoid Thin Relay drift
(interactor-spec §D / §F).

`OpenCoinSearch` follows S1.Q2 "thin payload" decision: native reads
`derivativesNavConfig` / `showConfigTimes` / `shouldShowNavGuide` from
platform prefs after the event fires.

The existing, non-AU body copy. Also the DEFINED fallback when the feature-restriction fact
is unresolved: a non-AU client shown AU copy is a correctness defect on every entity,
whereas an AU client briefly shown the existing copy is recoverable and is still gated from
trading by the show-condition.

Named `Standard` rather than `Default` so the variant name never collides with the `Default`
trait in Rust nor with a reserved word in a generated binding.

doc:
Which body copy the TradFi-perps risk-disclosure sheet renders.

Deliberately a VARIANT ENUM rather than a Rust-emitted `pr_*` CDKey: a Rust-emitted key must be
registered in BOTH Kotlin resolution cache tables, and a miss in one renders the raw key while a
miss in the other renders an empty string — on a compliance screen. Emitting a variant instead
keeps no key crossing the FFI boundary, so neither table needs an entry. Native maps the variant
to its own `R.string`.

There is intentionally NO third "unresolved" variant. The readiness fallback (FR-2-AC-3) resolves
an unavailable feature-restriction fact to [`Self::Standard`] inside Rust, so every value Native
can ever observe is already a real decision. Native therefore never needs a
placeholder-versus-resolved predicate, and cannot accidentally treat the default variant as
"not yet known".

Kotlin getter does (`SIDE_BUY_POSITION = "buy"` / `SIDE_SELL_POSITION
= "sell"`, identical on both sides).

completed (success or failure). The CeX HTTP amend path lives in

HTTP call the WS pushes the same order back with `amendResult` /

so Kotlin can apply the same skip rule end-to-end.

fields.name: max_size_display
fields.doc:
Max size ALREADY truncated to the target-ccy display digit, via the
same `convert_margin_trade` leaf convertor the margin-limit branch
calls. Native cannot re-derive this itself here: the shared dialog's
convertor branch is typed on `PureMarginLimitState`, so the market
surfaces passed `state = null` and silently fell back to a plain
`formatRustNumber(max_size)` — which only groups thousands and keeps
every digit Rust sent, so an unclamped server `max_size` rendered at
full precision. Precision is Rust's responsibility (native-layer A2),
so it is projected here instead. Suffix-inclusive, exactly like the
limit branch's `convertMarginTrade(...).display`; the dialog appends
the ccy separately and strips the suffix.

variants.name: ShowMaxMarketSizeExceededOnInput
variants.doc:
INPUT-time single-order cap toast (Lark recvviKLNszt9V, margin half).

Native shows this WHILE TYPING, straight from the amount input-change listener:
`MarginMarketTradePanelPresenter:80-92` -> `TradeMarketMaxSizeUtils.calSpotMarketSize`, which
toasts `pr_trade_placeorder_toastamount_can_not_exceed` and returns the boolean. The panel is
NOT blocked: no submit rail is touched, no keyboard is dismissed, and re-crossing the cap
toasts again (native re-runs the check on every keystroke — it is not edge-triggered).

Same payload as the spot sibling `PureSpotMarketUxEvent::ShowMaxMarketSizeExceededOnInput`.

name: TradeSessionHandle
doc:
Opaque cross-crate / cross-FFI handle to the trade session.

This exists solely so another crate's UniFFI factory (e.g. the retail-kline
K-line interactor) can receive the current session **without
`TradeSessionContext` itself crossing the FFI boundary or appearing on the
ABI**. Native holds it opaquely and passes it straight back into the
factory; it exposes no methods over FFI.

It wraps a `Weak`, so keeping the handle alive never pins the session past
its owning `MainTradeInteractor` (mirrors the child-interactor rule that the
session reference is always `Weak`). A dead `Weak` simply upgrades to `None`
and the consumer degrades gracefully.

Only `MainTradeInteractor::trade_session_handle` constructs this; there is
deliberately no `#[uniffi::constructor]`.

fields.doc:

fields.name: price_raw
fields.doc:
Machine-readable twin of `price_text`: the value a depth tap fills.

Behavior Contract = Native `DepthP.kt:142 / :160`, which hands the widget's DISPLAY
price straight into `price.formatS()` (`com.okinc.core.ktx`, the numeric-sanitiser
family). So this is `price_text` with formatting stripped, which means:
* it IS the rounded price (bid down / ask up by `ladder_digits`), not the
pre-rounding `OKTFormattedDepthItem::un_format_price`;
* for the `<{ladder}` lower edge bucket (row price 0, amount != 0 -- the sentinel
label from `depth_batch_convertor.rs:186-188`, mirroring native
`DepthM.kt:123-126`) the sanitiser leaves the ladder number: tapping "<10" fills
10, exactly as native does. Same for the EVENTS ">{1-ladder}" upper bucket.

Why the field has to exist: `price_text` is a DISPLAY value and is NOT always a
number. Feeding it to the order panel verbatim put the literal "<10" in as a price --
it parses nowhere, so the option sheet's IV plus its available / max-buy / max-sell
rows collapsed to "--" and flickered (recvvCBHHRkTfd, reproduced by tapping the "<10"
row; a numeric row was fine). This is the price-axis counterpart of `amount_raw`
below, which exists for the same reason on the amount axis.

EMPTY means "no numeric price on this row at all", and the host's existing
`price.isEmpty()` click guard then makes the tap a no-op. The edge bucket is NOT such
a row -- it carries the ladder.

name: MultiSlEditFocusField
doc:
R1b — render-ready projection of the stop-loss leg currently being EDITED in
the V1 `MultipleSlSettingFragment` "set multiple SL" dialog.

# Why this is separate from `PureContractMultiTpEditProjection`
The SL setting dialog differs STRUCTURALLY from the TP one (this is not a
1:1 mirror of R1a — verified against V1, not assumed):
- **No percent / progress.** A MULTI batch has many TP legs that split the
position by percent (`MultipleTpSettingFragment` seek-bar + `calcEstimateAmount`
+ set/remaining/full progress), but exactly ONE stop-loss that closes the
FULL position (V1 `MultiSlDetailView.kt:82-93` renders the constant
"100%"). So there is no `estimate_amount` / `set_percent` / `left_percent` /
`is_full` here — those TP fields have no SL analog.
- **No fragment-local compute to move.** R1a migrated
`MultipleTpSettingFragment.calcEstimateAmount:374` (a Fragment-local
`TradeAvailableManager` A1 violation). `MultipleSlSettingFragment` has ZERO
local arithmetic — it delegates entirely to `UniSetTpSlView` / the shared
`mSlPresenter` (`AbsTpSlPresent`). The only render-time derived value the SL
edit form shows is the estimated PnL, which this projection owns so the
eventual Kotlin pure-ification reads Rust state instead of the shared
presenter (A1: Rust owns the compute).

# Single SSoT note — what is and isn't here
The SSoT inputs (`edit_sl_trigger_px` / `_ord_px` / `_is_limit_kind` /
`_is_cost_price` / `_trigger_px_type`) cover the **trigger-price input mode**
(worklog scope #2). The V1 4-input-type cross-derivation
(price-change / pnl-rate / pnl-amount / dynamic — `TP_SL_BY_PRICE_CHANGE` /
`_RATE` / `_PNL` / `_DYNAMIC`, deriving the trigger from a PnL-rate /
PnL-amount / price-change input) is NOT wired here: it lives in the shared
`mSlPresenter`, not in the
SL dialog, and porting it is a separate design-gated round (the
`attach_facade::calc_trigger_price_by_rate` / `_by_pnl_amount` calculators
already EXIST — A3: reported as deferred, not fabricated).

# V1 source map (MultipleSlSettingFragment.kt / UniSetTpSlView.kt)
- `estimate_pnl`     ← SL PnL at the SL effective price for the FULL position
(`calc_pnl_display_by_price`, the SAME ByPrice formula as the OCO reverse SL
+ R1a TP profit). Signed; typically negative (a triggered SL is a loss).
`Placeholder` when not derivable (no effective price / metadata not loaded /
non-derivative inst — A3: no fabrication).
- `trigger_px` / `ord_px` ← echo of `edit_sl_trigger_px` / `edit_sl_ord_px`.
- `is_limit_kind`    ← limit-order (xian-jia) checkbox (`isSlLimitCbChecked`,
`UniSetTpSlView.kt:435`). Distinct from `is_cost_price` (verified: separate
controls).
- `is_cost_price`    ← cost-price (cheng-jiao-jia) SL (`slSwitch` →
`AMEND_PX_ON_TRIGGER_TYPE_OPEN_PRICE` → `isOpenPriceSl()`,
`MultipleSlSettingFragment.kt:213/244`). Trigger == mother order price, so
the estimated PnL at break-even is ~0.
- `trigger_px_type`  ← `slTriggerType` (last / mark / index).
- `is_estimate_visible` ← whether `estimate_pnl` is derivable (V1 shows the
SL PnL bubble only when the trigger yields a value).

Bug A (device: empty trigger / empty limit-order price on confirm neither
focuses the box nor blocks) — which SL-edit input the confirm should focus
when it hard-blocks on an empty required field. Native
`OKTFuturesMultiSLModuleVC.m valueIsValid` / `MultipleSlSettingFragment`
`getSlPriceInfo(checkValid=true)`: empty trigger -> focus trigger; limit-order
checked + empty order-px -> focus order-px. `None` = valid / not blocked.
One-shot: set only by a blocked `on_multi_sl_edit_commit`, read once by the
dialog, reset to `None` by the next projection recompute.

name: query_max_available_reference_px
doc:
Worst-case stop-loss reference price the **position-margin** TP/SL editor
feeds into its max-available fetch (B1 / Plan §2.5 step 1).

This is the Rust replacement for the Kotlin
`PureUniSetTpSlView.getMaxAvailablePx(side)` (`PureUniSetTpSlView.kt:687`),
which currently calls the trade_impl-local `StopLimitPriceEx.kt`
`getSingleStopLossPx` / `getDoubleStopLossPx`. It reads the kernel's
already-API-converted trigger / order prices + market flags directly from
the current `compute()` outcome (so no conversion is duplicated), then
dispatches single- vs double-leg exactly like the Kotlin host:
- TP selected only  → `get_single_stop_loss_px` on the TP leg
- SL selected only  → `get_single_stop_loss_px` on the SL leg
- both selected     → `get_double_stop_loss_px`
- neither selected  → `None`

`side` is the V1 close-direction side string (`"buy"` = `SIDE_BUY_POSITION`
short-position ×1.05 / max ; `"sell"` = `SIDE_SELL_POSITION` long-position
×0.95 / min). Returns `None` where Kotlin returns `null` / `""` (caller
then omits the price from the max-available request). The numeric work
lives in `business::tpsl::domain::stop_reference_px_use_case`, a pure port
of `StopLimitPriceEx.kt` that the margin-OCO panel's `balance.rs` arm
already validates — one parity-checked implementation, two callers.

Called by Native when a display-only setting that the row VOs read at
derive time changes while the list is already visible — currently the
"show realized PnL in positions" switch (`CHANGE_REALIZED_PROFIT_SWITCH`).
The switch value is already synced into the trade-setting cache (native
awaits `setRealizedPnlSwitch`'s optimistic local write before posting the
event), so the row VO gate `is_show_realized_pnl` reads the fresh value
once the pipeline re-runs. Unlike `on_visible`, this does NOT restart the
WS subscription (avoids market-data churn / flicker) and does NOT depend
on a market push arriving — it deterministically re-publishes the current
snapshot. Mirrors native `SimplePositionsFragment`'s IMMEDIATE re-render.

name: close_amount_display_for_percent
doc:
UI-ready order-quantity DISPLAY value for the seekbar percent (SWAP / FUTURES),
in the position-list trade-unit (contract/coin/USD/Lot) with FULL baseDig precision.

Mirror native `ConfirmPositionMoveSPView` seekbar `posActualAmtTv`
(`ConfirmPositionMoveSPView.kt:262-274`): raw contract (zhang) proportional amount
(`getFutureAmountCal`) → `toTargetFormatted` trade-unit conversion. Unlike
`close_amount_for_percent` (the SUBMIT-basis path, which lot-snaps the result
and thereby drops coin decimals — device: DOGEUSD CM coin "988,529 DOGE" vs
native "988,529.5743 DOGE"), this DISPLAY path keeps baseDig and does NOT
lot-snap. `percent` is the 0..1 seekbar fraction; `price` the live ticker price
(empty falls back to `position.last`). Returns `DisplayString::Placeholder`
for MARGIN / SPOT / OPTION / non-contract (host keeps its existing fallback)
and for non-positive base/percent. Pure read-only delegation to the manager.

fields.name: tp_type
fields.doc:
V1 line 179 / 255 — TPSL value-classifier enum from
`TradeConst.kt:756-760`:
- `TP_SL_BY_NONE = -1` (default sentinel; V2 surfaces as `0` when
TPSL is not OCO/checked so the Kotlin layer's `>= 0` gate works
identically to V1's `TP_SL_BY_PRICE` post-coalesce branch)
- `TP_SL_BY_PRICE = 0` (by absolute price — V1 default for spot
advanced-limit, set at V1 leaf:179-180)
- `TP_SL_BY_PNL_RATE = 1` (by P&L percentage)
- `TP_SL_BY_PNL = 2` (by P&L amount)
- `TP_SL_BY_DYNAMIC_PRICE = 3` (by dynamic-percent trigger;
the only non-PRICE producer V2 currently has)

**Round 10 CG-3 fix (R9 audit close)** — V1 leaf:189-194 reads
`getTPSLPresenter()?.getTPSLConfig()?.tpType` and coalesces
`TP_SL_BY_NONE` → `TP_SL_BY_PRICE`. V2 derives the value from
`PureTpslConfig`:
- When `tp_dynamic_trigger_px` is `Some` and non-empty →
`TP_SL_BY_DYNAMIC_PRICE` (3), matching V1 (`OkTradeOrderShowData`
carries `tpDynamicTriggerPx`/`slDynamicTriggerPx` ONLY when the
user picked dynamic-percent trigger)
- Otherwise → `TP_SL_BY_PRICE` (0), V1's default for spot
advanced-limit

V2's `PureTpslConfig` does not yet carry the pnl-rate / pnl-amount
trigger types (sibling `spot/limit/pure/state.rs:427-445` ditto) —
the spot advanced-limit panel's TPSL widget produces only price /
dynamic-price legs, matching the V1 default of `TP_SL_BY_PRICE`.
When the pnl-rate / pnl-amount producers port (P&L-based trigger
widget), this derive widens to read them from state.

# Round 9 extension (CG-3 close per independent audit 2026-05-25)

V1 `getOrderConfirmData` (`SpotAdvancedLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:172-286`,
114 LOC) builds an `OrderShowConfirmInfo` with ~22 fields. Round 9 extends
`PureAdvancedConfirmPayload` to ship the full superset so the Kotlin V2
confirm sheet (CG-4 close) can render V1-equivalent rows without re-reading
V1 widget state.

Field-source map (per V1 leaf:232-277):
- `inst_id` / `side` / `price` / `amount` / `probably_value` — direct from state
- `subtype_key` / `order_type_key` — D-ADV-3 / D-ADV-4 derives (state.rs)
- `mgn_mode` — sibling parity, defaults to `"cash"` until margin-mode
producer ports (mirror `SpotLimitConfirmSnapshot.mgn_mode`)
- `inst_type` — V1 hard-codes `TRADE_SPOT_TYPE`; payload propagates string
- `lever` — empty until `T-ADV-MARGIN-RPC-PORT` lands (V1 line 239-243)
- `trade_quote_ccy` — empty until trade-receive ccy producer ports (V1 line 276)
- `is_full_percent` — derived from seekbar (V1 line 211 `getSeekBarPercent() == 1.0f`)
- `trade_cost` / `asset_cost` / `earn_cost` — empty until transfer-allocation
producer ports (V1 line 273-275 `getTransferAmountString`)
- `lend_amount_str` / `origin_lend_amount` — empty until borrow producer
ports (V1 line 233 `getLendStr()`)
- `tp_type` / `sl_type` / `tp_trigger_type` / `tp_trigger_px` /
`tp_ord_px` / `sl_trigger_type` / `sl_trigger_px` / `sl_ord_px` —
read from `state.tpsl_config` when TPSL is OCO + checked (V1 line 185-208)
- `is_tpsl_checked` — surfaces TPSL toggle so Kotlin sheet can hide rows
- `display_quote_symbol` / `base_ccy` / `quote_ccy` — empty until
instrument snapshot field ports (mirror sibling)

name: PureOptionMultiLegInteractor
doc:
Pure option-multi-leg interactor.

`state: Mutex<OptionMultiLegState>` gives interior mutability so the
`#[uniffi::export] impl` methods can write through `&self`. The lock is
short-lived (one method body) with no cross-await, so a plain
`std::sync::Mutex` is sufficient.

`listener: Mutex<Option<Box<dyn PureOptionMultiLegUxEventListener>>>` is
the Rust → Kotlin event sink; `None` until Kotlin calls
[`Self::set_listener`], before which [`Self::emit`] is a no-op.

`runtime: Arc<dyn interactor::EffectsRuntime>` lets the interactor pull
data ITSELF (OKTradeCore-free) — `set_inst_family` resolves the underlying
in Rust and spawns an index-tickers fetch keyed by it
(INSTRUMENT_SESSION_FIX.md §2). State is `Arc<Mutex<_>>` so a spawned
(`'static`) async task can hold a `Weak` clone and write the result back
without keeping the interactor alive.

name: query_input_style_hints
doc:
Resolve the UI-ready input-style hint (`{symbol, max_decimal}`) for a
TP/SL pnl / trigger input row. Replaces the V1 inline derivation that
the strategy binders did against `TradeCoreProxy`:

- **ByProfit** — V1 `ByProfitSpPresent.initInputStyle` (lines 257-259):
`symbol = getSuggestedInstrument(instType, instId).getProfitSymbol()`,
`maxDecimal = getBiz(instType).getProfitDigWithIndex(instFamily)`,
empty → `DEFAULT_COIN_DIGIT`.
- **ByPrice / ByDynamicPrice / ByRate / PosMarginByPrice** — V1
`ByPriceSpPresent.initInputStyle` (lines 426-427): no unit on the
trigger row (`symbol = ""`), `maxDecimal =
getBiz(instType).getPriceDigit(instFamily)`, empty →
`DEFAULT_COIN_DIGIT`.

Native applies the same value to both the TP and SL legs, so `side` is
a forward-compat selection (the kernel returns the same hint for either
leg today); it is taken so a future per-side divergence is additive.
Pure query — no state mutation, no UxEvent (interactor-spec §C `query_*`).

ends active streams, and stops effects. On Kotlin call BEFORE
`destroy()`. Includes `stop()`.

shows the borrow row. = the panel `is_lend_amount_visible` gate AND a
non-placeholder borrow amount. Rust folds the gate so Kotlin flips one flag
instead of hard-hiding the view (sibling parity: spot-market / spot-limit
confirm `is_simple_borrow_visible`). Fixes: trigger confirm hard-hid the view.

simple-borrow gate is off or the response carried no positive amounts
(native `ConfirmSimpleBorrowView` collapses).

fields.doc:

(`simple_borrow_view`) shows the REPAY row. = the panel `is_repay_amount_visible`
gate (INDEPENDENT of the borrow toggle) AND a non-placeholder repay amount, so
the confirm panel mirrors the down-panel: on a simple auto-repay account with
outstanding debt the repay row shows even when borrow is OFF. Kotlin ORs this
with `is_simple_borrow_visible` for the container, then each sub-row self-gates
on its own amount so borrow + repay can coexist. Sibling parity with
`is_simple_borrow_visible`.

same `DisplayString` the panel repay row renders (`state.repay_amount_display`).

Rust-derived OR of the borrow-row and repay-row gates. Kotlin binds
`bindPure(visible = ...)` to this one UI-ready flag instead of OR-ing in the
native layer (A1); each sub-row still self-gates on its own amount.

this `DisplayString::TradingNumber` carries the digit-truncated value +
quote symbol so the confirm DISPLAY gets thousand-separators via the
canonical Kotlin `DisplayString.resolve(ctx)` (H-1/H-3 — Rust owns
precision + trailing-zeros, Native adds grouping + suffix). Mirrors the
sibling SpotLimit confirm price row (`limit/pure/confirm/snapshot.rs:94`
`TradingNumber { symbol = quote_ccy }`). The legacy V1 builder leaves this
`Placeholder` (it renders trigger_price its own way; BUG-3 is pure-only).

amount_label_key

name: update_side
doc:

doc-strings above already assume exists ("side is read from `state.side`,
set earlier by the side-tab action"). Without it the two place-order
buttons could not be distinguished — both submitted with the default
`state.side`. Native-layer A1: Kotlin pushes the chosen direction, Rust
owns the side + re-derives everything that depends on it.

Blueprint parity: `spot_limit_interactor.rs:4317 fn update_side(side)`
(same `OKTSpotSide` param). V1 ref: `SpotTriggerFragment.kt:380
makeOrderClick(isBuy)` via the Buy/Sell place-order buttons wired in
`AbsSpotTradePanelPresenter.kt:588 initSpotBuySell` (Buy → `makeOrderClick(true)`,
Sell → `makeOrderClick(false)`).

SIBLING-DEVIATION (R-MIG-105): the blueprint `update_side` clears
price/amount/probably_value/seekbar, prefills price from ticker, resets
`bbo_warning_accepted_for_submit`, re-derives borrow/transfer_prefill, and
emits `PrefillAfterInstSwitch`. ALL of that is DROPPED here — see the
impl SIBLING-DEVIATION block for the per-field justification (no
SpotTrigger state analog. SpotTrigger keeps its trigger/order prices, but
a genuine user side transition clears amount + seekbar per the current
Native/product contract.

name: seed_preset_triggers
doc:
Seed the PRESET trigger prices (K-line quick-preset / position preset feed,
Kotlin `applyPreset`). Unlike [`Self::update_trigger_input`] — which carries
USER-TYPED trigger text already in the DISPLAY domain — preset prices arrive
in the BASE (API/USD) domain (e.g. `PositionAddTpslBean.tpTriggerPx`). The
editor kernel lives in the DISPLAY domain: the ByPrice/ByRate/ByProfit
linkage engines take a BASE entry anchor and emit DISPLAY triggers via
`to_quote_formatted`, and submit converts DISPLAY→base in
`convert_outcome_api_prices_to_base`. Feeding a base preset straight through
`update_trigger_input` therefore mismatches the display-domain trigger the
editor expects — for an inverse+fiat contract the percent/PnL linkage pairs
a BASE preset trigger with a display entry and mis-derives (device:
DOGEUSD-CM + CNY, confirm/add pages). Convert each preset base→display once
here (mirror of OCO `seed_amend_legs`'s `to_display` closure), then delegate
to `update_trigger_input`. Empty / `-1` pass through unchanged; linear/USDT
and SPOT are identity no-ops (`base_price_to_display` returns the input). A
failed lookup (standalone host, instrument not loaded) falls back to the raw
base — no worse than the pre-seed behaviour. No-op after `release()`.

NOTE — do NOT route `seed_from_order` / the amend pre-fill through this: that
path already lands display-domain values, so a second conversion would
double-convert.

from the ASSEMBLED attach leg list, so SIMPLE / Advanced OCO / Trailing / MULTI are
all covered by one source; the liq price is this panel's own per-side
max-available estimate; the whole gate sits behind `getLiuPxConfirm()`.

Callers pass the two kernel-owned values verbatim:
`PureAttachedTpslInteractor::sl_trigger_px_for_liq_check` (already BASE -- do NOT
convert again; the previous revision converted because it consumed the DISPLAY-space
`compute().sl_trigger_px_api`, which could not see a MULTI leg at all) and
`sl_trigger_ratio_for_liq_check`. Side, liq prices, the user setting and the
dynamic-ratio reference price are all resolved here.

Limit orders DO support native's dynamic-trigger-price fallback
(`FutureLimitTradePanelPresenter`:1646 overrides `supportTpslDynamicTriggerPx` to
true), whose reference is `group.optional.px` -- this panel's `input_price`,
converted DISPLAY -> BASE. Pure query (spec section C); empty `message_key` => no
warning.

name: current_spot_tpsl_config
doc:
P9-1 — the SPOT-line submit config, single-sourced from THIS kernel.

Composes the `PureTpslConfig` the spot/margin panel submit consumes
(`build_attach_algo_ords`), replacing the Kotlin
`PureTPSLViewBinder.syncToRust` mapping and its `lastAppliedTpslConfig`
carry-forward patch tissue: the kernel already remembers the
advance-confirmed order px (`compute()` order-px api), the dynamic
percent and the per-leg axes (`current_prefill()`), so no Kotlin-side
"carry the sheet's value forward while rebuilding from inline UI"
is needed.

Leg presence mirrors the Kotlin composer (`currentOcoEchoConfig`):
a leg exists when it has a static trigger (api domain) OR a
dynamic-percent ratio. Order px falls back to the market sentinel
"-1" (native `MARKET_ORDER_PRICE`), matching `syncToRust`'s inline-only
leg behavior; `build_attach_algo_ords` treats both "" and "-1"
identically (P9-0 goldens freeze that).

Returns `None` while the kernel enable gate is closed or when neither
leg is present. Parent panels keep a matching `Some/None` projection,
but the composer also gates itself so drift cannot leak a hidden attach.

name: compute_deposit_options
doc:
Pure decision function: port of `FundTransferBtnDelegate.getOptionList`'s
5-arm tree + post-filter, taking `asset_amount` as an explicit param.

Delegates to the already-ported [`GetTransferOptionsUseCase`] (business
layer) so the branch order stays the single source of truth, then maps the
internal `TransferOption` enum to the FFI [`DepositOption`].

Inputs (V1 source for each):
* `is_spot_only_entity` — `TradeCoreProxy.getTradeConfig().isSpotOnlyEntity()`
* `is_fiat_currency`    — `isFiatCurrency(currencyModel)`
* `is_cr_market`        — `isCrMarket()` (= `TradeCoreProxy.getTradeConfig().isLite()`)
* `is_login_main_account` — `TradeAccountManager.isLoginMainAccount()`
* `asset_amount`        — `FundTransInTradingPageUseCase` valuation
(`None` = API error / empty → V1 priority-5 fallback)
* `is_trade_only_coin`  — `TradeCommonUtils.isTradeOnlyCoin(currency)`
* `is_single_account` — `TradeCommonUtils.isSingleAccount()` (PRD FR4 gate)
* `inst_type`         — current pair instType (`"SWAP"`/`"FUTURES"`/`"SPOT"`),
`None` when no pair context (FR4 off). The Pure spot-limit launcher passes
`Some("SPOT")` → FR4 inert there; the future/swap entry points pass their biz.
* `settlement_currency` — resolved USD settle ccy (PRD FR6), `None` on the
plain "+" path (no settlement context → no SettlementCurrency row).

name: apply_history_seed
doc:
T-HIST-ORDER-SEED-UNIFFI — apply the V1 history-order seed
([`PureHistoryOrderSeed`]) in one dispatch, replacing the V1 Bundle
Serializable round-trip of `TradeHistoryOrderData`. Writes the seed's
instrument filter + time window + hide-canceled flag into state. An
empty `start_time` and `end_time` together mean "no seeded window" and
leave the state's default 7-day preset untouched. Either supplied bound
makes the route seed a custom window and suppresses the host's default
preset dispatch (`applyArgumentsToInteractor` cold-start window).

formula multiplies by this (native `calculateCost` `.mulS(getFutureMult())`,
canonical `CalculateContractMarginUseCase` `ct_val * count * ct_mult`). Empty /
non-numeric is treated as 1 (native `.mulS("")` no-op).

fields.name: lot_sz
fields.doc: Lot size — minimum order size increment (e.g., "1" for most swap contracts)

fields.name: tick_sz

fields.name: inst_family

fields.doc: Underlying (e.g., "BTC-USD" for event contracts; empty for most)

fields.name: max_lmt_sz
fields.doc: Maximum order size for limit orders

fields.name: max_mkt_sz
fields.doc: Maximum order size for market orders

fields.name: max_stop_sz
fields.doc: Maximum order size for standalone TP/SL market orders (`/products.maxStopSz`).

fields.name: unit_per_lot
fields.doc:
Units per lot — DISPLAY value for the TradFi "N units per lot" education
(BE simpleProduct.unitPerLot, e.g. "100" for XAU; = lotSizeStd * ctVal).
NOTE: this is NOT lotSizeStd. Do NOT use it as the lot->zhang multiplier
(that is `SwapInstrument.lotSizeStd`, e.g. "100000" for XAU) — see
contract-make-order-convertor-v2.md §13.

fields.name: is_tradfi
fields.doc: Authoritative TradFi flag (coin groups "49", guide 65). NOT unit_per_lot.

fields.name: is_xperps
fields.doc:
X-Perp perpetual flag (`rule_type == "xperp"` or inst_family ends with `_XPERP`),
mirrors Native `BizInstrument.isXPerpsPair()`. Drives the Available-row settlement
gear entry (`XPerpSettleEntryVo`); a pure instrument predicate so the `From` impls
resolve it directly via `is_x_perps_pair()` (no coin-family config needed).

fields.name: is_usd_um
fields.doc:
USDⓈ-M contract flag (`inst_id` contains `_UM`, case-insensitive), mirrors Native
`BizInstrument.isUSDUMContract()`. Same UX class as [`Self::is_xperps`] for the
Available-row settlement gear entry (`XPerpSettleEntryVo` in the new v2 API):
UM pairs share the settle-gear + red-dot + settlement-ccy row with X-Perp because
both consume the same USDⓈ-M settle ccy source (`get_usd_settle_ccy`).

fields.name: transfer_ccy
fields.doc:
Deposit-currency symbol for the Available "+"/settlement-gear fund-transfer
flow — V1 `OrderShowUtils.getTransferSymbol` returns `getMarginSymbol()` for
SWAP/FUTURES, so the `From` impls fill it via `get_margin_symbol()`. Lets the
Kotlin renderer build `CurrencyModel` from Rust state instead of the
OKTradeCore `getSuggestedInstrument().getMarginSymbol()` lookup.

fields.name: transfer_currency_id
fields.doc:
Coin id for [`Self::transfer_ccy`] (V1 `getTradeCoinInfo(ccy).id`), resolved in
`enrich_contract_snapshot` via the Rust coin-wrapper
(`coin_wrapper().get_coin_by_symbol(ccy).id`); `0` = not-found / coins not

when) native would, so the confirm sheet can render the CMR rows.

`StrategyPreCheckHelper`): gate → RPC → on success show the confirm sheet
(with CMR); **on failure do NOT show the sheet**, surface the error instead.

records two device incidents where firing this RPC for an account native
would not pre-check made the server REJECT the order outright.

degrades to `false` and lv1 wrongly renders "Orders & Positions"
(recvvyAn89DbGS). Deriving it here reads the same account-level SSoT the

name: okt_offline_is_funding_rate_time_gte_delivery_end
doc:
Check if the current funding rate time is >= the delivery end time (startTime).

Mirrors ObjC `OKTPOSWAPHandler.isFundingRateTimeEqualOrGreatThanDeliveryEndTimeWithOfflinePlanModel:fundingRate:`.

When true, Native should:
1. Hide the predicted funding rate
2. Show the current funding rate as 0%
3. Change countdown label from "until settlement" to "until delivery"
4. Use the delivery time for countdown instead of settlement time

# Parameters
- `plan_model`: The offline plan model from Interactor state
- `funding_time`: `fundingRate.fundingTime` (millisecond timestamp string)
- `quick_state`: `fundingRate.quickState` ("1" for quick delist, bypasses time check)

# Returns
`false` if quick_state is "1"; otherwise `true` if `fundingTime >= startTime`

prices to the new fiat instead of leaving stale values. Empty until the first
projection/set. Internal (not rendered). Writers: `project_session_instrument_into_

Internal (not rendered). Writers: same as `price_fiat_iso`.

Price-box (trigger / order) decimal places = ALWAYS the instrument price
digit (`get_price_digit(inst_family)`), regardless of strategy. Distinct
from `max_decimal`, which for ByProfit is the PROFIT digit (profit box).
The host applies this to the trigger / order boxes so a ByProfit leg's
trigger box keeps the real price precision instead of being capped at the
coarser profit digit (device 2026-07-10: LTCUSDT ByProfit trigger showed
38.88 / 2dp vs native 38.8845 / 4dp). Falls back to `DEFAULT_COIN_DIGIT`.

`RustEventContractDepthFragment` embeds a depth fragment with the

engine apply the `1 - price` / asks↔bids mirror when

doc:
V1 5-variant `NormalDepthViewModel` family selector.

V1 source (KB 10-depth.md section "5 business-line NormalDepthViewModel"):
each variant attaches a distinct observer set on `TradePageDataRepository`:

| Variant | Observers                                                |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| Spot    | markPriceItem + indexTickerItem (2)                      |
| Margin  | markPriceItem + indexTickerItem (2 — same as Spot)       |
| Swap    | mark + index + fundingRate + estimatePrice + offlinePlan |
| Future  | mark + index + estimatePrice (3)                         |
| Option  | tickerPriceItem + mark + index + estimatePrice + optSum  |

The variant also drives the V1 amount-precision rules
(KB 10-depth.md section "Amount precision rules"):
• Spot / Margin → 3 digits (or `max(2, minSize precision)` when <1000)
• Swap / Future UNIT_U → contract→USDT (linear 2 / inverse 3 digits)
• Swap / Future UNIT_COIN → contract→coin (linear 2 / inverse 3 digits)
• Option → 3 digits

The Kotlin Pure Fragment uses `update_variant(...)` to push the active
variant after `update_inst_type(...)`, then the renderer picks the right
column count + format helper per the table above.

13. P1#4 (2026-06-09) — pre-formatted confirm-dialog display fields.

/ `market_limit` / `trigger_type` / `trade_quote_ccy` / `symbol_type`
/ `td_mode`) are still consumed verbatim by the Kotlin SubmitHost

(`rate_value`) is empty unless the pre-check resp is present (MCC/PM path),
so the rate row self-collapses on the cash path exactly like limit.

fields.name: is_simple_repay_visible

the borrow toggle) AND a non-blank repay amount, so the confirm panel mirrors

row shows even when borrow is OFF. Sibling parity with `is_simple_borrow_visible`.

payload — Android in `FixedPnlIndicator.kt`, iOS in `OKTFixedPnlDisplayUtil`
behind a Legacy Bridge. Produced by
`business::orders::domain::details::order_detail_fixed_pnl_use_case`.

steps (project the UI-ready value → bind the typed action → only then drop
their bridge method).

than flattening ~12 scalars). Every field is UI-ready (A2): prices go through
the per-biz price convertor Rust-side; trigger-type / market labels are
CDKeys; the delegate rows honour the V1 MARKET / placeholder branches.

Populated by `configure_spot` ONLY when the sheet opens in edit mode
(a prior TP or SL trigger px is present — V1 `OrderSpotTpslP.init:35`).

P/L (`tp_pnl` / `sl_pnl` + colors): filled Rust-side (R5) by REUSING the
verified `SpotCalculator::calc_earn_amount_from_price`
(`business/tpsl/calculator/spot`). Copy-spot is SPOT-only
(`TradeOrderLeadImpl.showTpslDialog:57-62` launches this sheet only for
TRADE_SPOT_TYPE), so V1 `SpEarnsManager.getProfitLossEarn`
(`SpEarnsManager.kt:27`, called with `TNO_MARKET`, `SIDE_BUY_POSITION`,
`isContract=true`) takes the SPOT arm -> `getSpotEarn(SIDE_BUY_POSITION)` ->
`calSpotBuyEarn` = `amount*(triggerPx - avgPx)`; the same kernel
`attached_tpsl/strategy/by_price.rs:2766` reuses. See
`order_lead_sp_confirm_interactor::compute_spot_edit_pnl` for the full
formula / formatting / color provenance.

name: on_select_current_pair_filter
doc:
Select the "current pair" filter — the trade-records / panel
"current pair" checkbox turning ON. The host passes NO instrument; the
value is resolved inside Rust from the process-global, device-scoped
[`TradeBizCache`] (the same persistent source the trade panel writes on
instrument load).

No-arg on purpose (spec §D: no business-branch flag param). Clearing the
filter ("show all pairs") is NOT a second branch of this action — it is
the existing `on_set_inst_filter("", "")` path (the filter sheet's
"All" commit), so this action has exactly one behaviour.

Why resolve the value in Rust (not host-passed): the trade-records page
runs on the ORPHAN interactor (`create()`, `session = Weak::new()`), so
the session-bound `MainTradeInteractor::get_current_inst_id()` is empty
there, and the legacy native `SelectBizManager.getCurrentBizInstrument()`
reads a *different* (stale) SP cache file when the Rust vs legacy gray
gates diverge — observed: panel on `ETH-USDT/MARGIN` (Rust
`core_trading_storage`) while the legacy `config.xml` still held
`LTC-USDT/SPOT`, so the seed filtered to the wrong pair. `TradeBizCache`
keeps the current-instrument identity single-sourced in Rust regardless
of Activity / session.

doc:

capability. The host calls this from its normal render-context update,
covering an account config that loads after child construction as well as
an in-place role/account switch.

The persisted ByRate preference is deliberately not rewritten. Only the
current SIMPLE projection is downgraded, and an active ByRate raw value is
cleared instead of being reinterpreted as a trigger price. Advanced OCO,
Multi, and Trailing ownership remains untouched.

The Kotlin `com.okinc.biz.TradeType` enum has more members app-wide (see e.g.
`TradeType.toOktSide` / `.toOktSpotSide` in OKTrade), but this K-line asset-TPSL
drag path only ever sends two of them — `trade_type`'s own doc comment already
states "the only other value K-line drags is SELL_CLOSE". A full mirror of
`TradeType` would be over-scoped for this path (the other members' semantics
are not verified here); this enum intentionally covers only the two values this
VO actually receives.

Additive: `trade_type` (String, `TradeType.name()`) stays for backward
compatibility — existing callers that only set it keep working unchanged. When
`trade_side` is also set, the kernel derives `side` from it directly instead of
string-matching `trade_type` (see `decider::side_of_typed`).

doc:
R5 — composite-seed projection for the V1 `StopProfitBean` the Kotlin
Fragment hands to `UniSetTpSlView.refreshTpslView(...)`.

# Why this lives Rust-side
The V1 path builds `StopProfitBean` directly in the confirm Fragment from
`OrderConfirmData` — a `unify_trade.biz.OrderConfirmData` dependency which
`pure/` Kotlin paths cannot import per R-MIG-021. V2 canonical pattern:
every field the bean needs is owned by this Rust state, projected through
`state()` as a structured uniffi::Record, and read by the pure Fragment to
construct the bean from a single snapshot reference (no field-by-field
Bundle plumbing on the Kotlin side, no `unify_trade.*` import).

# Field semantics
Mirrors V1 [`StopProfitBean`] field names verbatim so the Kotlin
translation is mechanical. `is_market_or_bbo` is derived from
`open_px.is_empty()` (V1 parity: empty `openPx` always means
market-or-BBO entry in the limit panel).

# Critical for input-enable
`open_px` MUST be non-empty for the composite's trigger ↔ percent
cross-input math to fire (R2.5 SEV-1 root cause when this field was
empty — V1 `UniSetTpSlView.refreshInputView()` short-circuits the
input enable + cross-input listener installation otherwise). The host
adapter must pass `state.price` from the parent panel; if the user

doc:
Date format enum that maps to native OKDateEnum.

Dates need to be localized on the native side because:
- Different locales have different date formats (e.g., MM/dd/yyyy vs dd/MM/yyyy)
- Month names need translation based on locale
- Date separators vary by locale

This enum is passed to the native side where it maps to the corresponding
OKDateEnum format pattern for locale-aware date formatting.

# Native Mapping (Kotlin)

```kotlin
enum class OKDateEnum(val format: String) {
NONE(""),
DATE_FORMAT_Y("yyyy"),
DATE_FORMAT_STANDARD("yyyyMMMd"),
DATE_FORMAT_STANDARD_YM("yyyyMMM"),
DATE_FORMAT_STANDARD_MD("MMMd"),
DATE_FORMAT_STANDARD_M("MMM"),
DATE_FORMAT_SIMPLE("yyyyMMdd"),
DATE_FORMAT_SIMPLE_YM("yyyyMM"),
DATE_FORMAT_SIMPLE_MD("MMdd"),
DATE_FORMAT_SIMPLE_M("MM"),
}
```

than an `Option<attempt_id>`: there is no order attempt while the user is typing,
and the host must NOT run its `consumeOrderCompletion(attemptId)` gate on this one
(that gate exists to drop stale terminal events of a finished attempt). Additive
variant per the crate's forward-compatibility rule.

After a successful market order the Rust state
already clears `input_size` / `amount_cal` / `is_seekbar_selected`, but

then have `submit_order` return `FocusAmountInput` silently (sz is empty
in Rust but the UI shows a non-empty value — user has no feedback).

`cleanInputContent` clears the amount input after every placed order.

pattern (`clearInputs()` in SpotLimitFragment.kt:3487/4517-4545).

name: is_order_confirm_open
doc:
#55-B — build the per-submit-attempt child confirm interactor.

§J.2 parent factory: builds the render-ready snapshot + sub-order list
from the current `state()` + the order `input`, captures a `Weak<Self>`
(so the child can call back via `proceed_after_confirm`) plus the order
input and the sub-order list, stashes a clone in
`pending_confirm_interactor`, and returns the `Arc`.

DEVIATION from #55-A (A3 — segment has no PreCheck): takes only the order
`input`; there is no `OrderPreCheckData` and no CMR / liq-px panel.
Live decision-time read of the order double-confirm toggle. V1 reads
`getOrderRemindConfirm()` per order right before showing the confirm
(`FutureSegmentTradePanelPresenter.makeSegmentOrder:162`, inside the
inner `placeOrder()` AFTER the immediate-fill hint dialog), so
config-not-loaded behaves as OFF (`get_order_remind_confirm()`
default-false). Pure query (spec §C `is_*`): zero side effects. Kotlin
gates the confirm sheet on it right before `create_confirm_interactor`;
OFF -> place the order directly.

name: margin_lend_row_visible
doc:
V1 `TradeCommonUtils.needShowLendAmount(instType = MARGIN)` reduced for the
margin panel (`OKTradeCore/.../universal/utils/TradeCommonUtils.kt:225`):

```text
(instType == MARGIN || (isSpot && isAutoBorrow && isMultipleAccount))
&& otherCondition && !isAssemblyAccount()
```

For the margin panel `instType == MARGIN` and `otherCondition` defaults to
`true`, so the whole predicate collapses to `!isAssemblyAccount()`. V1
`isAssemblyAccount() == (accountLevel == ACCOUNT_LEVEL_4)`, which is exactly
Rust `trade_setting().is_pm_account()` — so this is `!is_pm_account()`.

doc:
Align a BASE ticker / K-line price to the instrument's display precision
(priceDig) for the price input box. Margin is spot-with-leverage (no inverse
fiat leg), so this is identity + `priceDig` truncation (`RoundingMode::Down`,
matching V1 `OKTChargeConvertor` and the spot / contract limit interactors'

so an arbitrary-precision tapped price is aligned before it flows through
`on_price_changed` (the verbatim controlled-input channel), which would
otherwise echo back unrounded.

Empty input or a not-yet-bound instrument returns the input unchanged.

NOTE: a new `#[uniffi::export]` method requires UniFFI binding regen before
Kotlin / iOS can call it.

(`:2047`) / `getFutureFragment` (`:2152`), i.e. on every panel (re)creation —
so switching ORDER TYPE on the same instrument re-evaluated it too. Note V1
returns early WITHOUT running the gate when the panel does not need
rebuilding (`getSwapFragment:1984-1990` / `getFutureFragment:2077-2081`), so
the host must call this from the panel-swap path only, never from a rebind.

The instrument watch alone cannot cover it: an order-type switch does not
touch the session instrument.

fields.name: price_tick_msg
fields.doc:
Price-input tick-size hint. `None` when the price is empty/zero or
already a valid `tick_sz` multiple (no hint). When present it is a
`FormattedCDKey` over `pr_trade_text_tick_size_hint` with `{multiple}`
= tick_sz and `{number}` = the nearest valid price — the same CDKey +
params the sibling `increase_positions` `InvalidPriceTick` resolves to.

fields.name: amount_tick_msg
fields.doc:
Amount-input lot-step / min-size hint. `None` when the amount is
empty/zero or already valid. Lot-step uses `pr_trade_text_tick_size_hint`
(`{multiple}` = lot_sz, `{number}` = nearest valid amount); min-size uses
`pr_trade_placeorder_inputfield_integer_of_10` (`{num}` = min amount,
`{ccy}` = unit). Lot-step is checked before min-size, mirroring the
sibling submit chain order.

fields.name: price_corrected_value
fields.doc:
Lot/tick-aligned corrected values for the price / amount inputs — the
`{number}` baked into `*_tick_msg`. `None` when no hint fires. Native
`getPriceTickSizeMsg`/`getAmtTickSizeMsg` return `arrayOf(hint, corrected)`
so the input's `showCorrectValue()` snaps a misaligned input to the
nearest valid value; exposed separately because the value is otherwise
only embedded in the localized hint string (Kotlin cannot extract it),
which left the close button permanently blocked on misaligned input
(empty correct-value -> `showCorrectValue()` no-op -> error never clears).

fields.name: probably_value
fields.doc:
Estimated value pop (e.g. "≈ 50,000 USDT" / "≈ $2,190"). `None` when
inputs are empty/zero, the conversion is not meaningful, or the
instrument's probably-value convention is not ported (MARGIN/SPOT/EVENT).

OPTION ① (rust-migration-native-layer §A2.1): a `DisplayString` carrying
the UN-grouped value + prefix/suffix; Native applies the device-locale
thousands separator via `DisplayStringExt.resolve(ctx)`. Consistent with
the sibling `price_tick_msg` / `amount_tick_msg` fields above.

doc:
UI-ready inline-hint bundle for the close-position amount/price inputs.

Retires the three Kotlin local computations in
`RustClosePositionBottomSheet.kt`:
- `:251` `TradeInputUtils.getPriceTickSizeMsg(price, instTitle, instType)`
→ [`price_tick_msg`]
- `:302` `TradeInputUtils.getAmtTickSizeMsg(amt, instTitle, instType)`
→ [`amount_tick_msg`]
- `:312` `TradeInputUtils.getProbablyValue(price, amt, instTitle, instType,
indexPrice)` → [`probably_value`]

Produced by `ClosePositionManager::build_input_validation(price, amount)`
and projected into `OKTClosePositionState.input_validation`. The Kotlin
listeners read these fields directly instead of calling `TradeInputUtils`
/ `OKTNumberF` locally.

# Per-instType coverage (A6 sibling fan-out)
- `price_tick_msg` is produced for **every** instType that exposes a
`tick_sz` (SWAP/FUTURES/MARGIN/OPTION/EVENT) via the shared
`GetBestPriceUseCase` (the verified `getPriceTickSizeMsg` port already
used by `increase_positions`).
- `amount_tick_msg` reuses `GetBestAmtUseCase` (`new_contract` for
SWAP/FUTURES, `new_option` for OPTION, `new_spot_or_margin` for
MARGIN/SPOT) plus the contract `check_contract_min_size_by_inst`
(SWAP/FUTURES only — it returns `Ok` and contributes no hint for other
inst types, matching Kotlin which gates min-size on contract biz).
- `probably_value` is produced for SWAP/FUTURES (`calculate_amount_pop`)
and OPTION (`calculate_estimated_value_use_case`). **MARGIN / SPOT /
EVENT probably-value convention is NOT ported** — the native
`getProbablyValue` branches for those biz lines live in the binary-only
`TradeInputUtils` that is not source-readable in this worktree, so the
value stays `None` there rather than fabricating a formula. See the
`R-MIG-TODO` note in `build_input_validation`.

name: refresh_last_price
doc:
ISSUE #1 (2026-07-09) — sync `state.last_price` from the parent session's
InstContext `ticker.last` ON DEMAND. Replaces the removed per-tick ticker
mirror (which marked the whole form State dirty on every WS push → a full
panel re-render each tick with no UI field change). The build / confirm /
pre_check paths read `state.last_price` (the `manager.pre_check` last-price
arg, the market max-size USD cap, the `max_tp_sl` local-calc-price
fallback) but run on the shared state snapshot with no session handle, so
the value must live in State when they run. Called from user-driven actions
only (submit / confirm) + once on start / resume — NEVER per ticker push, so
it never re-creates the idle render burst. Mirror of
`PureSpotLimitInteractor::refresh_last_price` (`spot_limit_interactor.rs:3686`).
Only overwrites on a live value so a transient empty ticker read cannot
clobber a good price (`state.last_price` is `String` here, not spot-limit's
`Option<String>`); `modify_state` no-ops on an unchanged value.

The V1 `SpotStopSingleInteractor` had no production callers, but this state
Record is STILL the Kotlin renderer's data contract: the V2
`PureSpotStopSingleInteractor::legacy_state()` projection returns it and the

`mod.rs pub use types::*`.

The symbol-domain filter is active on one of the two NEW domains

Structural sibling of [`Self::CurrentPairModeEnabled`]: both say "a

name: ct_xperp_settle_entry
doc:
Derive the settle-entry state for the current pair (X-Perp + USDⓈ-M / UM
equivalence class).

`is_xperps` is the primary per-pair input — it comes from the caller's
instrument snapshot (`OKTContractInstrumentSnapshot.is_xperps`, itself
sourced from the Rust `is_x_perps_pair()` classification). The red dot and
USD settlement ccy are self-sourced from Rust (red-dot use case +
`trade_setting`). Non-X-Perp pairs return the inert default (plain "+", no
dot, no settlement row), so the caller can apply this unconditionally on
every instrument change without branching.

`is_icon_gray_hit` is the icon-only gray gate (2026 product decision:
`key_feature_available_icon` on Kotlin's `TradeAbTestManager`). When true,
[`XPerpSettleEntryVo::icon_uses_gear`] is forced false so the caller
renders the default plus icon — but `show_settle_gear` stays true for
X-Perp pairs, preserving red-dot / settlement-currency / delegate wiring.
Gray SDK is a native input (no Rust producer for AB values), so the flag
is passed in rather than read here — mirrors the `is_lite` / `is_cr_market`
native-input convention elsewhere in this crate.
`is_xperps` / `is_usd_um` come from the caller's instrument snapshot
(`OKTContractInstrumentSnapshot`). Both branches share the gear icon + red
dot + settlement-ccy row because they consume the same USDⓈ-M settle ccy
source (`get_usd_settle_ccy`); the red-dot use case (SP key) is shared, so
a user who dismisses the dot on one branch will not see it re-appear on the
other. Pairs outside the class return the inert default (plain "+", no dot,
no settlement row), so the caller can invoke this unconditionally on every
instrument change without branching.

doc:
View object for the reverse position confirmation page

Contains all formatted data ready for UI display.
Maps 1:1 to the page UI sections.

# Page Layout

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [TopBar] Reverse Position                     [X]         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [TopInfo]                                                 |
|   "BTC-USDT Perp"  [Isolated]  [Short to Long]           |  <- inst_name, margin_mode, reverse_direction
|   Latest Price: 65,230.5                                  |  <- (native ticker, NOT in VO)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [Origin Position]                                         |
|   | Market Buy                                            |  <- origin_entrust_state
|   | [Buy 20x]                                             |  <- origin_side, origin_lever
|   | Close amount        100 Cont                          |  <- origin_close_size (from API)
|   | Order price         Market                            |  <- (static)
+-------------- [Short to Long] ----------------------------+  <- middle_direction_text
| [After Reverse]                                           |
|   | Market Sell                                           |  <- reverse_entrust_state
|   | [Sell]                                                |  <- reverse_side
|   | Est. open amount    100 Cont                          |  <- reverse_open_size (from API)
|   | Order price         Market                            |  <- (static)
|   | Est. liq price      45,000 USDT (2.00%)              |  <- reverse_liq_price + reverse_price_gap
|   | Leverage            10x                               |  <- reverse_leverage (from API)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [Tip Note]                                                |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [ ] Do not show again                                     |
| [Confirm Reverse]                                         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

# iOS Reference

- `OKTPReverseCheckTopInfoVC` -> top info section
- `OKTPReverseOriginPositionInfoVC` -> origin position section
- `OKTPRPartingLineShowView` -> middle direction arrow
- `OKTPRAfterReverseInfoVC` -> after reverse section

# Usage

```ignore
let vo = manager.pre_check(&position).await?;

// Top info
instNameLabel.text = vo.inst_name
marginModeTag.text = native_localize(vo.margin_mode)  // "isolated" -> "Isolated"
reverseDirectionTag.text = native_direction_label(vo)  // uses pos_side + inst_type

// Origin position (formatted values)
closeSizeLabel.text = vo.origin_close_size.toString()

// After reverse (formatted values from API)
openSizeLabel.text = vo.reverse_open_size.toString()
liqPriceLabel.text = vo.reverse_liq_price.toString()

// Dialog decisions
if vo.is_leverage_changed { showLeverageMismatchDialog(...) }
if !vo.is_full_reverse { showPartialReverseDialog(...) }
```

[`CTMarginModeSyncState`]: that one tracks the margin-mode *submit* operation and
already gates the confirm button, so reusing it for list loading would conflate two
unrelated conditions in one field (spec: one condition, one channel).

`init` publishes `Loading` synchronously and returns immediately; the
`MarginModeEffect::LoadInstruments` effect publishes `Loaded` together with the rows.

Idle = pre-init frame) so the host can draw its first frame without waiting for the
full instrument scan.

name: set_attach_inst_id
doc:
GAP A root fix (2026-07-31): re-feed the LIVE `inst_id` into `ctx` after the
instrument settles. The attach binder is created early (fragment
onViewCreated) when the snapshot instId is not yet ready, so `init.inst_id`
(and thus `ctx.inst_id`) is empty; `set_contract_facevalue` re-feeds
ctVal/isInverse but NOT inst_id. With `ctx.inst_id` empty, `resolve_inst_family`
fails and profit_dig / price_digit / `to_base_for_order` all fall back
(inverse dual-pnl "--" + wrong precision). Kotlin calls this from
`PureTPSLViewBinder` alongside `set_contract_facevalue` with the live
`cachedInstId`, so once the instrument settles the dual-pnl compute resolves
the real per-family profit precision, tick precision, and inverse convertor.
Empty input is ignored (never clobber a good id with a bootstrap-race empty).
Additive FFI — iOS need not call it (no signature change).

name: on_visible

name: query_settle_collateral_relation
doc:
Query the enable-relation state for `ccy` before silently enabling it as
collateral (settle-ccy auto-enable, Rust cohort). Fetches the current
collateral assets and reports whether the caller must prompt the user to
also enable relation partners.

The `needs_prompt` rule mirrors the open-collateral interactor's
`enable_relation_prompt` (V1 `handleRelatedCoin(ccy, isOpened = true)`)
exactly: the base coin must have enable-relation partners AND at least one
of them must currently NOT be collateral-enabled. A partner that is missing
from the fetched assets list does NOT count toward the prompt
(`unwrap_or(false)`), matching the interactor's rule.

No submit / no state mutation — pure query. On success returns
`SettleCollateralRelationVo { needs_prompt, relation_ccys }`; the caller
decides which coins to pass to `enable_collateral_coins`.
