name: sl_liq_warning_key_at_confirm
doc:
Stage-2 of the SL-vs-liquidation warning: the ORDER-CONFIRM sheet's place-order
button. Empty string = no warning.

Native `OkTradePresenter.tradeOrderConfirm`:883-893 runs a SECOND check when the
confirm sheet's button is tapped, and deliberately uses a DIFFERENT, fresher
liquidation source than the panel stage: `checkData.liqPx`, i.e. the pre-check
response's estimate rather than the panel's max-available pair. That is why the panel
stage alone is not equivalent -- when the max-available snapshot carries no liq price
(native explicitly passes "" while the balance request is in flight,
`AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter`:2691-2696), native still catches the crossing here.

Suppression mirrors native's `group.optional.disableSlLiqTip`: that flag is set
exactly when the panel stage SHOWED its dialog and the user confirmed, and it makes
stage 2 skip so the user never sees two dialogs for one order. The frozen
`attached_tpsl_sl_liq_warning_key` on this attempt is the equivalent signal -- it is
non-empty if and only if the panel stage warned (and had the user chosen the
change-price button instead of place-order, no confirm sheet would exist to reach
this method).

Gated on the bare `get_liq_px_confirm()` like native, NOT on the confirm sheet's
`liq_shown` row-visibility flag -- that one additionally requires single/cross and
non-close, an intentional V2-only narrowing of the row projection which must not leak
into this gate. No dynamic-ratio fallback: native's stage 2 reads only the static
`attachSp.firstOrNull { it.slTriggerPx.gt(0) }`.

name: pure_fetch_deposit_prefill
doc:
Kernel deposit-prefill (PREFER path): self-source the decision flags from
Rust producers, fetch the asset valuation via Rust, and produce a complete
[`PureDepositPrefill`].

**Rust-self-source contract (no Kotlin round-trip)**: 5 of the 6 V1 decision
flags + `currency_id` are derived inside [`resolve_deposit_decision_flags`]
straight from OKCore producers (feature-restriction / account-manager /
settings currency-list / coin-wrapper). Native does NOT precompute any of
those with a legacy API and hand it back (that is the fake round-trip the
phase-4 audit gate bans).

The exported "+" launcher keeps `is_cr_market` as an input for wire
compatibility with its existing caller. Normal-order error recovery does
not use that input: [`build_order_error_deposit_prefill`] reads the Rust
app-mode provider directly before projecting the navigation payload.

The valuation fetch mirrors V1 `FundTransferBtnDelegate.requestAPI()` →
`FundTransInTradingPageUseCase(currencyId)` (POST
`/v2/asset/accounts/user-currency-list-balance`), already ported as
`QueryUserBalanceUseCase`. On API error / empty / `currency_id == 0` the
valuation is `None`, matching V1's error path (which routes through
`goToDepositPageDefault` — equivalent to the priority-5 fallback arm of the
option tree, where `asset_amount = None`).

`cancel_token` follows the standard async-export convention (see
`ct_fetch_entity_upgrade_state`).

gate so an originally-present leg whose trigger price the user then CLEARS is still
validated -> strict `check_required` emits `TriggerPriceRequired`
(trigger-price-is-required) instead of being silently skipped as absent.

Additive surface: presence-only flags, no render/notify (validation-only
state). Default `false` — hosts that never call this are unaffected. The
modify host re-asserts it on every editor setup, so it tracks the current
order being amended.

doc:
#2a (device recvqck62xDPO0) contract attached-TPSL direction-validity gate,
invoked by the 6 contract make-order fragments BEFORE the confirm sheet.
V1 mirror `OkTradeFuturePresent.checkSimpleTpSl` + `AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter
.checkSimpleTpSl`: for the OPEN direction, warn when the attached TP/SL trigger
price sits on the wrong side of the order price (open-long / BUY: TP < order,
SL > order; open-short / SELL: reversed) => "TP/SL setting may not take effect".

Reuses the direction-aware pure `PreOrderTpSlValidationUseCase`, which emits
native `pr_trade_futures_*` keys. This is a DISTINCT concern from
`validate_oco_tpsl` (which does the order-px-vs-trigger-px "may not fill
immediately" Check B). The orchestration performs the advanced direction check,
then uses the pure use case for price-only validation, including a Trailing
config's optional static SL. `order_px` = native
`simpleTpSlCheckPrice` (the order price; a market order passes its last price).
SL uses the trigger price only (native reads `slTriggerPx`), so no SL order-px /
limit-flag param is needed.
Pure query (spec section C), no side effect; `message_key == ""` => valid.

R-MIG-370 DEEP #1: also projects the resolved-token string into the
typed `state.td_mode` (`OKTSpotTdMode`) consumed by `derive_can_borrow`
Path-1 (`td_mode == Cross`), then re-runs the native can_borrow derive.

Copy-trade fix (device 2026-07-15): the Kotlin host resolves the non-multi
-attr value via `OrderLeadUtils.getSpotMgn` → `getOrderLeaderSwitchStatusList()`,
but that Kotlin `TradeConfig` switch-status list is NOT populated in Pure V2
— the close-switch SSOT moved to the Rust `inst_config_info` cache (written
by `ct_container_manager::set_lead_switch` / `trade_facade`). With an empty
Kotlin list `!contains(instId)` is always true, so `getSpotMgn` returned
`spot_isolated` for EVERY spot-lead stop order regardless of the close-follow
switch (single + double, buy + sell). Re-derive `getSpotMgn` here from the
populated Rust SSOT — native contract `OrderLeadUtils.kt:60-62`:
`isOrderLeaderSpotPosition(instId) && orderLeaderSwitchOpen(instId)` where
`orderLeaderSwitchOpen = isOrderLeaderSpotPosition && !close_switch_list
.contains(instId)` (R7: `close_switch_list` holds lead-CLOSED instIds, so
lead-on = NOT in the list). The multi-attr (MCC/PM) branch keeps the
Kotlin-pushed margin mode (cross/isolated), which this bug does not affect.
CTRSTrade globals are read OUTSIDE `modify_state` (ct_container_manager §A).

name: on_hidden
doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase). OCO twin
of the stop-single `on_hidden`.

The Pure host swaps spot order-type panels via show/hide keep-alive, so a
hidden panel gets no Activity pause. Native re-inflates a fresh Fragment
per order-type and on the single vs double variant switch, showing a blank
draft each time. The typed draft lives in Rust state and survives
hide/show, so mirror native by clearing the input draft (BOTH OCO legs) on
this hide transition ONLY.

Kotlin routing: `PureSpotStopDoubleFragment.onHiddenChanged(hidden=true)`
calls this ONLY when the hide is an in-container order-type / variant
switch (`!isHiddenByAncestor()`); a Home / Trade tab switch hides the
shell too, so it is NOT called and the draft is PRESERVED. Sibling parity
with `PureSpotLimitInteractor::on_hidden`.

Field set mirrors the canonical draft clear the panel already uses on a
side switch / pair switch / logout edge (`apply_side_state_mutation` +
`reset_for_logout`): single trigger/order price, both OCO legs, amount,
seekbar.

fields.doc:

Deliberately kept SEPARATE from the shared `PureTpslMode` enum (Oco / Oro)
so the spot shell's exhaustive `match cfg.mode` in
`spot/limit/pure/orchestration/tpsl.rs` stays untouched — the R2 MULTI
divergence is contract-local and never widens the shared enum.

fields.doc:
Contract-local advance mode flag for the Trailing tab. `false` = not
trailing (default), `true` = Trailing tab selected. Mirror of
`is_multi_mode`; deliberately kept SEPARATE from the shared `PureTpslMode`
enum so the spot shell's exhaustive `match cfg.mode` stays untouched (the
R3 Trailing divergence is contract-local, like the R2 MULTI one). The
trailing form's own inputs / validation live in the dedicated
`TpslTrailingStopAttachInteractor` (the Kotlin VM holds it); this flag
only drives the tab-content switch + confirm routing on the host side.

fields.name: is_trailing_tab_visible
fields.doc:
PM-gate for the Trailing tab (#84 T1-Rust). `true` = the Trailing tab
is shown; `false` = hidden (PM / portfolio-margin accounts do not
support trailing stop). Rust owns this business decision (A1 / H-4): the Kotlin
pure sheet reads it to add/remove the Trailing tab + its divider / info
icon, instead of calling `TradeCoreProxy...isAssemblyAccount()` (B1).

V1-REF: `TpslAdvanceContractConfirmFragment.initTpslModeTab` — the tab is
added only `if (!isPmAccount)`, where `isPmAccount =
getTradeDataSettings().isAssemblyAccount()`. V1 `isAssemblyAccount()` is
`getAccountLevel().eq(ACCOUNT_LEVEL_4)` (PM only), which maps EXACTLY to
the Rust `AccountConfigGetter::is_pm_account()` (`== ACCOUNT_LEVEL_4`) —
NOT `is_mcc_or_pm_account()`. Hence `is_trailing_tab_visible =
!is_pm_account()`. Derived in `project_session_data_into_state` (the
account-sourced projection point, mirroring `amount_symbol`).

fields.name: host_hides_multi_mode
fields.doc:
`true` = this order type HIDES the OCO<->MULTI mode switch (MULTI not
offered). Inverted sense so `#[derive(Default)]` = full-featured (limit /
market / advanced_limit keep MULTI). Set in set_header_seed via
`host_capabilities::apply_host_capabilities`.
V1-REF: trigger / segment hosts never expose the MULTI mode.

fields.name: tp_strategy_kind
fields.doc:
Per-leg TP strategy kind — which input mode the user selected:
BY_PRICE / BY_PNL_RATE (pnl-rate) / BY_PNL (pnl-amount) /
BY_DYNAMIC_PRICE.
V1-REF: `PositionUtil.showIncomeSelectDialog` exposes exactly these
(the dynamic option only when `supportDynamic`). Reuses the spot
`PureAttachedTpslStrategyKind` `uniffi::Enum` (no new FFI enum; §G
binary). `None` = not yet selected → the Kotlin pure sheet renders the
default ByPrice box. Rust owns the per-leg mode selection (H-4 business
decision) so the pure sheet stops deriving it via the B1 selector dialog
(the T3-Kotlin round reads this field instead).

`Option` (not a bare enum) so the struct keeps `#[derive(Default)]`
(the spot enum is byte-frozen and has no `Default` derive).

fields.name: tp_profit

TP ByProfit (pnl-amount) raw input — V1 `BY_PNL` amount the user typed.
Stored raw (mirror `tp_change_pct`). The reverse-compute (profit/rate →
trigger px + PnL) is owned by Rust as of Block 2 (see the projection fields
below): the stateless `attach_facade` (ByRate / ByProfit = V1
`ByRateSpPresent` / `ByProfitSpPresent`, same `FuturesCalculator`
formula) computes it from this raw input + session-sourced contract
metadata, so the shell no longer borrows the V1 composite
`TpslAttachInteractor` engine for these two strategy kinds. (The
`PosMarginByPrice` / `ByDynamicPrice` strategy kinds still defer to the
composite — they are NOT in Block 2 scope.)

# Device bug #5 — full V1 history tab parity (additive)
V1 `HISTORY_COMMON_ORDER_STRATEGY_TABLE` (`OrderValues.kt`, MP-supported
account) exposes 7 tabs: ALL / Limit|Market / Advanced Limit / TP/SL /

row can show all 7 V1 tabs. Adding enum variants is an additive,

`onAvailableTransferTap` callback based on an inaccurate comment that
V1 unified them. Audit Round 17 simple_account_icon_click_audit_2026-

plus icon would only ever open the chevron's dialog, not the deposit
flow). Splitting at the UxEvent layer lets Kotlin route the plus tap
through `FundTransferBtnDelegate.requestToShowDepositPage` while the
chevron stays on the existing [`ShowAvailableSettingDialog`] arm.

— V1 `OrderShowUtils.getSpotTransferSymbol(SPOT, instId, BUY/SELL,
tradeQuoteCcy)` parity (BUY → user-selected `trade_quote_ccy` falling
back to `instrument.quote_ccy`; SELL → `instrument.base_ccy`). Kotlin
wraps it in `CurrencyModel(currency = ccy)` and forwards to

variants.name: ShowTpslDirectionWarning
variants.doc:
TP/SL direction confirm dialog. Emitted by `submit_order` when the attached
TP/SL trigger sits on the wrong side of the entry (order) price; Kotlin shows an
OKDialog (continue / cancel).

**"Continue" KEEPS the attached TP/SL** — it only unlocks the gate and resumes the
BBO / pre-check / place pipeline with the frozen TP/SL payload intact
(`proceed_after_tpsl_direction_check_attempt`). This is a V2-only affordance on the
SPOT side and a deliberate divergence from the contract checker, which DOES drop
TP/SL on continue (`SwapAdvancedFragment.kt:854` / `SwapTriggerFragment.kt:571`
`group.sp = null; group.attachSp = null`, gated by
`OkTradeFuturePresent.checkSimpleTpSl`). Android Native has NO spot counterpart to
this dialog at all: `checkSimpleTpSl` / `checkAdvancedTpSl` are declared only on the
FUTURE presenter and every consumer is a contract fragment. The host states the same
contract in `SpotLimitDialogs.kt` ("Continue proceeds WITHOUT clearing TP/SL — spot
divergence from the contract checker").

The ONLY spot path that discards attached TP/SL is the server-price correction of the
51006 / 51137 / 51138 family (Native `OkTradePresenter.kt:1020` /
`OrderResultHandler.kt:233` `group.attachSp = null` after the user accepts the
suggested limit price) — see `pending_price_retry_discards_tpsl`, which is a
different trigger and a different lifecycle from this dialog. Do not conflate them.

(This doc previously claimed the continue path omits TP/SL from the submit snapshot,
which contradicted both the implementation and the host comment.)

`message` is the CDKey warning, resolved by
Kotlin via `DisplayString.resolve(ctx)`.

variants.doc:
Bug HH (2026-05-21) — limit-price-clipped dialog.

V1 reference (`RustSpotLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:2048-2085` /
`OkTradePresenter.kt:1218-1219` /
`PreCheckResultHandler.kt:228-266`): when the BE returns a
"limit-price modify" error code (`LimitModifyError` aka the BE typo
`LIMIT_MIDIFY_ERROR`, `SpotMarginLimitPriceBuy`,
`SpotMarginLimitPriceSell`) the payload carries a server-suggested
`_data` price (the clipped allowed limit). V1 surfaces a confirmation
dialog asking the user to accept submission at the clipped price:
- BUY  -> `pr_options_placeorder_limit_modify_price` ("Your order
price triggered the limit. Confirm submitting at the maximum
allowed buy price {price}?")
- SELL -> `pr_trade_modal_order_sell_limit_modify_price` ("Your
order price triggered the limit. Confirm submitting at the
minimum allowed sell price {price}?")

Before this variant existed, the Rust make-order pipeline routed the
BE `LIMIT_MIDIFY_ERROR` family through `RouteCategory::ModifyOrderDialog`
→ `ShowOrderFailed` → Kotlin `SpotLimitDialogs.routeOrderFailed` Stage-1
toast (real-device-confirmed loop: user accepts local BBO → preCheck
passes → confirm dialog → submit → BE returns clipped error → no
dialog → user re-taps → local BBO fires again).

Confirm in the dialog routes through
[`PureSpotLimitActions::proceed_after_limit_price_clip`] which writes
`state.price = allowed_price` then re-runs `confirm_order` (skips the
local BBO + pre_check stages — those already passed; the clip is BE-side).
Cancel dismisses the dialog without any state mutation.

the same `TradeSessionContext` as this `MainTradeInteractor`.

R-ARCH-4 (b) — session-tree path mirror of the other session-sharing
pure factories. The returned FFI shim resolves
its instrument via `session.get_instrument()` (set by `MainPageManager`
before this call), so the Kotlin host no longer constructs an
`OKTSpotInstrumentSnapshot` from the legacy
`com.okinc.unify_trade.biz.SpotInstrument` and pushes it via
`set_instrument(...)`. Instead, Kotlin calls
`refreshInstrumentFromSession()` (or relies on the eager hydrate in
[`PureSpotMpFfi::create_with_session`]) to keep state in sync.

`PureSpotMpFfi` is intentionally a `Mutex<>`-wrapped shim, not a true
`#[interactor::interactor]` Interactor (see the architecture caveat at
the top of `pure_spot_mp_ffi.rs`). This factory is the minimum
session-tree wiring while the spot-mp full Interactor refactor remains
deferred — exposing the parent session via `Weak<TradeSessionContext>`
without rewriting the underlying 1700+ LOC `PureSpotMpInteractor`.

name: ct_fetch_market_tickers
doc:
Fetch market tickers for an instrument type via priapi.

# Arguments
* `inst_type` - Instrument type, e.g. "SPOT" / "SWAP" / "FUTURES" / "OPTION"
* `inst_family` - Optional instrument family filter, e.g. "BTC-USD".
`None` (or blank) fetches every family of `inst_type`.
* `cancel_token` - Cancellation token so the caller can abort the request

# Returns
* `Ok(tickers)` - Ticker snapshot, may be empty when the API returns no rows
* `Err(FFITradingError)` - Network / parse failure, or `OperationCancelled`

# Kotlin Usage
```kotlin
import uniffi.core_trading.ctFetchMarketTickers
import uniffi.ok_future_utils.OkCancellationToken

val tickers = ctFetchMarketTickers(
instType = "SWAP",
instFamily = "BTC-USDT", // null fetches every family of instType
cancelToken = OkCancellationToken(),
)
```

`DisplayStringExt`); slice 1b ports `getBusinessTradeModeTitle` to build it

value (typing past max), which leaves `page_vo` byte-identical and would
otherwise be swallowed by `modify_state`'s old==new dedup, leaving the
EditText showing the raw over-limit text. Technical render-invalidation
version field (cf. `subscription_id` in `spec/interactor.md` §J.1), not
business state; native ignores it.

doc:
Observable state for the unified adjust-leverage page facade.

Field discipline (per `spec/interactor.md` §D):
- `scenario` is part of the contract — surfaced through `page_vo.scenario`
for native, kept as a separate state field so observers can react before
the first `page_vo` projection lands.
- `pending_submit` is the **business runtime state** for the high-leverage
confirmation flow. It lives in state (UniFFI `Option<Record>`) rather
than as a `Mutex<...>` struct field on the interactor.
- `long_input_cache` / `short_input_cache` cache the latest accepted user
input per section, so `Submit` can be dispatched without native re-sending
the values. These are session-scoped and live in state for visibility.
- `is_loading` / `is_submitting` follow the "every async action has a
visible `is_*_in_progress` boolean" rule (§I checklist).

V1 branches on whether `ccy` is the trade symbol (base) → base-ccy display
convertor, else (quote symbol / tradeQuoteCcy) → quote-amount convertor. In
every branch it renders `targetFormatter(abs(amt)).group().suffix()`, i.e.
truncate-to-digit → thousands group → append the ccy. This reuses
[`format_target`] for that leaf, selecting the quote digit when `ccy` is not
the base ccy (Group-1 `is_quote` semantics).

✅ abs magnitude ← V1 `amt.toSafeDouble().absoluteValue.toString()`
✅ digit ← base_dig when `ccy == base`, else quote_dig (V1 tradeSymbol vs
quoteSymbol/tradeQuoteCcy convertor split; tradeSymbol == base ccy)
✅ group + ccy suffix ← `.group().suffix()`

simplification as `convert_margin_ava` (module docs).

the caller renders its own `--` placeholder.

**assembled attach leg set**, in BASE/API space. Empty when no SL leg is attached.

Native mirror `AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter.getLiqPriceAndSlPrice`:2697 reads

`PureAttachedTpslBinder.buildContractAttachAlgoOrds`): MULTI first -- its params
are DISPLAY, so they go through the same `convert_multi_attach_params_to_base`
the submit path uses -- otherwise the OCO/Trailing v2 list, which

doc:
Clear ONLY the SL leg's user config back to init defaults, keeping the TP
leg + host-synced order context (entry / lever / position_size) intact.

Called from Kotlin `dispatchTpslConfig` when the advance sheet confirms
with the SL leg deleted (slLeg == null, TP retained). The former path
(`update_trigger_input(sl = "")`) is a NO-OP for a ByRate / ByProfit SL —
its empty-trigger clear only honors a ByPrice leg — so the retained
`sl_rate_raw` / `sl_strategy_kind` kept `sl_flag_active` true (the flag
falls back to the raw values) and `compute()` re-derived a ghost SL
trigger every tick that leaked into the panel echo, confirm sheet, submit,
AND reopen (device 2026-07-31). This resets EVERY SL field regardless of
strategy kind, so the delete is authoritative. `advance_oco_confirmed` is
left untouched: with the TP leg retained the config is still an
advance-confirmed (single-leg) echo — a full two-leg clear routes through
[`Self::clear_all_tpsl`] instead.

OCO twin of the Single sibling setter. SS-F-007/F-008 fresh-eye

Kotlin `getSpotMgn` reads `getOrderLeaderSwitchStatusList()`, but that
Kotlin `TradeConfig` list is NOT populated in Pure V2 (close-switch SSOT
moved to the Rust `inst_config_info` cache), so `!contains` was always true
and every spot-lead OCO stop order sent `spot_isolated` regardless of the

(`isOrderLeaderSpotPosition && !close_switch_list.contains`, R7); keep the
Kotlin margin mode on the multi-attr branch. Globals read OUTSIDE
`modify_state` (ct_container_manager §A). See Single sibling for the full
rationale.

hand-rolled `uniffi::Object` (not a framework interactor with a state
observer), so `release()` only needs to `stop()` and drop the UI-event
observer `Arc` that otherwise pins the Kotlin host via the foreign
callback handle map. There is no state observer to remove here, and the
foundation-generated release does not apply to this hand-rolled object.

doc:
Instrument scope the OPENING surface hands to the sheet.

The row list branches on the CURRENT instrument's `inst_type`
(`orchestration::list_assembly` — SPOT/MARGIN show the quote-ccy balance,
SWAP/FUTURES only when positive, OPTION never; and at L3/L4 SPOT/MARGIN take the
spot list while everything else takes the future list). Without a scope that
`inst_type` comes from the persisted "last biz"
(`TradeBizCache::load_last_biz`), whose only writer is the trade page's
instrument load (`main_page_manager::persist_current_instrument`). The OPTION
line never writes it — `ensure_option_shell_ready` just loads the OPTION biz
metadata — so the sheet opened from an option surface branched on whatever
spot/contract pair the user visited last (device: an option page showing the
SPOT list, complete with a "USDT balance" row native explicitly excludes for
options).

Fixing that by writing OPTION into the global cache was rejected: that key is
also read by the trade-record default pair filter
(`aggregate_records_manager`), the cold-start biz restore
(`main_page_manager::cached_instrument_request`) and the order / history list
"current pair" gates — none of which are in scope here.

Native has the same concept for "open this sheet for a specific instrument":
`BizInfoConfig.CustomArgsBizConfig(instType, instId)` ("memory only"), the
sibling of the `DefaultBizConfig` cache read the sheet uses today.

All three fields are plain identity forwarded by the host. Resolution order is
`inst_id` → `inst_family` → type-only.

name: refresh_last_price
doc:
ISSUE #1 (2026-07-09) — sync `state.last_price` from the parent session's
InstContext `ticker.last` ON DEMAND. Replaces the removed per-tick ticker
mirror (which marked the whole form State dirty on every WS push → a full

pre_check paths read `state.last_price` (TP-vs-SL leg classification, the
`manager.pre_check` last-price arg, the market max-size USD cap) but run on
the shared state snapshot with no session handle, so the value must live in
State when they run. Called from user-driven actions only (submit / confirm)
+ once on start / resume — NEVER per ticker push, so it never re-creates the
idle render burst. Mirror of `PureSpotLimitInteractor::refresh_last_price`
(`spot_limit_interactor.rs:3686`). Only overwrites on a live value so a
transient empty ticker read cannot clobber a good price (`state.last_price`
is `String` here, not spot-limit's `Option<String>`); `modify_state` no-ops
on an unchanged value.

`tick_sz` fractional count (PRICE precision) and the host also feeds it to
`activePriceInput.setMaxDecimal` (`PureMarginMpFragment.kt:1403`), which is correct
and must not move. `0` = not resolved yet (cold index config), and the host then
keeps using `quote_decimal_digits` exactly as before.

clears `seekbar_percent`) does not loop. R9 surfaces an explicit
boolean so the `clear_select_percent` action body can early-out
when already cleared in this UI tick. Reset by Kotlin (or by
`confirm_order`) once the user touches a non-percent input.

`on_percent_selected` derives a new amount and pushes it to the input,
the Compose input re-emits that value one frame later. Without this
guard `on_amount_changed` unconditionally clears `seekbar_percent = 0`,
blanking the slider the user just dragged. Mirrors margin-limit's
`dirty_source == PercentSlider` guard (R-MIG-377).

fields.name: balance
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed balance snapshot. V1 reads this via
`mBalanceModel?.getTradeBalance()?.second` to compute the
percent-derived order size (F28 `getAmountCal` percent branch) and
the market-leg max size (F29 `getNewMarketMaxSize`). R13 ships
the kernel-side store + the `update_balance` action so Kotlin
pushes the snapshot once per refresh and reads back the typed
percent-derived size via `compute_amount_by_percent`.

`None` means Kotlin has not pushed a balance snapshot yet (V1
fall-back returns empty string in that case, matching
`getNewMarketMaxSize` and `getAmountCal` empty-string branches).

fields.name: balance_side
fields.doc:
The side ("BUY"/"SELL") the current `balance` snapshot was FETCHED for.
DEVICE-FIX (Buy↔Sell reversed / 0 avail, 2026-07-01) — OCO twin of the
single-leg fix. The SPOT max-available `available` is side-dependent
(BUY → quote-ccy avail; SELL → base-ccy avail — `spot_types.rs:443-445`).
After a side flip the ROOT #2-retained snapshot belongs to the PRIOR
side; deriving/rendering it against the NEW `side` shows the other side's
value under the wrong ccy label (reversed) or a stale/0 figure. The avail
projection + seekbar percent-calc gate their `Loaded` output on
`balance_side == side`; a mismatch renders `--` (Loading) until the
side-change re-fetch stamps the new side here. Empty until the first
fetch lands.

fields.name: balance_inst
fields.doc:
The instrument (`inst_id`) the current `balance` snapshot was FETCHED for.
DEVICE-FIX (coin-switch stale avail, 2026-07-06) — OCO twin of the
single-leg fix. A same-side coin switch keeps `balance_side == side` TRUE,
so the avail projection gate passed the PRIOR coin's snapshot as `Loaded`
→ the row kept showing the previous coin's value AND ccy unit. The
projection + seekbar/market-max gates now also require
`balance_inst == inst_id`; a mismatch renders `--` until the inst-change
re-fetch stamps the new instrument here. Every balance write site sets it.

fields.name: instrument_snapshot
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed instrument snapshot (V1 `BizInstrument` cache).
Populated by `update_instrument_snapshot(...)` after Kotlin reads
`TradeCoreProxy.getTrade().getSuggestedInstrument(SPOT, instId)`.
Sibling parity: `PureSpotAdvancedLimitState.instrument` (sibling
`spot/advanced_limit/pure/state.rs`).

Drives the `state()` projection so the legacy
`OKTSpotInstrumentSnapshot` shape the Kotlin renderer reads
(baseCcy / quoteCcy / tickSz / lotSz / minSz / quoteCcyDigit)
reflects the live instrument. Without this slot every render
observed `instrument = default` and the panel rendered all
base/quote/amount fields empty (forensic B1 root cause).

`PureOKTSpotInstrumentSnapshot` is a `uniffi::Record`, so the
macro-added `uniffi::Record` derive on this state accepts the slot
directly (no serde skip needed now that serde is dropped — sibling
parity: `PureSpotStopSingleState.instrument_snapshot`).

doc:
V2 state for SpotStopDouble (OCO — dual TP/SL legs).

Field set partitioned into 8 groups (R3 → R8):
1. Identity & side (5)
2. Common inputs (5)
3. TP/SL specific inputs (dual leg) (8)
4. Display / max / decimals (7)
5. Misc account & feature flags (12)
6. UI / interaction transient (3)
7. R5 — symbol_type / order_confirm_enabled (2)
8. R8 — last_bbo_price (1)

Total: 43 fields. Sibling spot/limit `PureSpotLimitState` carries ~100;
the remaining ~60 (TPSL nested config, max-avail multi-mode, lead-context,
borrow chain, region/flavor) land in R4+ as actions wire them.

doc:

upgrade action" lives here, in `mapper::normalize_leverage_stops`.

(`SPOT` / `MARGIN` / `SWAP` / `FUTURES` / `OPTION` / `EVENTS`); `Unknown`
covers any unrecognized value so Native always has a defined fall-through.

instId: "BTC-UPDOWN-15MIN-260328-1000-1015"
→ method: "PRICE_UP_DOWN", start_ms: 1774839600000, end_ms: 1774840500000

instId: "BTC-ABOVE-DAILY-260327-1600-58000"
→ method: "PRICE_ABOVE", start_ms: 1774792800000, end_ms: 1774792800000

name: TradFiNavL1PlatformProvider
doc:
Native-injected tradFi L1 navigation preference (read + write).

Both directions live on ONE trait, mirroring `trade_mode_callback`: it is a
single native capability, the calls are synchronous and lightweight (NR-7), and
a foreign trait is trivially mockable in this crate's unit tests, whereas
asserting an emitted event round-trip would be indirect and would add ordering
risk for no benefit.

The implementation is pure transport to `MarketCoreService`. It must contain no
business judgment of its own (NR-8 / R-MIG-529): it does not decide when to
read, what the value means, whether it applies, or what a miss should become.

NOTE (cross-platform): the arity of these two methods is fixed by OKMarket's
published signatures, so changing it requires every foreign implementer to
change with it — Android `OKTTradFiNavL1Provider` does; the iOS Swift impl must
follow on its next OKCore sync.

doc:
R5 — composite-seed projection for the V1 `StopProfitBean` the Kotlin
Fragment hands to `UniSetTpSlView.refreshTpslView(...)`.

# Why this lives Rust-side
The V1 path builds `StopProfitBean` directly in
`TpslAdvanceMarginConfirmFragment.generateNormalStopProfitBean()` from
`OrderConfirmData` (L706-726) — a `unify_trade.biz.OrderConfirmData`
dependency which `pure/` Kotlin paths cannot import per R-MIG-021. V2
canonical pattern: every field the bean needs is owned by this Rust
state, projected through `state()` as a structured uniffi::Record, and
read by the pure Fragment to construct the bean from a single
snapshot reference (no field-by-field Bundle plumbing on the Kotlin
side, no `unify_trade.*` import).

# Field semantics
Mirrors V1 [`StopProfitBean`] field names verbatim so the Kotlin
translation is mechanical. `is_market_or_bbo` is derived from
`open_px.is_empty()` (V1 parity: empty `openPx` always means
market-or-BBO entry in the limit panel).

# Critical for input-enable
`open_px` MUST be non-empty for the composite's trigger ↔ percent
cross-input math to fire (R2.5 SEV-1 root cause when this field was
empty — V1 `UniSetTpSlView.refreshInputView()` short-circuits the
input enable + cross-input listener installation otherwise). The host
adapter must pass `state.price` from the parent panel; if the user
opens the sheet before typing a price, the composite falls back to the
live ticker subscription installed by `refreshTpslView` (V1 parity:
`ByPriceSpPresent.getChosePrice` falls back to `mView.getSelectMarketPx`
when `mBaseData.openPx.isEmpty() && from == FROM_ORDER`).

class); `server_only` skips the trailing local re-write so it cannot

fields.name: price
fields.doc:
Raw converted price string (Decimal.to_string(), no locale formatting).
Bid prices and ask prices are NOT rounded here — native applies rounding

Cumulative amount up to and including this price level.

Computed as: this level's sum_amount / max sum_amount across all levels on this side.

fields.name: ladder_digits
fields.doc:
Price precision (number of decimal places from ladder.digitFormat()).
Negative values mean whole-number grouping (e.g., -1 = round to nearest 10).
Native uses this for price rounding and display formatting.

fields.name: amount_digit
fields.doc:
Amount precision (number of decimal places for display).
Determined by inst_type, trade_unit, and contract type.
Native uses this for amount formatting with OKTNumberF.

fields.name: is_bid
fields.doc:
Whether this is a bid (buy) side entry.
Controls rounding direction: bid = DOWN, ask = UP.
Native uses this when applying price rounding via OKTNumberF.

doc:
A single formatted depth item ready for UI display.

Maps to Kotlin `TradeDepthItem` fields:
- price       -> raw converted price (Decimal.to_string(), NOT locale-formatted)
- amount      -> raw converted amount (Decimal.to_string(), NOT locale-formatted)
- originPrice -> numeric origin price (before unit conversion, for click-fill)
- unFormatPrice -> unformatted price (after conversion, before locale formatting)
- originAmount -> numeric origin amount (raw contract/coin count)
- sumAmount   -> cumulative amount up to this price level (for bar ratio)
- ratio       -> cumulative fill ratio (0.0 - 1.0) for the depth bar

**Formatting strategy**: Rust passes raw numeric values + precision metadata.
Native (Kotlin/Swift) uses OKTNumberF (with ICU locale) for final formatting
(locale separators, K/M/B/T suffixes, trailing zeros, rounding direction).

variants.name: StrategyTypeChange
variants.doc:
Audit-5.3b (2026-05-20) · field-decision #12.

V1 parity event for the in-panel "Market select" / "Limit select"
strategy switch (V1 `AbsSpotTradePanelPresenter.kt:196`
`strategyTypeLd: NonStickyLiveData<StrategyTypeConfig>` —
`setMarketSelect(false) + setMarketSelectListener` at L404-410). Producer
sites include V1 `MarginLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:662` /
`RustMarginLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:1020` (`postValue(MARKET)`) and
the mirrored Market→Limit transition at
`MarginMarketTradePanelPresenter.kt:481` (`postValue(LIMIT)`).
Consumer: `QuickOrderMarginTradePanelFragment.kt:223` swaps the hosted
panel Fragment based on the new strategy.

V2 pattern (R-MIG-40 H2): a top-level `MainTradeUiEvent` variant lets
any biz-specific interactor (spot_limit / margin_limit / future_limit)
broadcast a strategy-switch signal, and any host Fragment (today
`QuickOrderMarginTradePanelFragment`, tomorrow the pure-path host)
observes via `subscribe_main_trade_ui_events()`. Replaces the LiveData
channel without coupling to a presenter base class.

`target_strategy` carries the V1 `StrategyType` enum **name** (e.g.
"LIMIT" / "MARKET" / "TRIGGER" / "MP") rather than a Rust enum so the
event lives in this top-level module without depending on each
biz-specific `PureStrategyType` definition. Kotlin host fragments
`valueOf(target_strategy)` on the consumer side.

name: on_price_focus_changed
doc:
Clean price-focus entry (2026-06-13): updates ONLY the price-input focus
bit and recomputes the price-currency bubble. Unlike the 2-in-1
`update_price_bubble(quote_ticker_last, has_focus)`, it does NOT touch
`state.quote_ticker_last` (the kernel self-fed market price), so callers
that only have the focus signal (iOS / HarmonyOS) no longer have to echo
the current ticker back to avoid clobbering it. Sibling parity:
`spot/advanced_limit/pure/spot_advanced_limit_interactor.rs`
`on_price_focus_changed`.

name: resolve_initial_option_margin_type
doc:
Resolve the initial option marginType on the option main page entry.

Bridges Kotlin `OptionMainSharedModel.resolveInitial()`. Reads
`enable_linear_options()` from the Trade singleton, then delegates to
`OptionDefaultsResolver::resolve_initial_margin_type_impl`.

# Arguments
* `sp_manually_set` — `KEY_OPTION_MARGIN_TYPE_MANUALLY_SET` SP value
* `sp_default` — `KEY_OPTION_DEFAULT_MARGIN_TYPE` SP value (None when unset)
* `ab_default_usds` — `TradeAbTestManager.isDefaultUsdsOption()` AB result

# Returns
Either `"CM"` or `"UM"` (the latter only when linear options gate is open).

option chain. Combines the two conditions the V1/`Rust*` Kotlin evaluated via
OKTradeCore (`TradeCommonUtils.isEnableLinearOptions()` +

`OkTradeFuturePresent.checkOrderExceedBbo` continue). Set by

when the session's InstrumentChanged event fires (R-MIG-407).

fields.name: input_price
fields.doc:
Price input box current text (single source of truth under Rust subclass path).
Empty string means no input. No formatting applied.

fields.name: price_fiat_iso
fields.doc:
Fiat iso-code (`USD` / `CNY` / ...) that `input_price` is currently denominated
in, for coin-margined (inverse) contracts whose price box is shown in the user's
legal currency. Used to detect a legal-currency SWITCH (vs live rate drift) so a
depth legal-currency change re-converts the non-empty price to the new fiat instead of
leaving a stale value. Empty until the first projection/seed. Internal (not
rendered by Kotlin). Writers: `project_session_instrument_into_state` + `set_input_price`.

fields.name: price_fiat_rate
fields.doc:
USD->fiat exchange rate at which `input_price` is denominated (paired with
`price_fiat_iso`). Needed to recover the USD base on a fiat switch because
`get_exchange_rate()` only exposes the CURRENT fiat's rate. Empty until first set.
Internal (not rendered). Writers: same as `price_fiat_iso`.

fields.name: input_amount
fields.doc:
Current amount input content (UI text). SSOT for the amount input field
in Rust-backed subclasses. Written via `set_input_amount` from the
`onAmountInputChanged` hook in the Kotlin subclass. Empty string == no input.

fields.name: seekbar_percent
fields.doc:
Current seekbar percent as string (e.g. "0.5", "1.0", "" for unselected).
Using String instead of f32 to avoid float precision issues on the Rust side.
Written via `set_seekbar_percent` from the `onAmountSeekbarChanged` hook.
Kotlin boundary does Float <-> String conversion via `toSafeString` / `toSafeFloat`.

fields.name: is_seekbar_selected
fields.doc:
Whether the amount currently reflects a seekbar percent selection — drives the
"25%" cover in the amount box. Set true by `set_seekbar_percent` when a real
percent is chosen; cleared by `set_input_amount` (manual typing). Mirrors
SpotLimitState.is_seekbar_selected.

fields.name: raw_amount_unit
fields.doc:
Raw trade-unit code of the amount input ("0"=coin / "1"=zhang / "2"=settle-ccy /
"3"=lot, KB37). Persisted so the order cost (margin) recompute can convert the
unit-denominated `input_amount` into zhang via the #60a unit→zhang dispatch.
Writers: `on_amount_unit_changed` (user switch) + `update_instrument_snapshot` /
`project_session_instrument_into_state` (default unit on instrument bind).
Consumer: `recompute_input_cost` (R-MIG-167). Without it the cost stayed decoupled
from the entered amount (KB45 Behavior 1 root cause).

fields.name: is_bbo_selected
fields.doc:
Whether BBO (best bid/offer) mode is selected in the UI.
Persisted to CTLocalStorage under `key_select_bbo`.

fields.name: bbo_type
fields.doc:
The selected BBO type (e.g. "counter_bid_ask_1st").
Persisted to CTLocalStorage under `key_selected_bbo_type`.
Default `""`; `start()` seeds with CounterAsk1 value if storage is empty.

fields.name: td_mode
fields.doc: Trade mode (cross/isolated/cash) — pushed by Kotlin host on account mode change (D14/H-4).

fields.name: pos_mode
fields.doc: Position mode (net_mode/long_short_mode) — pushed by Kotlin host on account config change (D14/H-4).

fields.name: long_leverage
fields.doc:
Long leverage for buy button (open-long direction). Empty in net mode.
Producer: set_leverage() action pushed by Kotlin TradeContainerFragment.

fields.name: short_leverage
fields.doc:
Short leverage for sell button. In net mode, also used for buy.
Producer: set_leverage() action pushed by Kotlin TradeContainerFragment.

fields.name: trade_direction
fields.doc:
Open/close trade-direction tab: "open" / "close" (long_short mode) or "" (net mode).
Producer: set_trade_direction() action pushed by the Kotlin host from the Fragment
trade-type tab. Drives buy/sell button open-vs-close label text (V1 parity).

fields.name: is_tpsl_supported
fields.doc:
Whether TPSL is supported. True for contract limit orders on the main
panel; forced false for the K-line quick-order compact panel (mirror of
spot `is_quick_order` → hide inline TP/SL). Derived in `start()` as
`!is_quick_order`.

fields.name: is_pre_pending_staging
fields.doc:
Swap pre-pending-order staging (pre-market): when true the attached-TPSL
checkbox is force-hidden on top of the shared visibility rules (Native
`FutureLimitTradePanelPresenter` parity — it hides the TPSL presenter while
`currentPreQuoteState && isNotNewCoinOnLine`). Limit is the only panel shown
during staging (`market_phase` non-Trading forces Limit-only, C11). Wired by
`spawn_pre_pending_staging_subscription` (seed + `InstDataUpdate::PrePendingOrder`).

fields.name: is_quick_order
fields.doc:
Whether this interactor drives the K-line QUICK-ORDER compact panel
(`PureContractQuickLimitFragment`). Additive classification input, seeded
via `bind_standalone_instrument(..., is_quick_order)`. Rust-owned per
native-layer A1 — the compact fragment reads it, never infers it. Gates:
inline TP/SL (`is_tpsl_supported = !is_quick_order`), and is available for
lead-trader-tip / kline-page-type classification consumers. Mirror of spot
`PureSpotLimitState.is_quick_order`.

fields.name: price_tick_hint
fields.doc:
Red inline hint under the order-price box when the typed price is not a
multiple of the instrument tick (V1 `TradeInputUtils.getPriceTickSizeMsg`
-> `pr_trade_text_tick_size_hint`). `Placeholder` (default) = aligned /
no hint. Hint only: native `checkInputFocus` does NOT gate submit on a
price tick error (only empty/zero), so this drives display, not the gate.

fields.name: buy_approx
fields.doc:
Buy-button ≈value (2nd line) numeric part — the entered order size converted
into the currently-selected display unit. Mirror of Native
`AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter.getSwapDisPlayAmt` (KB45 Behavior 2):
non-LOT → `OkSwapBiz::create_zhang_to_unit_convertor_with_index(...).to_target_display`
(Bug#2a, DOWN + targetUnit suffix baked into the `TradingNumber` symbol); TradFi-SWAP+LOT →
`query_unit_display_for_zhang` (the bare lot count `Simple`, the unit goes to `approx_unit`).
`Placeholder` when the size is empty / invalid (Kotlin then renders no 2nd line).

NOTE on placement (R-MIG-167): the spec proposed `ContractBuySellBtnConfig`, but that
struct is built by the pure `derive_btn_config(pos_mode, direction, levers, cool)` which has
no `size_zhang` (the spec's own named STOP probe) and is shared by 8 sibling order types
(would ripple `..Default::default()` to all of them + be wiped on every `derive_btn_config`
rebuild). The size is reachable in `recompute_input_cost`, which projects into state — so
the ≈value lives here, limit-only, independent of btn_config rebuilds.

fields.name: sell_approx
fields.doc:
Sell-button ≈value — identical to `buy_approx` (`getSwapDisPlayAmt` is side-agnostic: the
order amount shown is the same on both buttons). Kept as a separate field for symmetry with
the labels and in case buy/sell ever diverge.

fields.name: approx_unit
fields.doc:
Unit suffix for the ≈value, appended by Kotlin as `"{value} {unit}"` exactly like
`getSwapDisPlayAmt`'s `"$amt $unit"`. `Placeholder` for non-LOT (the symbol is already
baked into `buy_approx`'s `TradingNumber`) and when there is no ≈value; the lot-label
`CDKey` (resolved Native-side, H-2) for TradFi-LOT.

fields.name: is_in_cool_time
fields.doc:
In options-newbie cooling-off period for current symbol (V1 isOpenCoolTime).
Sourced from session.get_option_cool_state().is_in_cool_time(trade_symbol).

Reduce-only view visible — derived (R-MIG-53) from account level (read from trade
setting) + position mode: net mode && not portfolio margin (stage-3 sub-3, mirror

fields.name: raw_available
fields.doc:
Raw (unformatted) available margin balance from the last max-avail fetch.
Writer: `run_max_avail_fetch` on `Loaded`. Consumer: the cost-mode percent
cascade (`compute_effective_cost` needs the raw numeric available; the
`max_avail.available` is a display-formatted `DisplayString`, not parseable).

fields.name: raw_max_buy_size
fields.doc:
Raw (unformatted) max buy/long size from the last max-avail fetch. Consumer:
cost-mode full-percent size clamp (Native `convertCostToAmountWithIndex:216`
`if size>maxAvail && percent=="1" → maxAvail`).

fields.name: raw_max_sell_size
fields.doc:
Raw (unformatted) max sell/short size from the last max-avail fetch. Consumer:
`recompute_input_cost` percent path (Fix1) — the seekbar percent on the SELL side is
applied to this max (V1 `getOrderSizeWithMargin(false)`), the BUY side uses
`raw_max_buy_size`. Captured raw (before `format_response_display`) so it stays parseable.

fields.name: raw_short_available_close
fields.doc:
Raw (unformatted) closeable short/long position from the last max-avail fetch.
Consumer: `derive_input_size_zhang_from_snapshot` close-tab percent base, crossed
by side (buy=close-short->short_available_close, sell=close-long->long_available_close),
mirroring V1/iOS `ContractAvailDisplayUseCase::get_percent_base_value`.

fields.name: raw_short_position
fields.doc:
Raw (unformatted) short/long POSITION size (net reduce-only percent base,
side-crossed: buy=close-short->short_position, sell=close-long->long_position).
Mirrors `raw_*_available_close` (close-tab); Net mode leaves *_available_close
empty so the position size is the closeable base (build_max_avail_loaded net_reduce_only).

fields.name: cost_effective_cost
fields.doc:
Cost-mode effective cost (percent→cost = `available*percent`, else typed cost).
Writer: `recompute_input_cost` cost branch via `ContractCostOrderManager`. Consumer:
Kotlin RenderExt echoes it into the cost-labelled amount box when seekbar-selected.

fields.name: cost_derived_size
fields.doc:
Cost-mode derived contract size (zhang) = `convert_cost_to_contract_size`. Used as the
submit `sz` in cost mode (Rust-derived, replacing the FFI passthrough) and as the
amount-echo size source. Empty when input is invalid / not in cost mode.
This is the LONG (buy-open) side size (long_leverage). See `cost_derived_size_sell`.

fields.name: cost_derived_size_sell
fields.doc:
Cost-mode derived size (zhang) for the SHORT (sell-open) side, using `short_leverage`.
Cost mode is long_short + open only, so the open-short button/confirm/submit must use
the short-lever size (native `convertCostToAmount(isLong=false)` -> `getFutureLeverage`
short). Submit / confirm pick `cost_derived_size` vs this by the order side.

fields.name: is_order_confirm_open
fields.doc:
Order double-confirmation toggle (V1 `OkTradePresenter.makeOrderConfirm`:
`getOrderRemindConfirm() != true` -> place directly, so config-not-loaded
behaves as OFF -> mirrors `get_order_remind_confirm()` default-false).
Refreshed from the canonical account-config cache at every
`pre_check_order` submit (decision-time read, V1 parity) so both the
trade-settings toggle AND the confirm-sheet "don't remind me" write take
effect on the very next order without any lifecycle round-trip.
Defaults `false` until the first submit refresh (no start()-time seed —
spec §H keeps start() side-effect-free); only meaningful at decision time.
Consumer: Kotlin `doProceedToOrderConfirm` gates the confirm sheet on it.

name: persist_tp_kind_pref
doc:

leg. Mirrors native `tpTriggerLimitCallback` (`UniSetTpSlView.kt:1975/1979`),

the observable effect is the persisted pref.

Stores instrument, sets default lever, fetches available balance,
subscribes to spot ticker, and triggers the initial preview.

the unit shown in the amount box on first entry (Android defaults to the
instrument settle ccy / BASE tab). Rust uses it as the initial `cost_ccy`
and spawns the first preview itself, so the initial preview no longer
depends on the caller making a perfectly-timed `on_ccy_changed` call after

OPTION V1 `getBuySellAvailableLabel()` (`OptionTradePanelPresenter.kt:151-172`)
toggles four labels (normal buy / margin buy / normal sell / margin sell)

Composes the Rust-owned business gate of Native
`NewerContractStudyGuideHandler.shouldShowGuide` (`NewerContractStudyGuideHandler.kt:82-89`)
1:1, EXCLUDING the Kotlin-owned gates:
* `!isShowAccountSetup` — a Kotlin static flag set by the account-setup guide sequencing.
* `!hasSeenGuide` — the one-shot "seen" SP flag (keyed on `current_login_uuid()`).
* the deposit gate — Rust `is_study_deposit_gate_met` applied AFTER (`rustDepositGate`).

Native chain (each mapped):
`isContractType(instType)`        → `inst_type == SWAP || inst_type == FUTURES`
`isLogin()`                       → `is_login()`
`isEqualOrGreaterSingleAccount()` → `trade_setting().is_equal_or_greater_single_account()`
`!isDemoMode()`                   → `!is_demo_mode()`
`isProMode()`                     → `is_pro_mode()` (app_mode_provider)
`isFirstPerpetualTrade()`         → `is_first_perpetual_trade()`

`inst_type` is the caller-forwarded current instrument type (a Native input); see
[`should_show_new_user_spot_study`].

trade-quote-ccy. Previously Kotlin callers (TradeWithSwitchView and
peers) imported the now-removed `#[uniffi::export] pub fn
resolve_persisted_trade_quote_ccy` directly. Routing the read through
the Interactor restores the architectural boundary: every cross-module
touch of the storage now flows through `PureSpotLimitInteractor`, so
future invariants (e.g. simulate-line filtering, session-aware
fallback) can be enforced in one place.

derives to update.

name: check_sl_trigger_liq_warning
doc:
Row-1 (reopened) SL-trigger-vs-liquidation pre-order warning.

Native mirror: `OkTradePresenter.checkSlTriggerLiqPx` fed by
`AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter.getLiqPriceAndSlPrice`:2690-2711. The SL price comes
from the ASSEMBLED attach leg list, so SIMPLE / Advanced OCO / Trailing / MULTI are
all covered by one source; the liq price is this panel's own per-side
max-available estimate; the whole gate sits behind `getLiuPxConfirm()`.

Callers pass the two kernel-owned values verbatim
(`PureAttachedTpslInteractor::sl_trigger_px_for_liq_check`, already BASE -- do NOT
convert again -- and `sl_trigger_ratio_for_liq_check`).

Market orders DO support native's dynamic-trigger-price fallback
(`FutureMarketTradePanelPresenter`:602 overrides `supportTpslDynamicTriggerPx` to
true). Native's MARKET branch references the touch price rather than a typed order
price -- `ask1` when buying, `bid1` when selling
(`getLiqPriceAndSlPrice`:2702-2707) -- and this panel has no `input_price` field at
all, matching that. Both ticker prices are already BASE. Pure query (spec section C).

doc:
Which L1 navigation category a tradFi coin should open under.

Tri-state by requirement (NR-2): SPOT and FUTURES MUST stay distinguished —
collapsing them into a single "own business line" value is explicitly wrong,
because confirmed requirement item 2 needs a coin to return to the spot
category or the futures category specifically.

Mirrors OKMarket's published `TradFiNavL1` enum one-for-one, so the value can
cross the bridge without a mapping table on either side.

`FUTURES` on a tradFi coin is in practice perpetual (tradFi has no delivery
futures); the caller does not need to distinguish, per the provider's own doc.

DELIBERATELY NOT `Default`. The derive existed for exactly one reason — to
express "no preference stored" as `Spot` — and the keyed model makes that both
unrepresentable and wrong: absence is now `Option::None` (a miss), and a miss
falls back to `TradFi`, not `Spot` (BR-7.3). Re-adding `Default` would let a
caller silently reintroduce the old, now-incorrect unset semantics.

doc:
Item 2: typed-input mutual-derivation result (Rust-owned).

When the user types into one of the limit double-layout inputs (price /
quantity / amount), Native dispatches the matching action and the Manager
recomputes the dependent field. Native echoes the recomputed string back
into the *other* input (controlled-input SRP) and never performs the
`price × qty` / `amount ÷ price` math itself (A1/A2 compliance) — exactly
the seekbar `CTSpotSeekbarState` contract.

`target` names which input the recomputed `value` should be written to:
`"amount"` (price/qty change → recompute quote amount) or `"quantity"`
(amount change → recompute base qty). `value` is `""` when an input was
cleared / invalid (Native clears the dependent field). `version` is a
monotonic counter so an identical recompute still re-renders.

name: bind_session
doc:
Host-callable session binder (FFI entry). Builds a `PositionData` from
the flat [`IncreasePositionBindArgs`] (the only FFI-passable shape —
`PositionData` itself is not registered in this crate's UniFFI
namespace) then delegates to [`Self::bind_session_for_native`].

The QuickOrder sheet host (R3) calls this right after
`create_for_native()` and before `on_visible()`. Returns `false` when
the instrument fetch fails so native can dismiss the sheet.

Leverage injection: `args.lever` becomes `context.leverage_text`
(context.rs:190) and flows into the cost→contracts margin formula
(build_open_order_request_use_case.rs:286) and the header — the increase
order submits at the HELD position's leverage, not a panel default.

marginLever / marginMode / positionSide from positionItem).

name: set_inst_family
doc:
spec 341/150 — host pushes the raw option instrument FAMILY (e.g.
`"BTC-USD"` / `"BTC-USD_UM"`); Rust resolves the underlying and pulls the
index price ITSELF (OKTradeCore-free). Faithful port of V1
`OptionMultiLegHomeViewModel.init(family)` →
`resolveUnderlying` (:183-186) + `initIndexPriceData` (:164-181).

Steps (INSTRUMENT_SESSION_FIX.md §2):
1. Resolve family → underlying via `OkOptionBiz.get_first_inst_with_fly`
(else strip `_UM`); write `underlying` / `current_underlying`; clear
stale legs (mirrors V1 `cleanLegsData`).
2. Spawn an index-tickers fetch keyed by the RESOLVED underlying (⚠️ NOT
the raw family — avoids the UM empty-idxPx bug); on result write
`datum_point_price` / `ticker_price` and run `bbo::derive_ticker`.
3. Recompute derived rows: `on_family_changed` (margin-switch visibility
+ chain grid) — does NOT push the raw family into the
already-resolved-underlying `on_inst_family_changed` path.

fields.name: input_price
fields.doc:
Current limit-price input content (UI text). SSOT for the price field. Written
via `set_input_price` from the `onOrderPriceChanged` hook in the Kotlin subclass.
AdvancedLimit IS a limit-type order (unlike Market/Trigger), so the cost recompute
uses this typed price as the deal price, falling back to session last price when
empty (V1 selectPrice). Empty string == use last price (R-MIG-167).

fields.name: price_fiat_iso

Fiat iso-code (`USD` / `CNY` / ...) that `input_price` is currently denominated
in, for coin-margined (inverse) contracts whose price box is shown in the user's
legal currency. Used to detect a legal-currency SWITCH (vs live rate drift) so a
depth legal-currency change re-converts the non-empty price to the new fiat instead of
leaving a stale value. Empty until the first projection/seed. Internal (not
rendered by Kotlin). Writers: `project_session_instrument_into_state` + `set_input_price`.

fields.name: price_fiat_rate
fields.doc:
USD->fiat exchange rate at which `input_price` is denominated (paired with
`price_fiat_iso`). Needed to recover the USD base on a fiat switch because
`get_exchange_rate()` only exposes the CURRENT fiat's rate. Empty until first set.
Internal (not rendered). Writers: same as `price_fiat_iso`.

fields.name: input_amount

via `set_input_amount` from the `onAmountInputChanged` hook. Empty == no input.

fields.name: seekbar_percent
fields.doc:
Current seekbar percent as string (e.g. "0.5", "1.0", "" for unselected). String
(not f32) to avoid float drift. Written via `set_seekbar_percent`.

fields.name: is_seekbar_selected

"25%" cover. Set true by `set_seekbar_percent`; cleared by `set_input_amount`.

fields.name: raw_amount_unit
fields.doc:
Raw trade-unit code of the amount input ("0"=coin / "1"=zhang / "2"=settle-ccy /
"3"=lot, KB37). Persisted so the cost recompute can convert the unit-denominated
`input_amount` into zhang via the #60a dispatch. Writers: `on_amount_unit_changed`
+ `update_instrument_snapshot` / `project_session_instrument_into_state` (default
unit on bind). Consumer: `recompute_input_cost` (R-MIG-167).

fields.name: is_tpsl_supported

multiple of the instrument tick (V1 `TradeInputUtils.getPriceTickSizeMsg`).

button. Empty string = no warning. See

(`OkTradePresenter.tradeOrderConfirm`:883-893) -- stage 2 compares against the

max-available pair. Static SL only: native's stage 2 reads
`attachSp.firstOrNull { it.slTriggerPx.gt(0) }` with no dynamic-ratio fallback.

assembled attach leg list (Kotlin fills it from

all covered without a dedicated input field.

Suppression (native `group.optional.disableSlLiqTip`, which stops one order from
raising two dialogs) uses the panel-stage warning key frozen into this exact
attempt. No live panel or attached-kernel state participates at confirm time.

doc:
UI-ready slim VO for the option position close-all entry points.

Replaces the legacy `TradePositionManager.PositionItem` previously rebuilt
(via `PurePositionRawInfoMapper.toPositionItem`) at the two option-close
`toPositionItem` sites in `PurePositionListFragment`:

1. `handleOptionClose` → `CloseOptionFragment.newInstance(positionItem)`
(the native V1 limit-close order panel — reads `instId` / `instType` /
`availPos` and runs its own biz lookups + `TradePresenter.makeOrderRequest`
internally; it is NOT a Pure fragment, so only the three fields it reads
are carried here — `inst_id` / `inst_type` / `avail_pos`).
2. `optionPositionCloseRedirect` → `PureOptionPositionCloseAllBottomSheet`
(the block-trade RFQ shell, driven by the Rust `OptionPositionCloseInteractor`).

The RFQ shell previously read off `PositionItem`:
- **interactor init params** — `instId`, `pos.abs → sz`, `getMarginModel()
→ td_mode`, `getSide() → quote_side` (`startInteractor`,
`PureOptionPositionCloseAllBottomSheet.kt:148-168`). All UI-ready here.
- **`initPositionInfo`** (`...:253-272`) — `TradeTitleUtils.changeTitle
(getSuggestedInstrument)` → `title_parts` (via `CTPositionFormatter::
format_title`), `getCoinUrl(tradeSymbol)` → `coin_url`, `getPositionsSide()`
→ `position_side` (the 4-way side used for the buy/sell tag; Native maps
`net_buy`/`net_sell` to the buy/sell tag CDKey + OKDS style).

The per-quote price / amount / estimated-PnL row depends on the runtime
best-quote price (only known once `OptionPositionCloseInteractor` emits
`QuoteReceived`), so it is NOT on this VO — it is produced on demand by
`get_option_close_quote(pos_id, quote_px)` → [`OktOptionCloseQuoteVo`].

doc:
Whether the SPOT new-user study guide should show for `inst_type`.

Composes the Rust-owned business gate of Native `NewUserGuideHandler`
(`NewUserGuideHandler.kt:48`) 1:1, EXCLUDING the two gates the native layer keeps
outside this predicate:
* `!SPUtils.getBoolean(uid)` — the one-shot "seen" SP flag (Kotlin storage, keyed
on `current_login_uuid()`).
* the deposit gate (`tradeAvailable > 10`) — the Rust `is_study_deposit_gate_met`
snapshot the Kotlin layer applies AFTER this returns (`rustDepositGate`).

Native chain (each mapped):
`currentInstType == TRADE_SPOT_TYPE` → `inst_type == TRADE_SPOT_TYPE`
`TradeAccountManager.isLogin()`      → `CTTradeAccountManager::shared().is_login()`
`!isDemoMode()`                      → `!CTTradeAccountManager::shared().is_demo_mode()`
`!isSubUser()`                       → `!CTTradeAccountManager::shared().is_sub_user()`
`getUserTradeExit() == false`        → `!trade_setting().get_user_trade_exist()`

`inst_type` is the caller-forwarded current instrument type (a Native input): the
Rust host feeds `MainTradeInteractor.get_current_inst_type()`, the native host feeds
its own `SelectBizManager` selection.

is a different surface. The only spot path that discards it is the 51006-family
server-price correction (`pending_price_retry_discards_tpsl`).

name: ct_option_limit_check_input_focus
doc:
V1 `OptionLimitTradePanelPresenter.checkInputFocus` (`:362`, base
`OptionTradePanelPresenter:470`). Pre-submit focus gate — decides which input
(if any) to focus before pre-check, in the SAME order as native:
- price empty / numerically zero → `Price`. Native `price.isNullOrEmpty() ||
price.eq("0")`; price is never negative (numeric input), so empty-or-non-
positive is equivalent to empty-or-zero.
- amount empty / `<= 0`, and the percent seekbar is NOT driving the amount →
`Probably`. Native `contract.lte("0") && isSeekBarSelectedPercent() != true`;
`isSeekBarSelectedPercent() == seekbar_percent.is_some()`.
- amount lot-misaligned (non-percent) OR, for BASIC_LIMIT, price
tick-misaligned → `AmountTickError`. Native's `getInputErrorMsg()` branch;
Kotlin surfaces it inline via `showCorrectValue()`.
- otherwise `None` (inputs valid → proceed to pre-check).

fields.name: avg_px
fields.doc:
Open average price of the position (`item.avgPx`), used to compute the
estimated close PnL `pl = (quotePx - avgPx) * (pos * ctMult)`.
Mirrors `PureOptionPositionCloseAllBottomSheet.renderQuote` `item.avgPx`.
Empty is treated as `0` (Native `subS`/`toSafeDouble` fallback).

fields.name: pos_signed
fields.doc:
SIGNED position size (`item.pos`, the raw value — short is negative, e.g.
"-1"). This is the single source of direction:
- the buy/sell tag: `pos_signed >= 0` → buy, `< 0` → sell;
- the avg-price rounding (via a synthetic "net" position side → derived
net_buy/net_sell in Rust from the sign);
- the estimated-PnL sign (`pos * ctMult`).

Do NOT pass a `getPositionsSide()` string here — Kotlin emits camelCase
("netSell") while Rust constants are snake_case ("net_sell"), so any string
compare silently mis-classifies. `sz` (absolute) is kept separately for the
RFQ leg; the sign lives only here.

name: spawn_account_balance_subscription
doc:
R-MIG-370 DEEP #1 — start the persistent max-available refresh effect
(OCO twin of `PureSpotStopSingleInteractor::spawn_account_balance_subscription`;
strict mirror of spot-limit `spawn_account_balance_subscription`).

NAME DRIFT — despite the name, this spawns NO WS subscription. It
consumes `MaxAvailRefreshDataSource::refresh_ticks()` (5-minute poll ⊕
`TradingEventBus` events, native `TradeBalanceTask` parity) and
re-fetches max-available over HTTP on every tick. See the trigger-model
comment in the effect body for why the original `AccountBalanceDataSource`
(`account` WS channel) trigger was removed.

The OCO max-available price is ALWAYS empty (V1 `isDoubleStopEarn == true`
sends NULL order_price for OCO), so the manager falls back to the backend
`max_size`. Writes the four raw balance fields + the Rust-derived
`can_borrow` into `state.balance`. No-op on the standalone path;
idempotent (`SkipIfRunning`).

keyed by quote ccy. Twin of `AssetTpslState::trade_quote_ccy_balances`,
built by the same shared `usd_settle_ccy_manager::build_balance_display`

balance lines. Native resolves the `DisplayString` directly — NO Kotlin
re-formatting (the legacy `formatTradeWithBalanceLabel` convertor path is
not used by the Rust sheet).

Sourced from a ONE-SHOT HTTP GET of
`/priapi/v5/account/balance?ccy=<picker ccys>` (NOT a WS subscription),
login-gated. A key missing from this map is the pre-network state and
renders as the "--" placeholder; a ccy the backend omits comes back as

[`OktHeaderTradeWithVo`]: `HeaderManager` rebuilds the whole `trade_with`
VO on every snapshot tick, so a field living inside it would be wiped by
the next unrelated data update — exactly the bug `mmr_state` /
`mmr_display` already carry a warning for in `HeaderInteractor`. Sole
writer: the `TradeWithBalances` coordinator.

doc:
String wrapper with metadata and key-value mapping

A flexible string container designed to bridge Rust and native platforms (iOS/Android)
with support for Content Design (CD) key resolution.

# Fields
- `is_cd_key`: Flag indicating if `value` is a Content Design key that requires native-side resolution
- `value`: Either a regular string value or a CD key identifier
- `map`: Additional metadata for context-aware rendering

# Content Design Key Resolution

When `is_cd_key` is true, the `value` field contains a CD key identifier that must be
resolved on the native platform. Native implementations should:
1. Check the `is_cd_key` flag
2. If true, use their localization/content system to resolve the CD key
3. If false, use the `value` directly

This design allows Rust code to remain platform-agnostic while enabling native platforms
to handle localization and content management in their preferred way.

# Example
```ignore
// Regular string
let regular = CTString {
is_cd_key: false,
value: "BTC-USDT-250328".to_string(),
map: None,
};

// Content Design key (resolved on native side)
let cd_key = CTString {
is_cd_key: true,
value: "pr_trade_content".to_string(),
map: None,
};
```

name: CTLocalStorageFFI
doc:
UniFFI wrapper for CTLocalStorage (intentionally public for FFI export)

This struct acts as a Foreign Function Interface (FFI) bridge between Rust
and native platforms (Swift/Kotlin). It wraps the internal `CTLocalStorage`
and exposes its functionality to mobile platforms via UniFFI.

**Note:** This struct MUST be `pub` for UniFFI to generate the FFI bindings.
It is not an internal implementation detail - it's the public API contract
for mobile platforms to access local storage functionality.

External Rust code should use `CTLocalStorage` directly instead of this FFI wrapper.

# Resource Management

This struct uses `&'static CTLocalStorage` which is safe because:
- `CTLocalStorage` instances are managed by `CTStorageManager` as singletons
- Static references have program lifetime and don't need explicit cleanup
- This wrapper is a lightweight reference holder, not a resource owner
- Actual resource cleanup (file handles, etc.) is handled by the underlying
`SharedPreference` implementation when the program terminates
- Factory functions return `Arc<CTLocalStorageFFI>` to ensure safe FFI boundaries

No `Drop` implementation is needed as this struct doesn't own any resources.

impl in [`PureAttachedTpslInteractor::set_strategy_kind`].

V1 had no enum: the Kotlin Fragment instantiated one of 5 `By*SpPresent`
subclasses directly (`new ByPriceSpPresent(...)`). V2 lifts the choice to
data so the binder can stay strategy-agnostic.

P1-δ fix (functional-parity audit 2026-05-26 §S4) — added
`PosMarginByPrice` 5th variant so the enum cardinality (5) matches the
`PureAttachedTpslShowTipsHost` trait cardinality (5 `render_by_*`
methods). Prior to this fix `render_by_pos_margin` on the trait was
unreachable because `render_show_tips` could not dispatch to it.

doc:
V2 state for `PureModifyOrderInteractor` (V1 `ModifyOrderFragment`).

Field set partitioned (28 fields total — yellow KPI zone, justified: the
V1 normal-amend dialog genuinely surfaces last-price + available + a full
two-leg TP/SL section in one screen, so every field is UI-ready and has a
writer):
1. Identity (4)  — order_id / inst_id / inst_type / order_type
1b. Display (4)  — side / pos_side / td_mode / tgt_ccy (editor-seed only)
1c. Dynamic (3)  — last_price / available / max_buy_sell (session-free)
2. Inputs (4)    — original_price / original_size + new_price / new_size
3. TP/SL legs (6)— TP triple (original+new) + SL triple (original+new)
4. Submit (4)    — submit_state + flags

name: convert_price_to_display
doc:
Align a BASE ticker / K-line price to the instrument's display precision
(priceDig) for the price input box. Spot has no inverse fiat leg, so this
is identity + `priceDig` truncation (`RoundingMode::Down`, matching V1
`OKTChargeConvertor` and the contract limit interactor's exported
`convert_price_to_display`). Used by the K-line quick-order seed path so an
arbitrary-precision tapped price is aligned the same way the ticker
fallback (`state.last_price`) is already aligned by the display convertor;
without it the raw seed flows through `on_price_changed` (the verbatim
controlled-input channel) and echoes back unrounded.

Empty input or a not-yet-bound instrument returns the input unchanged
(graceful; a later render/tick aligns it once the instrument is ready).

NOTE: a new `#[uniffi::export]` method requires UniFFI binding regen before
Kotlin / iOS can call it; the Rust side compiling is the gate here.

name: ChaseConfirmSideLabelKind
doc:
Trade-direction tag *text* discriminator. Mirrors V1
`ChaseOrderConfirmFragment.getSideString(side, posSide)` exactly (6 outcomes).
Rust owns the side+pos_side business classification (A1 / H-4) AND now emits
the resolved CDKey via [`Self::to_cd_key`], so the state field is a
`DisplayString::CdKey` (Kotlin resolves it via `.resolve(ctx)`, H-2/H-3 —
it no longer maps the enum to `R.string` itself). This enum stays as an
internal classification helper; it is NOT a state field.

CDKey mapping:
- `Buy` → `pr_trade_btn_buy`
- `Sell` → `pr_trade_btn_sell`
- `OpenLong` (buy + long) → `pr_trade_iso_btn_long`
- `OpenShort` (sell + short) → `pr_trade_iso_btn_short`
- `CloseLong` (buy + short) → `pr_trade_orderlist_label_text_close_long`
- `CloseShort` (sell + long) → `pr_trade_history_label_close_short`

Note the tag *color* is decided separately by [`ContractConfirmSideColorKind`]
(V1 `TradeDirectionColorUtil.getTagStyle(side)` keys off buy/sell only).

name: ensure_cost_derived_fresh
doc:
V1 `checkTPSLPreValid` / `checkInputFocus` for the TPSL advanced entry, lowered to
Rust (A1). Advanced limit always requires the order price (no BBO skip), then the
amount(sz) empty branch, then the amount tick-size branch — mirrors the first three
branches of `pre_check_order`'s pre-flight. Pure query (interactor-spec §C, no state
mutation); injects the cost-aware entry toast on the empty branches and `toast:
None` on the tick branch (Kotlin `showCorrectValue`). `input` is the representative
input the advance sheet already builds (Kotlin `buildAdvancedLimitOrderInput(isBuy =
true)`), so `order_request.sz` matches submit (no drift, correct in cost mode).
Cost mode: recompute `cost_derived_size` via the EXISTING cascade if it is empty while a
cost is entered (the cascade dep -- leverage / deal_price -- may have settled AFTER the
last input-triggered recompute). Reuses `recompute_cost_mode` (same formula, no drift);
no-op in amount mode / when already derived. Called at the gate + submit so the sz
reflects the current cost (device recvqnnXvx6KW4).

§1.3; existing native/Rust callers populate it via named fields.

fields.name: avail_pos
fields.doc:
Available position for closing (only for buy/sell mode). Mirrors
`PositionData.avail_pos` (`types/position/position_data.rs:63`). Additive,
forward-compatible. Standalone sheets (e.g. K-line facade) must populate
it: the close-amount long/short branch reads `position.avail_pos`
(`close_position_manager.rs:1821`); leaving it empty makes the confirm

fields.name: liab
fields.doc:
Borrowed amount (MARGIN positions only). Mirrors `PositionData.liab`
(`types/position/position_data.rs:87`). Additive, forward-compatible.

Raw pass-through: the MARGIN position TP/SL estimated profit needs
`abs(liab + interest)`, and that sum is derived in Rust
(`business::tpsl::domain::derive_position_total_liability`, exported to the
hosts as `derive_position_total_liability`) — never in Kotlin/Swift.
Contract positions leave it empty, which the derive reads as "no debt".

`#[uniffi(default = "")]` (trailing field) keeps hosts that have not yet
regenerated — or that build this Record from a row without a liability —
source-compatible; the earlier additive fields (`pos_ccy` / `interest` /
`margin` / `avail_pos`) landed without one and broke committed callers
one-by-one (see `PositionItemOktMapper`'s doc).

`update_trade_capability` state-write logic (single writer, no

`TradeCoreProxy.getTrade()?.isLogin()` / `getBiz("SPOT")?.isEnableTrade()`

Unified business biz_facade trait for all trading products

Provides common interface for Spot, Swap, Futures, Options, etc.
This trait is exported via UniFFI, enabling polymorphic usage on iOS/Android.

# iOS/Android Usage

```kotlin
// Kotlin - polymorphic container
val bizMap: MutableMap<String, BizFacade> = mutableMapOf()
bizMap["SPOT"] = factory.createSpotFacade()
bizMap["SWAP"] = factory.createSwapFacade()

bizMap.values.forEach { biz ->
println("${biz.getBizType()}: ${biz.getAllInstruments().size}")
}
```

TP-limit entrust-price display (mirror native
`ConvertPosTpslOrderData.getLimitTpEntrustPriceNoSign`): the TP-limit entrust
price row shows the LIMIT committed price `px` (NOT the trigger price, and NOT
`tp_ord_px`) when the order is a TP-limit (`is_tp_limit`). Native builds it via
`createChargeConverterWithIndex(instFamily).toQuoteFormatted(px).group()` gated on
`px > 0` (else `NO_VALUE_PLACE_HOLDER`) — the SAME charge-convertor + per-inst-family
priceDig (A5) + side round-mode (A4) + no-sign path. #13 (2026-07-17): sourced from
`px` here; `tp_ord_px` is an algo/conditional field that is empty/"0"/"-1" for a
plain limit-TP order, so the earlier `tp_ord_px` source rendered "--". UNGROUPED
(native `formatRustNumber` adds locale thousands). Populated in
`inject_price_display` ONLY for TP-limit rows (`is_tp_limit == true`); `format_px`
mirrors native's `px > 0` gate, so empty otherwise and the contract-normal tab can
gate the row on emptiness. Additive, defaults empty.

fields.name: sz_display
fields.doc:
B1 / A2 migration twin of the per-row close-amount NUMBER (mirror native
`RustPosContractNormalSpFragment.formatAmount`,
`RustPosContractNormalSpFragment.kt:1008-1029`). The fixed-quantity tab amount row
currently formats `sz` (raw contract count) in Kotlin via the OKTradeCore
`TradeCoreProxy` trade convertor (`createTradeConverterWithIndex` /
`createTradeConvertorWithIndex(TRADE_UNIT_LOT)` + `setPrice(transferPrice)`,
then `.round().group().suffix().changeUnique().toSafeNoSignString()`). This
twin moves that conversion into Rust so the per-row sz formatting lives where
numeric conversion belongs (A2): the canonical `PositionConvertor
::get_quantity_formatter(sz, Some(transfer_price))` auto-routes to the LOT
branch for TradFi SWAP and to the price-aware coin/contract branch otherwise — the
SAME convertor `lot_sz_display` / close-position / order-list use, so precision
is shared (NOT reinvented). `RoundingMode::Down` + trailing-zeros removed mirror
the `OKTFormatter` default the display path keeps (A4, same as `lot_sz_display`).
Sign/unit-symbol dropped (native `toSafeNoSignString`) — the unit label ("Cont" /
"Lot" / coin) is carried separately by `amount_unit` / `amount_unit_display`.
`transfer_price` is derived per-row from the VO via the native `getTransferPrice`
rule (`RustPosContractNormalSpFragment.kt:1026-1039`). Empty when `sz` is
empty/unparseable (native `NO_VALUE_PLACE_HOLDER`). Populated in
`PositionTpslInteractor::inject_price_display`. Additive, defaults empty.

NOTE (device-verify caveat): the Kotlin switch to `szDisplay` should be parity-
checked on-device against the legacy `formatAmount` for inverse contracts, where
the `setPrice(transferPrice)` price-dependent contract↔coin conversion matters most.

V1 parity: `SpotAdvancedLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:457-480 onResume`.

V1 onResume body (Round 2 SEV-2 close, audit § 9):
1. `isPmUnique` branch — toggle amount-input percent visibility
2. `addDelayInputChangeListener(lendAmountChange)` on amount
3. `addInputChangeListener(priceChangeListener)` on price
4. `addDelayInputChangeListener(assetPriceChange)` on price
5. `addInputChangeListener(amountChangeListener)` on amount
6. `addInputChangeListener(probablyChangeListener)` on probably
7. `showSpotPriceCurrencyCal()` when price input is non-empty
8. `loadAvailableAndTicker()` — ticker prefill + delayed checkAvailable

Round 2 surface contract: the action body is intentionally empty (no
state writes, no UxEvent emits) — Kotlin's Fragment.onResume calls
this hook so the trait declares an explicit attach-point. Round 3
will wire (a) the listener-attach side effects via Rust producers
(T-LIFECYCLE-onResume) and (b) the ticker prefill / available pull
once the manager + session subscriptions land (mirror spot-limit
baseline `on_visible`).

doc:

- Liquidation: MMR <= 100%         (100.0 exactly -> Liquidation)
- Unknown:     data missing or unparseable

doc:
V2 state for `PureModifyTriggerOrderInteractor` (V1
`ModifyTriggerOrderFragment`).

Trigger orders have *two* user-editable price inputs:
- `trigger_price` — the price at which the order becomes live.
- `order_price`   — the execution price after the trigger fires
(empty / "-1" means market price).

`trigger_price_type` is the V1 `triggerPxType` selector ("last" /
"mark" / "index").  The dialog also lets the user switch the
execution mode between limit and market.

20 fields total:
1. Identity (5)  — order_id / inst_id / inst_type / order_type / algo_id
1b. Display (5)  — side / pos_side / td_mode / leverage / tgt_ccy
(variant-4 widen, subtitle + trade-with only)

new_trigger / new_order / new_size +

name: query_panel_unit_projection
doc:
Native-callable: build the future trade panel unit projection for the
given instrument + selected trade unit + balance/price snapshot.

Returns `None` when the instrument is not TradFi or the user has not
selected the Lot unit — native then falls back to its existing
zhang/coin/usdt rendering. When `Some(_)`, every field is UI-ready and
native must render verbatim (no parsing, no recomposition).

Native is expected to call this query at the following moments:
- on entering the panel (initial render),
- when the user toggles the trade unit chip,
- when max-available updates push a new value,
- when the ticker last-price ticks (throttled),
- when the user types a new amount (estimated value re-render).

`max_buy_zhang` / `max_sell_zhang` are zhang (contracts) — Rust handles
the zhang→lot conversion using the instrument's `lot_size_std`.
`current_amount_lot` is the user's typed amount **already in Lot units**
(the panel input field's Lot-mode content). Empty string means "no
input yet" → estimated value falls back to the 1-lot canonical demo.

`long_order_size_zhang` / `short_order_size_zhang` are the
percent-applied order sizes in **zhang** (raw, not lot) — same as what
Native passes to `BalanceLoader.refreshOrderPxSize`. These drive the
`buy_cost_display` / `sell_cost_display` cost computation. Pass empty
strings to disable cost — Native then falls back to BE
`buyCost`/`sellCost` for the cost label.

`leverage` is a decimal string (e.g. "10"); empty disables cost.
`is_market_price_selected` is the user's market-price toggle (limit-style
strategies); when true Rust uses `ticker_price` instead of `last_price`
as the deal price (mirrors Native `MarginInfoHelper.selectPrice`).

doc:
Build a fresh [`PureSpotLimitConfirmInteractor`] populated from the
current state (via [`build_confirm_snapshot`]). The child carries a
`Weak<PureSpotLimitInteractor>` so its `confirm()` action can route
back through [`Self::proceed_after_confirm`].

Lifecycle:
1. The pre-check pipeline calls this when `is_order_confirm_open` is
true (see `pre_check_order`).
2. The interactor is stashed in `pending_confirm_interactor` and the
`ShowOrderConfirm` UxEvent is emitted.
3. Kotlin retrieves the child via
[`Self::take_pending_confirm_interactor`].
4. The child is alive as long as the BottomSheet holds it; once the
sheet dismisses, the last Arc drops and the child is freed.

Marked `#[uniffi::export]` so future callers (e.g. a future Kotlin
direct-invoke path that bypasses the event channel) can build a child
on demand. Stage-1 callers go through `pre_check_order`.

§J.2 parent factory: builds the render-ready snapshot from the current
frozen submit attempt and returns a child carrying only that attempt id.
The Kotlin host calls this after the existing price-relationship check (replacing the
legacy OKDialog confirm). Stop (TPSL) orders have NO PreCheck (A3) — there
is no PreCheck result param, unlike the trailing confirm.
Live decision-time read of the order double-confirm toggle. V1 reads
`getOrderRemindConfirm()` per order right before showing the confirm
(stop funnel `OkTradePresenter.makeOrderConfirm:594`), so
config-not-loaded behaves as OFF (`get_order_remind_confirm()`
default-false). Pure query (spec §C `is_*`): zero side effects. Kotlin
gates the confirm sheet on it right before `create_confirm_interactor`;
OFF -> place the order directly.
