fields.doc:
Maximum amount formatted for display.

Phase 4.3 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust TradeConvertor
port (see `common::display::trade_display::format_max_amount_display`)
and emits a `DisplayString::TradingNumber { sign: None, symbol:
Some(target_unit), .. }` (USDT/USD for U mode; base coin for COIN mode;
"Zhang" for CONTRACT mode). Helper consumes Phase 4.0
`cached_ticker_price` for branches that need a conversion rate (linear-U,
inverse-COIN); when the ticker has not arrived yet it returns
`Placeholder` so the row reads "--" matching Native.
Single ALSO routes this through the TradeConvertor port (same chain as
dual, with its own ticker subscription — `single/interactor.rs`).
Margin / Coin / BorrowedCoin format via `common::display::spot_margin_display`
(`format_spot_amount_4dp` / `format_borrow_amount`). ContractExp /
AccountRiskComparison do not render this row.

`LeverInfoValue::Single` for every scenario except Margin, which emits
`DualUnit` ("base or quote") off the response's quote-side amount.

fields.name: margin_display
fields.doc:
Required margin formatted for display.

Phase 4.2 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust SizeConvertor
port (see `common::display::size_display::format_margin_display`) and
emits a `DisplayString::TradingNumber { sign: None, symbol:
Some(profit_symbol), .. }` (USDT for linear; settle ccy for inverse).
Single ALSO routes this through the SizeConvertor port (same as dual).
Margin formats via `spot_margin_display::format_margin_required`. Coin /
BorrowedCoin keep `Single` here, but the row is not rendered (mapper only
pushes the max-amount row). ContractExp / AccountRiskComparison omit it.

Margin emits `DualUnit` ("base or quote") off the response's
`quote_margin`; the quote-only fallback is how V1 renders "0 USDT" when
the base-side margin is empty.

fields.name: liq_px_display
fields.doc:
Liquidation price formatted for display.

Phase 4.1 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust
ChargeConvertor port (see
`common::display::charge_display::format_liq_px_display`) and emits a
`DisplayString::TradingNumber` (linear: no sign; inverse: fiat sign).
Single ALSO routes this through the ChargeConvertor port (same as dual).
Margin keeps `DisplayString::Simple` here, gated off by `show_liq_px`
(V1 margin has no liq row — pending L3 device confirm whether isolated
margin surfaces one). Coin / BorrowedCoin: Simple + not rendered.
ContractExp / AccountRiskComparison omit it.

name: ensure_cost_derived_fresh
doc:
V1 `checkTPSLPreValid` / `checkInputFocus` for the TPSL advanced entry, lowered
to Rust so the readiness DECISION (which box is empty, which toast, tick error)
is the single source of truth (A1). Pure query (interactor-spec §C, no state
mutation): mirrors the first three branches of `pre_check_order`'s pre-flight —
empty price (unless BBO) -> empty amount(sz) -> amount tick-size error — but
injects the cost-aware entry toast on the empty branches (V1
`getTPSLPreValidMessage`) and returns `toast: None` for the tick branch so Kotlin
calls `showCorrectValue`. Kotlin performs only the UI side-effect (focus +
toast/showCorrectValue), never the decision. `input` is the same representative
order input the advance sheet already builds (Kotlin
`buildContractLimitOrderInput(isBuy = true)`), so `req.sz` is derived identically
to submit (no gate/submit drift, correct in cost mode too).
Cost mode: recompute `cost_derived_size` via the EXISTING cascade if it is empty while a
cost is entered (the cascade dep -- leverage / deal_price -- may have settled AFTER the
last input-triggered recompute). Reuses `recompute_cost_mode` (same formula, no drift);
no-op in amount mode / when already derived. Called at the gate + submit so the sz
reflects the current cost (device recvqnnXvx6KW4).

doc:
Pre-check resp snapshot — the margin-relevant fields lifted out of the
shared `OrderPreCheckResp` (`types/make_order/order_pre_check_resp.rs`).

# Why a margin-owned snapshot (not the raw `OrderPreCheckResp`)
`OrderPreCheckResp` is a serde-deserialize wire type, not a UniFFI Record,
and it carries ~30 fields. State must be a `#[interactor::state]` UniFFI
type, so the interactor projects only the margin-confirm-relevant subset
here. Every field stays a RAW string (server convention) — the
`DisplayString` / `TradingNumber` formatting (A4 HalfUp, symbol/sign) is
applied at b016 (`orchestration::confirm`) when shaping the display rows.

All fields mirror `OrderPreCheckResp` 1:1 (same name, raw string). The
`change_*` siblings are the "after-order" values; the bare names are the
"before-order" values — i.e. the before/after pairs the margin confirm
sheet renders (Positions Total, Liability, MMR/IMR check).

reduces to the global leader flag. Rust-owned (mirror

H-4 cross-platform). The amend dialog has two tabs (TPSL / trailing-stop);
which are visible depends on the order's EXISTING attach type, classified in
`bind_order` (A1 — no Kotlin classification): order carries a trailing stop
→ trailing-only; carries OCO/MULTI TP/SL → tpsl-only; neither → both.

* Then format via `TradeCoreManager.getTrade()?.getBiz(instType)?
.createBaseCcyDisplayConverterWithIndex(...)` (when `isDigitDisplay`
and ccy is the trade symbol) or `.createTradeConverterWithIndex(...)`
otherwise.

Stage-1 Rust port: looks up the SPOT instrument by `inst_id`, derives the
target ccy with the same BUY/SELL branching, and returns the raw size as
both `display` and `raw`. Precision formatting is deferred to the Kotlin
caller (see [`QuoteCcyConvertResult`] doc).

name: ct_order_detail_build_deal_section
doc:
Build the fill details (fill-details) section JSON for the order-detail page.

Mirrors V1 `convertNormalOrderDetailDealHeader` (column titles) +
`convertTradeFillsDataToOrderDetailDeal` (formatted rows), rendered by
`OrderDetailsDealHeaderItemBinder` + `OrderDetailsDealItemBinder`.

Each fill is formatted through `TradeFillDataExt` (side-aware price rounding,
HalfUp amount rounding, fee value + fee-currency symbol — the SAME convertor
path V1 uses via `getPrice` / `getAmount` / `getFeeWithoutSign`). The fill
timestamp is emitted as a `DisplayString::Date` so the native layer renders a
locale date (V1 `fmtOrderDetailsTime` = DATE_FORMAT_SIMPLE + TIME_FORMAT_SIMPLE
→ `DateFormat::SimpleMonthDayTime`). Column titles are CDKeys.

`show_fee` mirrors the native fee-column gate (`OrderDetailsDealItemBinder.showFee`,
hidden for OPTION).

# Parameters
- `fills_json`: JSON string of `Vec<TradeFillsData>`
- `inst_type`: instrument type (drives the OPTION fee-column gate)
- `_is_history`: history flag (kept for forward compatibility / parity with
the V1 `convertTradeFillsDataToOrderDetailDeal(history, ...)` signature)

# Returns
JSON string of `OrderDetailDealSectionVo`, or an empty-section JSON on parse
failure (never an empty string, so the native side always gets the column
titles even when fills are absent).

name: seed_amend_market_price
doc:
Seed the LAST price for the modify / position-TP/SL path. The editor
kernel built via `create_with_self_session` holds a minimal session with
no live WS ticker, so the ByPrice price-change%/PnL linkage cannot anchor on the
market price (the order-attach path borrows the panel's live session and
does not need this). The Kotlin modify fragment pushes its observed
`viewModel.lastPrice` here on each ticker tick; both the OUTCOME compute
(`PriceSourceHost::ticker_price` → `apply_by_price_rate_linkage`) and the
amend `validate_*` path (`resolve_market_price`) fall back to it when the
session ticker is empty. The override lives on `native_host` rather than
in State because the compute path reads the price through the host, never
from a State field. Additive — a no-op when never seeded.

name: create_pure_spot_advanced_limit_interactor
doc:
Create the spot advanced-limit panel as a CHILD of this container,
sharing the SAME `TradeSessionContext` MainTrade owns (sourced from the
manager — A1 re-parent shares the session, never creates a new one;
design §3.1) AND — A (side fix) — handing the panel the container's
BUY/SELL `watch` receiver (`manager.subscribe_side()`) so
container-driven side switches flow Rust parent -> child instead of
through the Kotlin global tab (single-track: the panel no longer needs
the native `update_side` push). Mirrors
`create_pure_spot_limit_interactor`; the MainTrade-fallback factory
passes `None` (no container shell, side keeps coming from the native
tab). Supersedes the earlier B2 "create-routing only" shape (no
session / no side watch) now that advanced-limit self-reads its
session-derived data.

not carry, so `from_order_data` defaults this to the proxy-free subset
(conditional / oco only) and the order-list interactor recomputes it via

cache. The Pure order-list signal-clone-share CTA reads this ready flag for STRATEGY_TRIGGER
rows (the sibling `TradeOrderVo.is_positive_contract` covers TNO_LIMIT rows) instead of the
cold OKTradeCore biz accessor (null under the Rust gate).

(For strategy rows, only ord_type == "trigger" passes the ord_type conjunct;
"conditional" / "oco" are excluded, matching native.) Read by the Kotlin
binder directly. See `resolve_is_show_signal_clone_share`.

doc:
Which primary action the auto-earn OPEN page must offer.

Behavior Contract = native `AutoEarnActivity.refreshShowDepositEntry`
(`AutoEarnActivity.kt:273-300`): the host queries the account balance for the
page currency and shows the deposit entry when
`TradeAssetsUtils.isEqLteZero(detail)` (a MISSING detail also counts as
at-or-below-zero, `?: true`).

RUST-FIRST replacement for the Native-computed `show_deposit_entry` bool: a
plain bool cannot distinguish "balance says Enable" from "no verdict yet",
so its `false` default silently rendered "Enable" for zero-balance users on
any host that did not push the value. `Unknown` makes the un-resolved case
explicit instead.

name: on_collateral_changed
doc:
Collateral-coin switch — re-derive the panel (V1 onResume reload).

CONSOLIDATED handler for rxbus/002 + rxbus/005 + observers/003 +
observers/004 (V1 `BaseTradePanelPresenter:362-371` /
`BaseBusinessFragment:390-400`): all four V1 entries observe the
`collateralChangeDetector` flow (Rust-gated path) and call `onResume()`,
which reloads order state + margin info. In V2 the ViewModel collects the
`collateralChangeDetector` flow and calls this single action. The panel
re-derive == re-pull max-available (the margin-info reload). Consolidated
4 V1 entries → ONE action.

variants.name: Low

doc:
Simple-account borrow risk level.

Rust-owned classification derived from the margin ratio. Native maps each
variant onto a colour in `getSimpleModeLoanStatusTextRes` (L147-153):
- `None`        -> profit green (risk-free / no borrow record). Native shares
the green colour with `Low`, but the classification is kept distinct so the
consumer preserves the "no record" semantics (status label + board = 700).
- `Liquidation` -> `ContentPrimary` (mgnRatio <= 100%).
- `High`        -> `SemanticNegative` (100% < mgnRatio <= 300%).
- `Medium`      -> `SemanticNotice`  (300% < mgnRatio <= 500%).
- `Low`         -> profit green      (mgnRatio > 500%).

name: on_hidden
doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase).

Distinct from `stop_balance_stream` (which the Fragment calls on BOTH the
order-type-switch hide AND Activity backgrounding): the Pure host swaps
spot order-type panels via show/hide keep-alive, so a hidden panel never
gets an Activity-level pause. Native, by contrast, re-inflates a fresh
Fragment per order-type and on the single vs double variant switch, so it
shows a blank draft each time. The typed draft lives in Rust state and
survives hide/show, so to mirror native we clear the input draft on this
hide transition ONLY.

Kotlin routing: `PureSpotStopSingleFragment.onHiddenChanged(hidden=true)`
calls this ONLY when the hide is an in-container order-type / variant
switch (`!isHiddenByAncestor()`); a Home / Trade tab switch hides the
shell too, so it does NOT call this and the draft is PRESERVED (native
keeps the cache slot on tab-return). Sibling parity with
`PureSpotLimitInteractor::on_hidden`.

Field set mirrors the canonical draft clear the panel already uses on a
side switch / pair switch / logout edge (`apply_side_state_mutation`
side_changed block + `reset_for_logout`): trigger price, order price,
amount, seekbar. Additive action, forward-compatible with bindings that
never call it.

name: take_pending_confirm_interactor

Drain the pending-slot set by `pre_check_order`. Kotlin calls this in
the `ShowOrderConfirm` UxEvent handler to retrieve the child.

**Re-bind step**: the child stashed by the effect closure carries a
`Weak::new()` parent reference (the closure had no Arc<Self>). When
Kotlin retrieves the child via this method we re-create the parent
`Weak` from the live `Arc<Self>` and substitute the stashed child
with a freshly-built one that captures the correct parent — the
freshly-built variant inherits the current state (so the user-typed
price / amount the moment the dialog opens is reflected, including
any race-window edits).

Returns `None` when no confirm flow is pending (e.g. Kotlin
re-entrant call after dismiss).

variants.name: SubmitFullSuccess
SubmitPartialSuccess
variants.doc:
Submit succeeded on some — but not all — of the enabled dual sides.
Native keeps the page open so the user can edit / retry the failed
side. The `*_succeeded` flags identify which side(s) need attention.
Only dual scenario emits this; single / margin emit `SubmitFullSuccess`.

variants.name: SubmitErrorToast
variants.doc:
Transient toast bridge for `LeverageBusinessError::GeneralError` —
the only error variant whose behavior strategy is `Toast`. The
persistent rendering still flows through state (input section error
/ submit error_message); this event triggers the additional
transient toast. `message` is a CDKey-resolvable string.

variants.name: HighLeverageConfirmationRequired
variants.doc:
The facade requires the user to confirm a high-leverage submission.
Native renders the warning dialog using the provided CDKeys and bolds
the leverage number(s) carried by `long_trigger` / `short_trigger`.
Native calls `confirm_high_leverage_warning(section_id)` to continue
or `cancel_high_leverage_confirmation()` to abort.

Exactly one of `long_trigger` / `short_trigger` is `Some` for the
dual single-side cases; both are `Some` when long+short both trip.
For single / margin scenarios `long_trigger` carries the section id
(`"single"` / `"margin"`) and `short_trigger` is `None`.

variants.name: SubmitAccountRiskSuccess
variants.doc:
AccountRiskComparison scenario-specific success variant. Carries the
full BE `SwitchAccountPresetResponse` so callers (e.g.
`RiskComparisonBottomDialog`) can read `lever` / `curAcctLv` /
`acctLv` / `riskOffsetType` and decide their own dismiss + toast
behavior. The S16 contract diverges from the other 6 scenarios:
V2 must NOT self-toast or self-dismiss here. The other scenarios
continue to use `SubmitFullSuccess` (which Native interprets as
"show success toast + dismiss page").

variants.name: SubmitAccountRiskError
variants.doc:
AccountRiskComparison scenario-specific failure variant. Paired with
`SubmitAccountRiskSuccess` so V1 callers always receive a
`(success, resp)` signal (V1
`AccountRiskCompAdjustLeverDFragment.kt:115-116` invokes
`mSubmitCallback?.invoke(false, null)` on failure). Native still
renders the persistent error through state (R2 red line — error
message stays in `page_vo.error`), but this transient signals the
caller's callback fire.

doc:
One-shot UI events emitted to native after each action completes.

UxEvent (one branch = one variant) rule: never reuse a variant with a
"kind" tag. See `spec/interactor.md` §F.

All user-visible strings are CDKeys (per §D + §F) — Rust does not know
the device locale and never hardcodes natural language.

**Phase 5.1 contract**: submit outcomes are split into three transient
events plus a state-only "all failed" channel. Errors are not routed
through a generic `SubmitError` variant — `mapper::apply_submit_error`
reflects them onto `page_vo.is_locked` / `submit.error_message` /
`input_sections[*].error` (R2 red line: errors do not ride on transient
toasts), and only `LeverageBusinessError::GeneralError` additionally
surfaces `SubmitErrorToast` as a transient bridge (the persistent
rendering still flows through state — see `mapper::apply_submit_error`).

name: get_close_all_blocked_message
doc:
Build the explanation CDKey for a blocked "Close all" action.

Sibling of [`Self::get_close_all_message`] and deliberately the same
shape: Rust owns the key, Native keeps only the toast render. FR-10
requires every Rust-produced row title AND disabled reason to travel as a
`DisplayString`/CDKey rather than a Rust bare string, and TC-20 guards it;
routing this round's new reason through a typed enum with the copy owned
in Kotlin would have left it as the one piece of Rust-decided
user-visible text that never enters the DisplayString pipeline.

TOTAL over [`OKTBatchCloseBlockedReason`] on purpose — no `_` catch-all,
so a future variant cannot silently fall through to someone else's copy.
`None` resolves to `Placeholder` (`DEFAULT_VALUE_NONE`): nothing is
blocked, so there is no message to show.

The two already-shipped reasons are mapped here as well, even though
Kotlin deliberately KEEPS its existing `when` branches for them
(`PureMainPositionsFragment.kt:775-787`, which resolve
`pr_trade_positions_toast_closeall_not_available` and

doc:
Post-order-success reset — native `TPSLViewBinder.clearTPSLConfig(false)`
parity. Native's `resetData` keeps the master take-profit/stop-loss
checkbox + panel visibility, and `clearInputLayout` is type-gated
(`curTpType == TP_SL_BY_PRICE`) so ONLY a ByPrice leg's box clears while a
ByRate / ByProfit leg keeps its value. Unlike [`Self::clear_all_tpsl`]
(uncheck / order-type switch — a full wipe to ByPrice), this leaves the
panel checked with the simple by-rate value intact after placing an order.
- advanced / OCO / MULTI / Trailing active -> clear the active advanced
config, then restore a parked simple ByRate / ByProfit draft when one
exists. Programmatic advanced presets without a draft return blank.
- inline simple -> per-leg: a ByPrice leg fully clears; a non-ByPrice
(ByRate / ByProfit) leg keeps its rate / profit value + strategy kind.
The master checkbox is Kotlin-owned (kernel does not drive it), so the host
simply does NOT uncheck it around this call. Host-synced context pricing
(entry / lever / position_size) is kept either way.

doc:
New-coin min-size-hint suppression predicate (the DEFER-GAP deliverable).

Combines the two V1 `bindFloatWindow` inputs into ONE Rust-owned boolean
so Native does NO classification (A1 — the Fragment reads one flag, never
`&&`s two Rust state fields on the Kotlin side):
suppress = `is_new_coin_online_blocking` (`isNewCoinOnLineAndNotWhiter`,:3574)
|| `is_in_new_coin_countdown`    (`newCoinOnLineLv` true,:3576)
REQUEST 2 (Image 20): input ① now reads the Rust self-derived
`is_new_coin_online_blocking` (session-projected) instead of the
deprecated Native-push `is_new_coin_disabled` — iOS stopped pushing the
latter, so any reader still on it got `false` and the float-window was
never suppressed. `is_in_new_coin_countdown` is kept as-is.
When `true`, the (later-round) min-order-amount soft-keyboard float
window must be unbound / not bound; when `false`, it binds with the
min-size hint. The float-window widget that consumes this is a follow-up
round; this round delivers the predicate + its two inputs.

doc:
Close order error classification.

`ClosePositionsBasePresenter.makeOrderRequest`:

name: update_seekbar
doc:
**Seekbar percent selection** — BUG-5 (real-device 2026-06-03): selecting
a seekbar percentage did NOT fill the amount input because the trigger
panel had no percent action (the foundations note above predates the
seekbar attach). Wire the percent→amount chain mirroring the sibling
SpotLimit `update_seekbar` (`spot_limit_interactor.rs:665` decl + `:4513`
impl): `is_selected=true` writes `amount` from `percent × max-amount`
(rounded via the shared `calculate::percent_to_amount`) + records
`seekbar_percent`; `is_selected=false` clears both.

VALUE contract = trigger V1 NATIVE (`AbsSpotTradePanelPresenter`
`getSumMaxSize`/`getSumAvailable` :1036-1076): the max-amount the percent
scales is the side-aware balance — BUY → `max_size` (=`avail_eq`, the
base-ccy max-buyable), SELL → `available` (=`avail_balance`, the base-ccy
sellable) — with the loan portion subtracted when `!can_borrow` (V1 `if
(!canBorrow()) max = max.subS(loanMaxSize)` / `avi.subS(loanAvailable)`).
This is the SAME side-pick + loan-fold `on_depth_amount_clicked` /
`recompute_avail_displays_internal` use, so the seekbar amount matches the
displayed max-buy/max-sell figure. A2/H-1 — the multiply/divide/round is Rust
Decimal, never Kotlin.

doc:
Dynamic-trigger-price companion of [`Self::sl_trigger_px_for_liq_check`].

A ByDynamicPrice stop-loss leg emits `sl_trigger_ratio` and CLEARS
`sl_trigger_px` (the API rejects both -- see the OCO builder in
`base/make_order.rs`), so the static getter above returns "" for it. Native then
derives the comparison price from the ratio, but ONLY on panels whose
`supportTpslDynamicTriggerPx()` is true -- limit
(`FutureLimitTradePanelPresenter`:1646) and market
(`FutureMarketTradePanelPresenter`:602). Advanced-limit and SwapAdvanced do NOT
override it, so they must keep skipping the ratio path. The panel interactor owns
that decision plus the order price, so this getter only surfaces the raw ratio.

MULTI carries no dynamic stop-loss (`OKTMultiAttachParam` has no ratio field, and
`tpsl_multi_interactor::convert_params` drops it), hence "" while MULTI owns the
attach.

doc:
V2 state for `PureModifyContractAlgoOrderInteractor` (V1
`ModifyContractAlgoOrderFragment`, 686 LOC).

Contract-algo (TPSL) orders carry up to two legs (TP / SL) like the
spot-algo state, PLUS the contract identity triple
(`pos_side` / `td_mode` / `leverage`) the contract amend flow needs
to surface on the V1 dialog.  V1 also tracks the all-position-close
boolean which drives whether `new_size` should be sent over the wire
at all (V1 `amendOrder()` body: `if (isAllPositionClose) newSz = ""`).

24 fields total:
1. Identity (8)  — algo_id / order_id / inst_id / inst_type / order_type
+ pos_side / td_mode / leverage
1b. Display (3)  — side / tgt_ccy + immutable amount_snapshot
2. Inputs (8)    — TP triple + SL triple + size pair
3. Contract-specific (1) — is_all_position_close
4. Submit (5)    — submit_state + data_changed + is_reduce_only +
is_dirty + is_close

here is enough to re-anchor the displayed percent — the binder calls

updateMarketInfo }`), and `apply_by_price_rate_linkage` now resolves the
per-leg anchor against the newly-selected base price (MARK / INDEX /

no type picker).

name: on_resume
doc:
V1 `onResume` — host signals panel visible.

Root-cause fix (R-MIG-216): the panel is a child of the main trade
session, so the instrument must be sourced FROM the session — it is not
pushed in. Previously `on_resume` only flipped the lifecycle flags and
never read the session instrument, leaving `state.instrument` empty
(`instId`/`baseCcy`/`quoteCcy`/`tickSz`/`lotSz`/`minSz` all blank) so
`fetch_max_available` failed with "inst_id is required" and the Kotlin
RenderExt could not project units / labels / digits.

Mirrors `spot/stop_double`'s `on_resume` (seed instrument → fetch
max-available) + `margin/mp`'s `on_visible` (spawn the shared
`pure_mp::session_watcher` SessionWatch effect):
1. Synchronously seed `state.instrument` from the session via the
shared `session_watcher::snapshot_from_session` (same mapping the
watcher uses) so `instId` is present BEFORE the fetch.
2. Dispatch `fetch_max_available` now that `instId` is non-empty
(margin path keeps `MaxAvailableManager::fetch_margin()`).
3. Spawn the persistent SessionWatch effect so the instrument +
ticker `last_price` stay live and re-seed on instrument switch,
re-fetching max-available on each switch.

name: update_instrument_snapshot
doc:
Apply a resolved spot instrument precision snapshot to the kernel.
Session projection and the standalone Rust biz-cache fallback both use
this writer. Without it the
internal `self.instrument` stays `None`, so `fetch_max_available`
renders "--" (max_avail stuck `Idle`) and `confirm_order` silently
returns (no order placed). Sibling parity:
`PureSpotLimitActions::update_instrument_snapshot`
(`../../limit/pure/spot_limit_interactor.rs:528`) +
`PureSpotAdvancedLimitActions::update_instrument_snapshot`.

Re-fires `fetch_max_available()` after binding so a snapshot that lands
after `start()` (the usual onResume race) still transitions the stuck
`Idle` max-avail into a real fetch.

Returns a new `LiqPriceRiskInteractor` instance ready for `start()` + `init()`.

convertor.

name: on_depth_amount_clicked
doc:
**Depth AMOUNT-row tap** — caps the tapped depth amount to the user's
side-aware max-available balance, then routes it through
`on_amount_changed` so the single canonical amount-writer runs all the
downstream side-effects exactly once (R-INT-1). Mirrors V1
`SpotTriggerFragment.kt:133-151` `depthViewModel.depthItemAmtLd`
observer (the AMOUNT row, NOT the depth PRICE row — the depth price is
forwarded separately through `on_trigger_price_changed` /
`on_order_price_changed`, matching V1 `setInputPrice`'s EditText-focus
routing which is a Native-only concern).

A1 / A2 (native-layer): the cap is business + numeric logic that MUST
live in Rust. V1 leaked it into Kotlin via `getQuantitySpotBookCal` +
`getAmountDigit` + `OKTNumberF.formatDownToMax`
(`SpotTriggerFragment.kt:143-148`). Here Kotlin only forwards the raw
tapped `amount`; Rust caps + writes state.

SIBLING-DEVIATION (R-MIG-105) vs SpotLimit `on_depth_row_clicked`
(`spot_limit_interactor.rs:3976`):
- SpotLimit's action ALSO sets the depth price (single price input).
SpotTrigger has TWO price inputs (trigger / order) and V1 routes the
price by EditText focus (`setInputPrice`, :118) — a Native-only
decision — so the price-set is intentionally NOT folded in here;
Kotlin forwards it through the existing price actions. Amount-only.
- SpotLimit caps via the 4-way `PureMaxAvailState::Loaded`
(`max_buy/sell_with/without_loan`). SpotTrigger's
`OKTSpotMaxAvailState::Loaded { avail_balance, avail_eq }` carries
only the two raw `SpotMaxAvailResponse` fields (`available` /
`max_size`), so the side pick is done against those two: BUY →
`avail_eq` (=`max_size`), SELL → `avail_balance` (=`available`) —
V1 `getSpotAmtBalance` parity (BUY=maxSize, SELL=available).
- V1 SKIPS the cap entirely in quote-amount mode
(`currentAmtSymbolType == SPOT_TYPE_QUOTE`, :135) — only the price is
set, the amount input untouched. Mirrored: no-op in `Quote` mode.

Reuses the shared pure min `CapDepthAmountUseCase` (R-MIG-066 — the
numeric min already exists in `business::make_order::spot_limit::domain`;
not re-implemented).

doc:
Spot instrument precision snapshot pushed across UniFFI by the Kotlin
Bridge (`PureSpotMarketFragment.pushInstrumentSnapshotFromBridge`).

The market Pure kernel has no `session` handle
(only `state.inst_id` was set via `on_instrument_changed`), so the
resolved `SpotInstrument` was never injected: `fetch_max_available` and
`confirm_order` both bailed early on `self.instrument == None`. This record
carries the precision fields the kernel + `SpotMarketOrderManager` need,
mirroring the sibling limit/advanced-limit bridge record
(`PureOKTSpotInstrumentSnapshot` at `../../limit/pure/state.rs:592`).

`max_mkt_sz` / `max_mkt_amt` are market-specific (the limit record omits
them); when empty/"0" the `SpotSizeValidator` skips the cap check
(`business/make_order/validator/spot/size_validator.rs:83`), so leaving them
blank degrades gracefully to "no cap" — the keystone fix does not depend on
them being populated.

doc:
Which symbol domain the positions/assets filter narrows by.

FR-1 replaces today's single "current symbol" checkbox with THREE selectable
types. FR-2 then splits what used to be one boolean into two orthogonal
dimensions, and this enum is only the first of them — "which type is
selected". Whether the filter is actually running is the separate
`symbol_filter_active` flag. The two are deliberately NOT collapsed into an
`Option<OktSymbolDomain>`: "a type is selected but the filter is not active"
is a real, observable state.

An enum rather than a string id because both hosts must dispatch
exhaustively (Swift `switch`, Kotlin `when`); a bare string id would push a
validation/fallback branch into each platform, which is business judgment in
the native layer.

`CurrentSymbol` is the default, which is exactly the shipped behaviour for a
user who has never touched the new control.

The shared `Symbol` suffix is REQUIRED, not incidental: these three names are
the cross-platform contract for this round and are what the Kotlin `when` and
Swift `switch` arms are written against, so the variants are not renamed to
satisfy `enum_variant_names`.

Intentionally NOT part of the DEX pair fan-out, and it must not become part of it: split

name: get_instrument_filter_list
doc:
Pure read — the instrument list for the requested business line,
used by the Kotlin Fragment to build the instrument filter
chip on the history-order page.

Backed by `BizFacade::get_instruments()` (the documented
instrument-list API; `trait_def.rs:199`), selected per `inst_type`
via `BizFacadeFactory::create_facade`. Returns the full
`InstrumentRecord` set (FFI `uniffi::Record`) so Kotlin can read
`inst_id` for the filter value and `display_id` / `base_ccy` /
`quote_ccy` for the chip label without a second FFI round-trip.

`inst_type` is one of `"SPOT"` / `"MARGIN"` / `"SWAP"` /
`"FUTURES"` / `"OPTION"` (the API `instType` contract values, see
`guides/07-types-and-enums.md` §5). An empty / unknown `inst_type`
yields an empty list (no facade for that biz line).

This is a side-effect-free list accessor (spec §B "List accessor"),
so it lives in the `#[uniffi::export] impl` rather than the actions
trait, and reads no interactor state.

`ByPriceSpPresent.getChosePrice` returns `getSelectMarketPx` for the position /
all-position / algo (`FROM_ONGOING_ORDER`, `isLimit=false`) TP/SL surfaces, while
the PnL entry (`getOrderPrice`) stays on the position avgPx — the two anchors are
SPLIT. Only the contract-ALGO amend host sets this true (its `entrust_price` carries
the avgPx for the PnL entry, so the %-conversion must NOT reuse it). Every other host
— the down-order place sheet AND the limit / trigger amend hosts, whose `entrust_price`
IS the order price the %-conversion should anchor on — leaves it FALSE (default), so
their %-anchor stays `entrust_price` unchanged. Consumed by `oco_leg_derive` (populates
the reverse / forward `change_anchor`, which overrides the %-anchor ONLY, leaving the
PnL `order_price` on avgPx).

fields.name: price_seeded_from_ticker
fields.doc:
One-shot guard for the ticker-driven initial price seed. The continuous
ticker loop seeds `price` from `ticker.last` only while this is false AND
the box is empty; it flips true after the first seed OR after any user
price edit (`on_price_changed`, incl. clearing). Reset to false on
instrument change so the new instrument gets one fresh seed. This
distinguishes "never seeded" from "user cleared" — `price.is_empty()`
alone cannot, so a cleared price was re-filled on the next tick (F).
Spot-limit avoids this by seeding only at discrete lifecycle points
(`prefill_price_from_ticker`), never inside the continuous ticker loop.

doc:

# Deprecated (REQUEST 2 / Image 20)

Stage-2 has landed — Rust now self-derives the new-coin-online gate from
the session `NewCoinNotifyOutput::is_online_blocking()` and projects it
into `state.is_new_coin_online_blocking` via `refresh_new_coin_online_blocking`
+ the `TradeUpdate` branch. The seekbar-enable derive
reads that mirror, NOT the Native-push value below. This setter is kept
only for binding/ABI compatibility (it still mirrors the legacy
`transfer_prefill.is_new_coin_blocked` field for any caller that has not
migrated), but the seekbar gate no longer depends on it.

**Do not add new callers — stop pushing `is_new_coin_disabled`.** The
Rust `#[deprecated]` attribute is intentionally NOT applied: the UniFFI
scaffolding for a `#[uniffi::export]` method re-emits the signature and
would trip the workspace `warnings = "deny"` (`-D deprecated`) lint on the
generated wrapper, which a per-method `#[allow(deprecated)]` cannot

name: is_order_confirm_open
doc:
#55-B — build the per-submit-attempt child confirm interactor.

§J.2 parent factory: builds the render-ready snapshot from the current
the frozen attempt + the fee-only `pre_check` result and returns a child
carrying only that attempt id. The Kotlin host calls this in its
`PreCheckCompleted { result }` handler.

DEVIATION from #55-A (A3 — documented): the trailing PreCheck is fee-only
(`ContractTrailingStopPreCheckResult`, not `OrderPreCheckData`), so the
snapshot renders an estimated-fee row instead of a CMR / liq-px panel.
Live decision-time read of the order double-confirm toggle. V1 reads
`getOrderRemindConfirm()` per order right before showing the confirm
(strategy funnel `OkTradeStrategyPresenter.makeOrderConfirm:382`), so
config-not-loaded behaves as OFF (`get_order_remind_confirm()`
default-false). Pure query (spec §C `is_*`): zero side effects. A live
query (not a state field) because the non-HK path skips
`pre_check_order` entirely, so a submit-time state refresh would never
run there. Kotlin gates the confirm sheet on it right before
`create_confirm_interactor`; OFF -> place the order directly.

name: spawn_liq_refetch
doc:
Re-fetch max-available so BE re-estimates the liquidation price for the
updated input (#79). The estimate is BE-driven, so a fresh input size means a
fresh round-trip -- the local `recompute_input_cost` cannot recompute liq.

Gated to "liq row currently visible": when liq is hidden (liq_px_confirm off /
reduce-only / close / PM), `recompute_input_cost` already covers cost + approx
locally and no BE round-trip is warranted.

Mirrors the sibling `IncreasePositionInteractor::spawn_fetch_available`: reuses
the `MaxAvailable` effect key with `AlwaysCancel`, so rapid typing aborts the
prior in-flight fetch (one-shot fetch -> the dropped future never writes stale
state, the sec J.1 stale-push concern only applies to streams). Debounce is handled
by the request center on the data source -- no Rust-side timer. Loading is NOT set
here so the panel keeps its current values instead of flickering to "--" while

parent order (V1 `orderData.attachAlgoOrds[0].attachAlgoId`). When the order already
carries an attached TP/SL, the amend must CANCEL the existing algo (a
separate `attachAlgoOrds` entry with the id + triggers "0") in addition to
adding the new leg — V1 `ModifyOrderFragment.amendOrder():855-866`. Empty
when the order has no existing attached algo (a freshly-added TP/SL). The
Kotlin bridge flattens it from the order JSON. Additive Record field.

fields.name: original_tp_ord_kind
fields.doc:
NEW-TP-ORD-KIND FIX: the parent order's original TP order-kind
(`attachAlgoOrds[0].tpOrdKind` — "condition" / "limit"). It carries the
LIMIT-KIND (limit-take-profit) product mode, which `submit_amend` echoes
verbatim into `newTpOrdKind`, mirroring V1 `ModifyOrderFragment
.amendOrder():851` (`newTpOrdKind = if (spReq.isTPLimit == true)
TP_ORDER_KIND_LIMIT else TP_ORDER_KIND_CONDITION`). For SPOT/MARGIN modify
this mode is non-switchable (`UniSetTpSlView.isTpLabelClickable` returns
false), so it equals the seed. NOTE: this is INDEPENDENT of whether the TP
carries an order price — that market/limit-execution flag is derived from
`tpOrdPx` (== "-1") separately. Additive Record field (default ""). Empty
means "condition".

flattened from the order JSON by the Kotlin bridge (mirror native
`ModifyOrderFragment.setCtMult(order.ctVal)`). Feeds the zhang<->coin size
conversions when the option biz cache is not yet loaded (amend launched
from the order list) so `get_biz_info_for_id` returns None. Empty for
spot/margin (their conversions are no-ops — identity preserved, no
regression). Additive Record field (default "").

OPTION IV/USD amend anchor context (2026-07-14, device #99/#100). V1
`TradeOrderData.pxType` / `pxUsd` / `pxVol`, flattened from the order row
by the Kotlin bridge. When `px_type` is "pxVol" / "pxUsd" the OPTION
modify form shows the 4-field IV/USD layout and `submit_amend` sends
`newPxVol` / `newPxUsd` instead of `newPx`/`newSz` (native
`ModifyOrderFragment.initOptionIvInput` / `amendOrder():890-896`). Empty /
"px" ⇒ normal coin-price amend (no regression for spot/margin/other).
`px_vol` is the BE FRACTION (the box shows %×100). Additive fields
(default "").

doc:
Bind-order parameters bundled into a single UniFFI Record.

CRASH FIX (2026-06-18, device-proven): `bind_order` previously took 18
separate FFI args (16 `String` + 2 `bool`). Marshalling 16 by-value
`RustBuffer` structs through the JNA-based Kotlin binding deterministically
SIGSEGV'd in the macro-generated arg dispatch (tombstone
`uniffi_core_trading_fn_method_puremodifyorderinteractor_bind_order+284`,
null deref at fault addr 0x0, on every open). Collapsing the args into ONE
Record = one `RustBuffer` on the FFI boundary — robust, and also satisfies
interactor-spec §I ("Input VO ≤ 10 fields → split into a sub-record").

name: is_show_symbol
doc:
Check if a currency symbol should be shown (not hidden)

Returns `true` if the symbol is not in the hidden currency list.
Currencies not in the hidden list are visible by default.

# Arguments
* `symbol` - Currency symbol (e.g., "BTC", "ETH")

# Returns
* `true` - Symbol should be shown (not hidden)
* `false` - Symbol is in hidden list

# Example (Kotlin)
```kotlin
if (facade.isShowSymbol("BTC")) {
// Display BTC in the currency list
}
```

multi-tp / multi-sl arrays, trailing-stop variant slots).

the proc-macro interactor's generated `state()` can return this type at
the FFI boundary (sibling parity: `PureModifyOrderState`). All fields are

so `uniffi::Record` holds.

Income-type kind the leg was CONFIRMED with (#1-P4 reopen memory).
Same `#[uniffi(default = None)]` pattern as `is_limit_kind`: existing
spot/margin construction sites stay unchanged; only the contract OCO
confirm stamps it, so `dispatchTpslConfig` can forward it to the inline
interactor (`set_confirmed_income_kinds`) and a later reopen restores the
sheet picker instead of falling back to ByPrice (change-%). `None` = unset.

fields.name: is_limit_kind
fields.doc:
Explicit TP-kind axis (limit-TP LIMIT vs trigger-TP TRIGGER), Rust-owned:
`Some(true)` = limit-TP (`tpOrdKind=limit`), `Some(false)` = trigger-TP
(`tpOrdKind=condition`). This is the single source of truth carried IN the
config so every `dispatchTpslConfig` call site forwards it — no consumer
re-derives it from `order_px` presence (that heuristic conflated pure-limit
with trigger+limit-order, since both carry a non-empty order price).
`#[uniffi(default = None)]` keeps every existing Kotlin construction site
(spot/margin) unchanged; only the contract OCO confirm sets it explicitly.
`None` = caller did not specify → the consumer falls back to its legacy
derivation (behavior unchanged for spot/margin).

Re-derive the full margin context from the Rust trade core + the current
instrument snapshot. Replaces the Kotlin `pushMarginV1ContextToRust`

/ `TradeCommonUtils.isCross` / `BizInstrument.level` / `MarginSwitchView`)
and pushes the result — it only *signals* that the context may have
changed (instrument change / margin-mode toggle), and Rust does every
derivation here:
* account flags ← `derive_margin_account_flags` (V1
`TradeCommonUtils.isMultipleAccount` / `isAutoBorrow`)
* td_mode + is_cross ← `derive_margin_td_mode` (V1
`MarginModeManager.getCurrentMarginMode`), keyed by the current
instrument family (margin/spot: inst_family == inst_id)
* leverage ← the session instrument snapshot's `lever` (V1 pushed
`BizInstrument.level`; the snapshot already carries it). max_leverage
mirrors current until the async max-lever fetch lands — same as the
V1 bridge.

Mirrors V1's two trigger points (instrument observer + MarginSwitchView
`.marginSwitchMode` observer) which both re-ran `pushMarginV1ContextToRust`.
`is_margin_switch_open` is intentionally NOT set here: no margin-pure
derivation reads it, so the dead push is dropped (it keeps its default).

doc:
Projected open-order marker for the depth ladder.

One marker per open order on the current instrument that carries a usable
price + side. The kernel resolves the price-per-order-type and the side in
Rust (replacing the gray Kotlin `RustDepthOrderMarkerManager` +
`DepthOrderMarkerView.getOrderPrice` / `getOrderListBySide` /
`getSupportOrderMarkerList` logic), so the thin Kotlin renderer only has to
match each marker price against the rendered ladder row's `unFormatPrice`
and paint a marker bitmap on that row.

V1 source (mirrored field-for-field):
`DepthOrderMarkerView.getOrderPrice` (`:212-250`) — limit/advanced-limit →
`px`; plan (trigger) → `triggerPx`; conditional → `tpTriggerPx` (or
`slTriggerPx` when tp is empty/"0"); OCO → buy = min(sl, tp), sell = max(sl,
tp). `getOrderListBySide` (`:278-292`) keys the side off the order `side`
field ("buy" → bid). `getSupportOrderMarkerList` (`:146-194`) filters to the
supported order types + the current instId/instType.

The `price` here is the RAW (unformatted) order price string so the View can
compare it directly against `TradeDepthItem.unFormatPrice` (which the Pure
renderer fills from `PureDepthRow.price_text`). The inverse-contract fiat
rate the V1 `formatPrice` applied is a 1.0 no-op for the spot path; non-spot
rate conversion is deferred.

name: apply_instrument_selection
doc:
Record an AUTHORITATIVE instrument selection established OUTSIDE the sheet —
a route seed (the K-line buy/sell-marker jump) or the "current pair" switch.

The entry chip has to read exactly like the sheet row it stands for, so the
label is derived here with the SAME rule the browse rows use
(`filter_row_title_for`) instead of being re-derived by the host. Independent
of `load_filter_data`, so it is valid before the entries list has ever been
built — which is the point: a route seed is known at page open, long before
anyone opens the sheet.

An empty `inst_id` means there is no instrument filter at all and CLEARS the
selection — that is exactly what the chip's "All Instrument" label stands for.

A pair that IS named but cannot be titled here LEAVES the committed selection
untouched, because "I cannot name this" is not "there is no filter" and clearing
would silently drop a selection the sheet legitimately made. That covers an
unknown line, an instrument the biz layer has not loaded yet, and EVENTS —
deliberately not handled, since its filter rows are event SERIES, not
instruments, so labelling one as an instrument would misreport the row it
corresponds to.

name: on_pause
doc:
V1 parity: `SpotAdvancedLimitTradePanelPresenter.kt:505-517 onPause`.

V1 onPause body (Round 2 SEV-2 close, audit § 9):
1. `removeInputChangeListener(priceChangeListener)` on price
2. `removeInputChangeListener(amountChangeListener)` on amount
3. `removeInputChangeListener(probablyChangeListener)` on probably
4. `setPercentSeekBarListener(null)` on amount
5. `getInputView().seekBarClickCallback = null` on amount
6. `removeDelayInputChangeListener(assetPriceChange)` on price
7. `getInputView().onFocusChangeCallback = null` on price
8. `removeDelayInputChangeListener(lendAmountChange)` on amount
9. `mBalanceLoader = null`
10. `mViewModule?.destroy()`

Round 2 surface contract: empty body — Kotlin's Fragment.onPause
calls this hook so the trait declares the explicit detach-point.
Without this surface, V1 listener detach has no Rust counterpart
and Round 3 / Round 4 listener-attach close has no symmetric tear
down — leading to listener leaks on Fragment re-attach.

`state()` + the order `input` + the `pre_check` result, captures a
`Weak<Self>` (so the child can call back via `proceed_after_confirm`) plus
the order input, stashes a clone in `pending_confirm_interactor`, and
returns the `Arc`. Mirror of `ContractLimitInteractor::create_confirm_interactor`
(advanced runs the same pre-check flow, so it carries the CMR / liq-px panel).
The Kotlin host calls this in its `PreCheckCompleted { result }` handler.

doc:
Resolve the active strategy's percent-input floor (`min_percent`).

Fix C (Phase-R R4): the percent clamp threshold used to live in Kotlin
as a `unify_trade` constant (`Tpsl.PROFIT_MIN_PERCENT` for ByPrice,
`Tpsl.DYNAMIC_MIN_PERCENT` for ByDynamicPrice). Per OKCore A1 the
business threshold belongs in Rust; the Kotlin binder now reads this
echo instead of holding its own const. The value mirrors the strategy
trait `min_percent()`:
- ByPrice / ByRate / ByProfit / PosMarginByPrice → `PROFIT_MIN_PERCENT`
- ByDynamicPrice → `DYNAMIC_MIN_PERCENT_STR`

The kernel keys off the take-profit leg's strategy kind (V1
`ByPriceSpPresent.getMinPercent()` is a single per-presenter override;
SPOT/single-mode hosts keep both legs on the same kind, so the TP-leg
read is byte-identical to V1). Pure query — no state mutation, no
UxEvent (interactor-spec §C `query_*`).

fields.name: amount_percent_guard
fields.doc:
Re-entrancy guard for `clear_select_percent`. V1
`BaseStopFragment.clearSelectPercent` (lines 533-540) guards the
0% slider rewrite so a re-entrant `on_amount_changed` (which also
clears `seekbar_percent`) does not loop. R9 surfaces an explicit
boolean — single-leg twin of the OCO sibling slot.

fields.name: from_slider_guard
fields.doc:
Render-echo guard for slider-originated amount changes. When
`on_percent_selected` derives a new amount and pushes it to the input,
the Compose input re-emits that value one frame later. Without this
guard `on_amount_changed` unconditionally clears `seekbar_percent = 0`,
blanking the slider the user just dragged. Mirrors margin-limit's
`dirty_source == PercentSlider` guard (R-MIG-377).

fields.name: balance
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed balance snapshot — single-leg twin of the OCO
sibling slot. V1 `SpotStopSingleFragment.getAmountCal` percent
branch (line 644-694) and `getNewMarketMaxSize` (line 700-713)
both read `mBalanceModel?.getTradeBalance()?.second`. R13 stores
the snapshot here so the Rust kernel can compute the
percent-derived size without re-reading V1's BalanceLoader.

fields.name: balance_side
fields.doc:
The side ("BUY"/"SELL") the current `balance` snapshot was FETCHED for.
DEVICE-FIX (Buy↔Sell reversed / 0 avail, 2026-07-01): the SPOT
max-available endpoint returns a SIDE-DEPENDENT `available`
(BUY → quote-ccy avail e.g. USDT; SELL → base-ccy avail e.g. the coin —
`spot_types.rs:443-445`). After a side flip the retained snapshot
(ROOT #2 keeps it to avoid a `--` flash) belongs to the PRIOR side, so
deriving/rendering it against the NEW `side` shows the other side's value
under the wrong ccy label (reversed) or a stale/0 figure. The avail
projection + the seekbar percent-calc gate their `Loaded` output on
`balance_side == side`; a mismatch renders `--` (Loading) until the
side-change re-fetch stamps the new side here. Every balance write site
sets this to the side it fetched. Empty until the first fetch lands.

fields.name: balance_inst
fields.doc:
The instrument (`inst_id`) the current `balance` snapshot was FETCHED for.
DEVICE-FIX (coin-switch stale avail, 2026-07-06): the max-available
`available` / `max_size` are per-instrument. A coin switch that keeps the
SAME side (`apply_instrument_snapshot` only rewrites `s.inst_id`, never
invalidates the ROOT #2-retained snapshot) leaves `balance_side == side`
TRUE, so the avail projection gate passed the PRIOR coin's snapshot as
`Loaded` → the row kept showing the previous coin's value AND ccy unit.
The projection + seekbar/market-max gates now also require
`balance_inst == inst_id`; a mismatch renders `--` until the inst-change
re-fetch stamps the new instrument here (spot-limit "switch invalidates"
parity). Every balance write site sets this to the inst it fetched.

fields.name: instrument_snapshot
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed instrument snapshot. Single-leg twin of the OCO
sibling slot. See `PureSpotStopDoubleState.instrument_snapshot`
for the canonical commentary. Drives the `state()` projection so
the renderer observes live base/quote/tickSz/lotSz/minSz instead
of the default-empty values that triggered B1.

`PureOKTSpotInstrumentSnapshot` is a `uniffi::Record`, so the
macro-added `uniffi::Record` derive on this state accepts the slot
directly (no serde skip needed now that serde is dropped).

fields.name: resolved_td_mode
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed resolved tdMode token ("cash" / "cross" / "isolated").
V1 derives via `MarginModeManager.getCurrentMarginMode()` when
`currentAccountHasMultipleAttr()==true`, else falls back to
`OrderLeadUtils.getSpotMgn(type, instId)`. V2 keeps the resolution
on the Kotlin side (the V1 helpers depend on
`TradeCoreProxy.getTrade()` infrastructure that is intentionally
kept out of the Rust source tree per R-MIG-021 / V2 4-goals) and
pushes the resolved token into this slot via
`update_resolved_td_mode(...)`. `fetch_max_available` and
`build_single_confirm_payload` consume this slot when non-empty,
falling back to "cash" for parity with the prior placeholder.

V1 ref: `SpotStopSingleFragment.kt:478-481` (mgnMode arg of
`makeSpotOrderModule(...)`).

fields.name: market_stop_max_sz
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed per-instrument market-stop max size cap
(`TradeBiz.getMarketStopMaxSz(...)`). Empty string means no cap is
available yet; `submit_order` then skips the gate (V1 parity:
`marketLimitMax` returns false on null/empty `maxSize`).

V1 ref: `SpotStopSingleFragment.kt:352-364` (`marketLimitMax`).

fields.name: simple_account_spot
fields.doc:
Kotlin-pushed simple-account-spot flag
(`TradeCommonUtils.simpleAccountSpot(instType)`). When true the
Fragment attaches the V1 `lendAmountChange` listener on the
amount input. Rust does not branch on this slot directly today;
it is exposed so the Fragment-side wire stays observable through
the same dispatch + pumpState surface as other host hints (lets
the audit verify the value is being pushed correctly).

fields.name: is_trading_account
fields.doc:
V1 `TradeCommonUtils.isTradingAccount()` (= acct_lv == "1") mirror —
Rust live read (`setting.is_trade_account()`) in the borrow-config
refresh, same producer site as `is_multiple_account`. Owner directive
2026-07-29: the lend-amount row's simple-account branch is Lv1 ONLY and
the four hidden-set panels (stop x2 / trigger / mp) pass this SAME
literal signal (predicate uniformity — the panels are structurally
spot, so no `is_spot_inst_type` term is needed). Sibling parity:
`PureSpotTriggerState::is_trading_account`.

fields.name: is_available_borrow_account_eligible
fields.doc:
Exact Native gate for the borrow explanation on Available:
`isTradingAccount() || isMultipleAccount()` = account Lv1 or Lv3.

fields.name: direction_hint_accepted_for_submit
fields.doc:
Per-submit guard mirroring `bbo_warning_accepted_for_submit`.
`submit_order` emits `ShowDirectionHintDialog` once per attempt
when the direction-hint gate trips; Kotlin re-invokes
`submit_order` after the user accepts the dialog, but only after
dispatching `accept_direction_hint(true)` which flips this flag.
`confirm_order` resets the flag at end-of-cycle so the next
submit attempt re-evaluates.

doc:
V2 state for SpotStopSingle (conditional / single-leg).

Field set partitioned into 5 groups (R3):
1. Identity & side (5)
2. Inputs — single trigger (5)
3. Display / max / decimals (7)
4. Misc account & feature flags (8)
5. UI / interaction transient (3)

Total: 28 fields. The OCO sibling carries 40 (dual TP/SL adds 12). The
remaining ~70 to reach sibling spot/limit parity land in R4+ as actions
wire them.

name: update_is_pro
doc:
Push the current pro-app-mode flag into state.

core-trading has NO native producer for pro-app-mode (`is_pro_compliant()`
is a hardcoded TODO; `config_factory.rs:166` still TODOs
`OKTradeCoreBridge.isProAppMode()`). Across every spot order interactor
the value is *pushed in* by Native via `update_is_pro(bool)` — this
mirrors `SpotLimitInteractor::update_is_pro` exactly. Native calls this
from `on_visible` / `onResume` with `OKAppService.isPro()` so the
last-price dialog "Learn more" button (`PurePositionListFragment.kt:603`)
and the empty-state recommend card (`:386`) read
`state.config_flags.is_pro` instead of reaching `TradeCoreProxy` /
`OKAppService` directly. Pro/Lite switching triggers Activity recreation,
so a single push at panel entry is sufficient.

name: submit_order
doc:
**Keystone trade action** — placement entry point.

Reads `state.side` (already Rust-owned via the side-tab action; native-layer
A1 — Kotlin pushes nothing here) and runs the canonical 3-path confirm flow:
validate inputs → write `validation_error` on failure (errors via state, not
transient UxEvent — ux-side-effect R2) → route by confirm/pre-check flags:
- dialog OFF: emit `DirectPlaceOrder` then place directly.
- dialog ON + pre-check needed: spawn `PreCheckOrder`; on success emit
`ShowOrderConfirmDialog` (Kotlin then reads `build_confirm_snapshot`).
- dialog ON + no pre-check: emit `ShowOrderConfirmDialog` directly.

V1 ref: `SpotTriggerFragment.kt:380 makeOrderClick` +
`BaseBusinessFragment` submit/reportMakeOrderClick (tasks listeners-018 /
listeners-019 Buy/Sell place-order buttons). Blueprint parity:
`spot_limit_interactor.rs:4688 submit_order` + legacy SpotTrigger
`spot_trigger_interactor.rs:637`.

SIBLING-DEVIATION (R-MIG-105): the task brief labels this `submit_order(side)`,
but BOTH canonical siblings (blueprint:4688 + legacy:637) declare
`fn submit_order(&self)` with NO side parameter — side is read from
`state.side`, set earlier by the side-tab action. Per R-MIG-066 the

Server limit-price correction dialog — Android Native
`OkTradePresenter.kt:1013-1021` / `OrderResultHandler.kt:211-233`.

When PLACE returns the limit-price family (51006 / 51137 / 51138) with a non-empty
`_data` suggested price, Native pops its price-limit confirm dialog ("your order price has
hit the price limit; confirm placing at the currently allowed price")
instead of toasting. Accepting it adopts the suggested price, **drops the attached
TP/SL** (`if (group.attachSp.isNotNullOrEmpty()) group.attachSp = null`, commented
"Discard TPSL when price changes during order placement") and re-runs the confirm.
Cancel dismisses without touching state.

market-execution plan order has no user limit price for the server to correct.

the attempt has to stay current so `proceed_after_limit_price_clip_attempt` can find
it. Kotlin reuses the shared `SpotLimitDialogs.showLimitPriceClippedDialog`, which
formats the price and picks the BUY / SELL CDKey itself, so this payload carries the
RAW decimal string — no grouping, no ccy suffix.

name: PureHistoryOrderListInteractor
doc:
V2 pure interactor for the history-order list page.

# 2026-06-11 session-restore refactor
This interactor used to be an orphan `.create()` node holding no session
tree (the V2 PureHistory regressed from V1
`RustHistoryOrderListPresenter`, which was sessioned via
`parent.createHistoryOrderListInteractor()` —
`RustHistoryOrderListPresenter.kt:87,103`). It is now a sessioned child
node mirroring the canonical `HistoryOrderListInteractor` shape: it holds
`Weak<TradeSessionContext>` and **actually subscribes** to the session's
`TradeUpdate` channel so the history list refreshes on instrument switch
(spec §"Six hard rules" #2 — holding a Weak without
subscribing is a zero-reference placeholder). The kernel is obtained via
`MainTradeInteractor::create_pure_history_order_list_interactor()`, NOT a
`#[uniffi::constructor]` (parent-child tree rule). The `create()`
constructor is retained for the test / standalone fallback path only.

History stays a one-shot HTTP-paginated list (no live WS feed) — the only
session-driven behaviour is the instrument-switch refresh, which mirrors
V1 (`switch_instrument` + `refresh`).

UI-ready *business data* for the position share poster.

Replaces the price / PnL / name / side derivation that Kotlin
`SharePositionDataMapper` + `ShareUtils.positionToShare`
(`ShareUtils.kt:354-437`) previously reconstructed from a legacy
`TradePositionManager.PositionItem` via `TradeCoreProxy`. Native consumes
this VO and keeps ownership of the poster rendering itself — the poster
image, `PlanetShareUtil.getPositionShareModel` planet JSON, theme/colors,
the `AssetShareBean` (`com.okinc.unify_trade.biz`) shape, and the IM share
params all stay in Kotlin (they are rendering, not business data).

Native-source field map (Kotlin `ShareUtils.positionToShare`):
- `entry_price` ← `SharePositionDataMapper.getFormattedEntryPrice`
(`SharePositionDataMapper.kt:216-247`) via
`CTPositionFormatter::format_share_entry_price`.
- `last_mark_price` ← `SharePositionDataMapper.getFormattedLastMarkPrice`
(`SharePositionDataMapper.kt:295-315`) via
`CTPositionFormatter::format_share_last_mark_price` (last-vs-mark by
`isPnlSelectedLastPrice`).
- `pnl_text` / `pnl_unit` ← `SharePositionDataMapper.getFormattedPnlTextAndUnit`
(`SharePositionDataMapper.kt:147-163`) via
`CTPositionFormatter::format_share_pnl_text_and_unit` (sign + SPOT/MARGIN
margin-margin vs profit `fmtPl`).
- `pnl_ratio` ← `positionItem.getPnlPriceRatio()` (`ShareUtils.kt:397`):
the raw PnL ratio at the selected price-type. Mirrored by
`PositionData::get_pnl_ratio` (OPTION always mark). Carried RAW (not
percent-scaled) because Native binds `AssetShareBean.rate` to the raw
ratio string exactly as `getPnlPriceRatio()` returned it.
- `share_name` ← `getShareName(instId, instType)` (`TradeOrderDataExtension.kt:2149`)
across the 5 product lines: SPOT/MARGIN → `BASE/QUOTE` from coinFormat;
FUTURES/SWAP/OPTION/EVENTS → `TradeTitleUtils.getTitleByIdAndType`. The
`TradeTitleUtils` title is a Native title-formatter read (instrument
display name), so Native keeps the `share_name` derivation; this VO does
NOT duplicate it (see note below).
- `share_business_name` ← `getShareBusinessName(instType, instId)`
(`TradeOrderDataExtension.kt:2123`): static CDKeys per product line (+
FUTURES pre-market empty-string gate). Native owns the CDKey mapping.
- `share_type_side` ← `getShareType(positionItem)` = `getPositionsSide()`
(`ShareUtils.kt:915-917`): the 4-way side `net_buy`/`net_sell`/`long`/
`short`. Mirrored by `PositionData::get_position_side`. Native maps it to
the label CDKey via `getShareTypeString` (`ShareUtils.kt:919-935`) — UI
copy stays Native.
- `is_rise_up` ← `positionItem.isRiseUp(getPositionsSide())`
(`PositionItemEx.kt:292`): `net_buy`/`long` → true else false. Drives the
poster rise/fall color + `isLong`.
- `settle_ccy` ← EVENT settle currency
(`(getSuggestedInstrument(...) as EventInstrument).settleCcy ?: USDT`,
`ShareUtils.kt:415`): only consulted by Native when the position is an
EVENT contract and `pnl_unit` is empty. Empty string for non-EVENT.

Why some fields are intentionally NOT on this VO (left to Native):
- `share_name` (title): a `TradeTitleUtils` display-name read, kept native
so this VO does not couple to title-format business that lives elsewhere.
- The `getShareTypeString` / `getPositionLastMarkPriceText` CDKey labels:
UI copy, mapped by Native from `share_type_side` / `share_uses_last_label`.
- Poster rendering / planet JSON / theme: rendering, not data.

fields.doc:
Funding-rate ceiling formatted as a canonical percent NUMBER (no "%").
Mirrors the business part of Native `OKTNumberF.formatPercent(num,
fee_rate_dig, minDigits=0, RoundingMode.UP)`: scale x100, round to
`fee_rate_dig` decimals away-from-zero, strip trailing zeros, keep "-" for

`annual = raw_rate * (24 / funding_time_interval) * 365`, then the same
canonical percent formatting as `funding_rate_ceiling_pct`. Empty when the
raw rate or interval is missing/zero (the V2 Pure dialog shows a
placeholder). Used by the V2 Pure funding-fee detail dialog summary row.

fields.name: funding_time_interval
fields.doc:

Mirrors Native `FundingRateData.getTimeInterval()`:
`(fundingTime - prevFundingTime) / 3600000` — the CURRENT settlement time
paired with the PREVIOUS one, looking BACKWARDS. The sign is preserved:
an instrument whose `prevFundingTime` is later than its `fundingTime`
yields a NEGATIVE interval, and Native renders that verbatim in the
"Funding rate (Nh)" label, so the Pure dialog must too. Empty when either
timestamp is missing/non-positive (interval undeterminable → the Pure
dialog renders its own placeholder).

formatted as a canonical value WITHOUT the +/- direction sign.

DEFAULT_FUNDING_FEE_DIG=8)`. The result keeps the profit symbol (e.g.
"0.00012 USDT") but NOT the +/- sign — the V2 Pure dialog wraps it with
the receive/pay direction text (A2.1: locale-invariant business value,

doc:
Chase-limit amend fields for a "Chase Limit post-trigger type" plan order.

V1 backend contract (`/api/v5/trade/amend-algos`, pre-trigger only): the amend
request carries ONLY the editable VALUES (`advChaseParams:[{newChaseVal,
newMaxChaseVal}]`); the chase MODE (sub-type / distance-type / unit) and the
max-chase ENABLED flag are IMMUTABLE and are NOT sent. So the mode/unit/enabled
fields below are DISPLAY-ONLY (seeded from the bound order's `advChaseParams`,
mirror of the PLACE trigger interactor's chase state shape) and only the gap
value (`new_chase_val`, editable in gap/distance mode) + the max value
(`new_max_chase_val`, editable only when max-chase enabled) accept edits.

Layout by variant (C8):
- at-BBO (`chase_sub_type == BidAskPrice`, chase_val 0) → entire chase area
display-only; nothing editable.
- gap (`chase_sub_type == BidAskDistance`, chase_val > 0) → gap input editable;
unit shown but fixed.

Inline red on the SL section when the SL trigger/limit price is
direction-wrong vs the parent order price. Set by `on_multi_sl_edit_commit`'s
shared `compute_sl_verdict` (hard block, no commit); cleared on any SL edit
(recompute) and saved across ctx recompute (`recompute_all`). Rendered by
PureContractMultiSlEditDialog. Soft limit-vs-trigger warning is deferred to
the order-placement gate (V1 parity), not surfaced here.

row5 (device recvqnuW42kSug) — SL soft-warning force-flag: the "continue
order" button on the limit-vs-trigger warning dialog sets this via
`set_multi_sl_validation_result(true)` before re-calling `on_multi_sl_edit_commit`,
so the second commit passes the SoftConfirm arm. Reset on any SL edit
(recompute_multi_sl_edit_projection). Mirror of OCO `validation_legal`.

red, set by `on_multi_tp_add/update` via `compute_tp_verdict`. Mirrors

fields.name: percent_error
fields.doc:
Bug2 - min-trade-size inline red on the quantity(%) box: set by `on_multi_tp_add`
when the leg percent is below the minimum-trade-size percent (native
`getMultipleTpPriceInfo` min-pct gate → `pr_social_tpsl_tp_order_pct_low`).
Blocks the add (no commit); cleared on any TP edit (recompute). Mirrors
`tp_validation_error`'s lifecycle. `Placeholder` = no error.

fields.name: position_liab
fields.doc:
MARGIN position total liability `abs(liab + interest)` for the est-profit
POSITION PnL, empty when there is no debt (contract positions, or a fully
collateralised margin position).

Derived in Rust (`business::tpsl::domain::derive_position_total_liability`,
native `PosMarginByPriceSpPresent.showProfitAndLoss` →
`SpEarnsManager.getMarginEarn(isPos = true)`), NOT by the host: the kernel
gate needs BOTH `position_asset` (= `position.pos`, couriered as the TP/SL
binder's `openSz`) and `position_liab` before it uses the position formula
`asset - liab*close` (quote-margined short) instead of the order-close
`(close - open) * amount` — see
`attached_tpsl::strategy::by_price::compute_pnl_display_by_price`. Leaving it
empty silently degrades a margin position's estimate to the order-close calc
(device: SL showed -1.92 where web / iOS / Android-V1 show -1.94).

`#[uniffi(default = "")]` keeps every existing Kotlin / Swift constructor of
this Record source-compatible.

name: set_account_level
doc:
Sets the account level configuration.

# Parameters
- `level`: Account level identifier
- `collateral_coin_configs`: Optional collateral coin configurations.
When provided, each element can be:
- "all" type: `PledgeCoinConfigParam { config_type: "all", collateral_enabled: true/false, ccy_list: [] }`
- "custom" type: `PledgeCoinConfigParam { config_type: "custom", collateral_enabled: true/false, ccy_list: ["BTC", "ETH"] }`
When `nil`/`null`, the collateral configuration will not be updated.

# Returns
A future that resolves to UpdateConfigResult on success.

# Errors
- `FFITradingError`: Configuration update failed

(V1 `PLACEHOLDER_LINE`).

fields.name: last_price
fields.doc:
Latest price — UI-ready `TradingNumber` (V1
`OrderLeadSpConfirmP.getLastPrice:32-36` →
`createPriceConvertor(instId,instType).toQuotePrefixNoSign`, HalfUp,
value only, no sign/prefix). Formatted by the live-ticker effect armed
in `on_visible` before it writes state. Blank (`Simple("")`) until the
first ticker push (V1 `lastPriceTv` starts empty).

fields.name: mark_price
fields.doc:
Mark price — UI-ready `TradingNumber` (V1 `OrderLeadSpDetailFragment
.markPxTickerLd` observer → `converterPriceWithIndex(it.price)` →
`OrderLeadSpConfirmP.onHandleCallback` writes `markPriceTv`,
`OrderLeadSpDetailFragment.kt:114-117` / `OrderLeadSpConfirmP.kt:66`). The
`tickers` WS channel carries NO markPx, so the mark is sourced from a
SEPARATE `subscribe_mark_price` subscription armed alongside `last` in
`on_visible`. Formatted by the same per-biz price convertor as `last_price`.
Blank (`Simple("")`) until the first mark push (V1 `markPriceTv` starts
empty).

fields.name: raw_mark_price
fields.doc:
RAW (unformatted) mark price in the API price domain. `mark_price` is a
UI projection and may be converted for inverse/fiat display, so TP/SL
linkage and submit-time validation must consume this field instead.

fields.name: raw_index_price
fields.doc:
RAW (unformatted) index price for the panel instrument's underlying.
V1 `SpPriceViewModel.indexPxTickerLd` seeds this from an immediate REST
fetch and keeps it current through the index-tickers WS channel. Native
forwards the value to the attached TP/SL kernel for INDEX linkage and
submit-time trigger-direction validation. Empty until the first source
value arrives; SPOT sessions keep it empty because they do not expose an
index trigger type.

fields.name: raw_last_price
fields.doc:
RAW (unformatted) latest ticker price — the numeric string as it arrives
off the ticker WS, kept alongside `last_price` (which is the UI-ready
formatted projection). This is the value stamped onto the FROM_POSITION
strategy `_last` field at submit (V1 `OkTradeStrategyPresenter
.requestLast:807-816` sets `group.req._last = data?.last` from the RAW
ticker `last`, NOT a formatted value). Under A2 Kotlin only holds the
formatted `DisplayString`, so it CANNOT supply this — Rust sources it from
its own ticker subscription. Empty until the first ticker push (fallback
then blanks `_last`, matching V1 `data?.last ?: ""`).

fields.name: subtitle_side_cd_key
fields.doc:
Subtitle side-label CDKey (`pr_trade_bot_label_buy` / `_sell` /
`pr_datas_top_chart_long` / `_short`), or `None` for the Kotlin
`else -> "" to null` arm. Derived via `ResolveSideInfoUseCase`
(`OrderLeadUtils.getSideInfo`, `OrderLeadUtils.kt:22-39`).

fields.name: subtitle_side_color
fields.doc: Subtitle side-label color intent (paired with `subtitle_side_cd_key`).

fields.name: subtitle_lever
fields.doc:
Leverage badge — UI-ready `DisplayString::Formatted { value, suffix: "x" }`
(e.g. "10x" / "12.5x"), mirroring V1 `getBotLever(mPositionData.lever)`
(`StrategyConvert.kt:496-503`, `OrderLeadSpConfirmFragment.kt:157`): round
HALF_UP to `DIGIT_LEVERAGE`=2 dp, strip trailing zeros, append the
`LEVERAGE_UNIT`="x". `Simple("")` (empty) when the rounded lever is `<= 0`
(V1 `setScale(2,HALF_UP).lte(0)` -> EmptyString) — Kotlin then skips the
append. The value flows through Native `localizeIfNumeric`, the "x" suffix
lives in Rust (rust-trading-number-displaystring.md value+fixed-suffix). The
append CONDITION (also gated on `should_hide_lever`) stays in the Kotlin
RenderExt (see R6 report).

fields.name: should_hide_lever

the TP/SL kernel's contract by-price PnL branch needs it to compute the
per-leg estimated earn (`compute_pnl_display_by_price` contract branch is
inert when `ct_val` is empty). Resolved Rust-side in `configure_header` from the
instrument; the fragment re-feeds it into the attached-tpsl binder via
`setContractFacevalue` (mirrors `PurePositionTpslViewModel` reading
`state.ctVal`). Empty for spot copy (`configure_spot`) — contract branch
stays inert (BUG 5 / R7).

fields.name: is_inverse

Inverse-contract flag (`ctType == "inverse"` / `FUTURE_NEGATIVE`) — paired
with `ct_val` for `setContractFacevalue` (BUG 5 / R7).

is configured. NOTE: the underlying `refreshBizInfoDetail` network fetch

seeded header so the sheet can leave its loading state.

fields.name: spot_edit_mode

trigger px present ⇒ EDIT (`PosTpslEditMView`, read-only display), else

only when `spot_edit_mode` (populated by `configure_spot`); `None` in

name: convert_depth_batch
doc:
Batch convert raw depth data to display-ready format.

Accepts raw order book entries (bids + asks) along with instrument context
and returns formatted depth items with:
- Price rounded to ladder precision (bid DOWN, ask UP)
- Amount converted per user's trade unit preference
- Cumulative sum amounts and bar fill ratios

# Arguments
* `request` - Contains instrument info, raw depth entries, display size,
ladder precision, and trade unit preference.

# Returns
`OKTDepthConvertResult` with formatted bid and ask lists.

# Conversion Pipeline
1. Slice bids/asks to `depth_size`
2. For each entry:
a. Parse origin price and amount
b. Convert quantity per trade unit (contract/coin/U)
c. Pass raw price + amount as strings (Decimal.to_string())
d. Pass precision metadata: `ladder_digits`, `amount_digit`, `is_bid`
e. Handle special case: price=0, amount!=0 → display "<ladder"
3. Compute cumulative sum_amount per side
4. Compute ratio = sum_amount / max_sum_amount

# Formatting Note
Prices and amounts are returned as RAW numeric strings without any
formatting (no rounding, no locale separators, no K/M/B/T suffixes).
The Kotlin/Swift UI layer applies all formatting using the metadata
fields (`ladder_digits`, `amount_digit`, `is_bid`) via `OKTNumberF`.

Copy-spot EDIT-mode read-only display projection (V1 `PosTpslEditMView`).

One nested VO (interactor-spec §L — keeps the state field count green rather
than flattening ~12 scalars). Every field is UI-ready (A2): prices go through

CDKeys; the delegate rows honour the V1 MARKET / placeholder branches.

variants.doc:
Percentage value with configurable sign display.

Separate from `Formatted` because ICU percent formatting is distinct from
ICU number formatting on native platforms. The native side will use
ICU percent formatting which automatically handles the "%" suffix and
locale-specific formatting.

**Important**: The value is used as-is with no scaling on the native side.
If you need to display 12.5%, pass "12.5" not "0.125".

# Fields
- `value`: The percentage value as a string, already scaled (e.g., "12.5" for 12.5%)
- `sign_type`: Controls sign display behavior:
- 0 (AUTO): Show "-" for negative only, no sign for positive/zero
- 1 (ALWAYS): Show "+" for positive and zero, "-" for negative
- 2 (EXCEPT_ZERO): Show "+" for positive, "-" for negative, no sign for zero

fields.name: sign_type
fields.doc:
Sign display mode: 0=AUTO, 1=ALWAYS, 2=EXCEPT_ZERO

The sign POLICY is a business decision and therefore belongs to the producer,
not to the renderer: a balance/valuation/price must never show a leading `+`
while a PnL must (Native `formatDexAssetBalanceUsd` -> `¥6.66` vs
`formatDexAssetPnl` -> `+¥6.66`, both through the same
`formatUsdValueToLocalValue`, differing only in `signType`).

Before this field existed both Kotlin resolvers hardcoded EXCEPT_ZERO, so every
producer got a `+` (device 2026-09-23: the DEX row valuation rendered `+¥17.32`
where Native shows `¥17.32`). Same shape as [`DisplayString::Percent`] and
[`DisplayString::Pnl`], which already carry this field.

Native cannot be handed a pre-signed string instead: the resolver parses the
value through `toSafeDouble()` before `formatFiatSymbol`, which drops a `+`.

variants.doc:
Fiat currency value that requires full ICU formatting on the native side.

Used exclusively for PnL values that have been converted from USD to the
user's selected local fiat currency. Rust provides the already-converted
numeric value; native formats it with ICU `formatFiatSymbol` which handles:
- Correct sign position (e.g., "-$1,134.64" not "$-1,134.64")
- RTL language support (Arabic, Hebrew)
- Locale-specific thousands separator and decimal point

# Fields
- `value`: Already-converted fiat value as string, e.g. "-1134.77" (no thousands sep)
- `iso_code`: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "USD", "CNY", "EUR"

# Native usage (Kotlin)
```kotlin
value.toSafeDouble().formatFiatSymbol(
code = isoCode,
roundingMode = RoundingMode.HALF_DOWN,
signType = DisplaySign.EXCEPT_ZERO
)
```

variants.name: DexPrice

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Already fiat-converted raw value, e.g. "0.000365"

fields.name: iso_code
fields.doc: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "USD", "CNY"

variants.doc:
DEX token price formatted in local fiat currency with subscript-style notation.

Used exclusively for DEX asset price fields (average buy price, last price).
Rust provides the USD→local-fiat converted raw value; native formats it with
`formatFiatSymbolWithSubscriptStyle` which renders leading zeros as Unicode
subscript characters (e.g. "$0.₀₀₀₀₅" for 0.000050 USD).

# Fields
- `value`: Already fiat-converted raw numeric string, e.g. "0.000365" for CNY price
- `iso_code`: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "USD", "CNY"

# Native usage (Kotlin)
Kotlin recomputes `Precision` from the value's magnitude (matching `formatDexPrice` rules):
- `== 0`         → `fixedPrecision(2)`
- `< 1`          → `significantPrecision(1, 5)`
- `[1, 10)`      → `minMaxPrecision(0, 4)`
- `[10, 1000)`   → `maxPrecision(OKTDexCurrencyAmountFormat.getCurrentIosBean().precision)`
Then calls `value.toSafeBigDecimal().formatFiatSymbolWithSubscriptStyle(code, DOWN, precision)`.

fields.name: sign
fields.doc: Literal currency sign for prefix path (`"$"` / `"¥"`); mutually exclusive with `symbol`.

fields.name: symbol
fields.doc: Literal unit for suffix path (`"USDT"` / `"BTC"`); mutually exclusive with `sign`.

fields.name: polarity
fields.doc: Sign polarity strategy; defaults to `Auto`.

variants.doc:
V2 generic trading-numeric variant — covers price / amount / PnL /
available balance / max-buy / available margin / any trading metric that
needs locale thousand separators + literal sign/symbol + sign polarity.

Rust already handles truncation / trailing zeros / unit conversion; native
only adds the locale thousand separators, literal sign/symbol concatenation,
and the `+` prefix when polarity asks for it. Rendering MUST go through one
of three native entry points:
- `String.formatRustNumber(polarity)`  — value only
- `String.formatWithPrefix(sign, polarity)`  — sign prefix
- `String.formatWithSuffix(symbol, polarity)` — symbol suffix

# Field contract
- `value`: truncated / trailing-zeros-aligned plain decimal string. Negative
sign is Rust-native (`-12.50`); empty / placeholder cases must emit
`DisplayString::Placeholder` instead — `value` is never empty inside a
`TradingNumber`.
- `sign`: literal currency sign for prefix (`"$"` / `"¥"` / `"€"`).
- `symbol`: literal unit for suffix (`"USDT"` / `"BTC"` / `"USDC"`).
- `sign` and `symbol` are mutually exclusive — a value never carries both
`$` prefix AND ` USDT` suffix.
- `polarity`: controls whether positive values get a `+` prefix. Defaults
to `Polarity::Auto`.

# Out of scope (use V1 variants)
- DEX micro prices (subscript `0` shorthand) → `DisplayString::DexPrice`
- Percentages (24h change / yields) → `DisplayString::Percent` (ICU
`formatICUPercent`)
- Dates → `DisplayString::Date`
- CD keys → `DisplayString::CDKey` / `FormattedCDKey`

# Examples

```ignore
// Price "67,890.50 USDT"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "67890.50".to_string(),
sign: None,
symbol: Some("USDT".to_string()),
polarity: Polarity::Auto,
}

// Position PnL "+28.39 USDT"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "28.39".to_string(),
sign: None,
symbol: Some("USDT".to_string()),
polarity: Polarity::ExceptZero,
}

// Fiat balance "$500.00"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "500.00".to_string(),
sign: Some("$".to_string()),
symbol: None,
polarity: Polarity::Auto,
}
```

fields.name: require_current_presentation
fields.doc:
recvuUk4Fw297b: `presentation_revision` only means something for a
background load that decorates the interactor's OWN held
`PureTradeShareState::presentation` (the `prepare_position` /
`handleEvent` flow) — there, if a NEWER attempt lands and replaces
`state.presentation` before this load finishes, the stale result must
be dropped. A caller-supplied, self-contained presentation (history
order / split list — never written into `state.presentation` at all)
has nothing for that revision to protect; checking it anyway means
ANY unrelated `on_visible()` (which unconditionally bumps
`state.revision` in `invalidate_state`) landing during the async
image-load window silently kills a perfectly valid share request.
Set `true` only for revision-bound queries; `false` lets the OTHER
four staleness guards (`background_revision` / `account_epoch` /
`watcher_generation` / manager request-current) keep doing their job.

doc:
UI-ready per-strategy-type order count for the chip / tab badge.

Mirrors the native chip-badge contract "All(N)" / per-strategy "(N)":
each entry's `count` is the **de-duped item count for that one bucket**
(the BE-returned list size, native `originDataList.size`), never a
cross-bucket aggregate.  See the bug guarded against in
`OrderCountData::normal_order_total` — adding strategy buckets into a
"normal/all" count double-counts (the "All Orders" badge showing 13
instead of 7).

`count` is `u32` (a raw item count, not a formatted/localized string),
so it is identifier-shaped data and does not need a CDKey.  Kotlin
renders the badge label itself from `(strategyType, count)`.

fields.name: asset_domain
fields.doc:
Coin-level asset domain (FSP-9744 FR-6a): `"CRYPTO"` / `"TRADFI"` /
`"OTHERS"`, or `""` when the backend answer is not available.

This record field is what makes `assetDomain` visible to the native side at
all. Its native consumer is OKTradeCore's `TradeCoinInfoMapper`, which
copies it onto the Kotlin `TradeCoinInfo` data class that OKMarket reads.
That module is outside this workspace — see `cross_module_handoff_report.md`
in OKTrade. Adding the field here without that mapper edit compiles cleanly
and leaves the Kotlin value permanently null, so the two are one change.

doc:
Current phase of the close-all RFQ lifecycle.

Drives the three visible states in the native layout:
- `Requesting` / `WaitingForQuote` / `Searching` → loading spinner shown,

- `Unavailable` (expired / failed) → "block trade unavailable" dialog + dismiss.
