name: update_fiat_rate
doc:
Bridge pushes USD→local-fiat conversion + symbol.

Round 22D follow-up (closes Kotlin call site Bug T): Round 21C shipped
the `recompute_price_currency_bubble = price × usd_to_local_rate` formula
+ the `usd_to_local_rate` / `local_fiat_symbol` state fields, but the
action that lets Kotlin push the rate/symbol was never added. Kotlin
`SpotLimitFragment.observeViewModel()` reads
`TradeCoreManager.getTrade().getTradeDataSettings().getCurrentCurrencyData()`
+ `getLocalRate(isoCode, true)` and pushes via this entry; the resulting
state update feeds `calculate::recompute_price_currency_bubble`, which
drives the `≈ ¥XXXX (CNY)` / `≈ $XXXX (USD)` bubble below the price field.

SUPERSEDED by self-fetch (Image #6 problem 1, 2026-06-11); retained for
Android until it migrates off the native-push round-trip.

The Rust-held fiat rate + symbol are now self-sourced from the
`CurrencyRateManager` (`populate_fiat_rate_from_rust`, driven by
`on_visible` / `start` / `resume`), so iOS / HarmonyOS do not need to
push them in. Android currently still reads
`getTradeDataSettings().getCurrentCurrencyData()` + `getLocalRate(...)`
out of Rust and pushes them back via this entry (a round-trip) — once
Android drops that hop this method can be removed. Until then it remains
a legal secondary writer of the SAME `state.usd_to_local_rate` /
`local_fiat_symbol` fields the self-fetch populates (last-writer-wins;
both sources read the same `CurrencyRateManager` data so they agree).

F1 wave-5 B1 — push the full instrument snapshot from Kotlin.

so the `state()` projection observes live base/quote/tick/lot/min
instead of the default-empty values the renderer was rendering.

either slot is empty so downstream consumers
(`fetch_max_available`, percent-derive, confirm payload) see a
consistent triple atomically.

Sibling parity: `spot_advanced_limit_interactor.rs::update_instrument_snapshot`
(line 3813) — the Stop sub-panel is structurally simpler so the
fan-out is narrower (no margin-mode / borrow / chevron derive).

# Wave-10 D2 USDS routing fix (2026-06-03)
User real-device (DOGE-USDⓢ pair, backend instId = "DOGE-USD"):
pre-fix Double seeded `trade_quote_ccy = snapshot.quote_ccy` which
for USDS pairs is the RAW backend value ("USD"), NOT the user-
selectable display ccy ("USDC"). Spot-limit sibling resolves the
initial value via `trade_quote_ccy_storage::
resolve_persisted_trade_quote_ccy_slice(supported_quote_ccys, ...)`
which:
1. returns the persisted user pick if it is in the new list
2. falls back to `list[0]` (the V1 display ccy) when empty
3. returns `None` when the list is empty / not USDS pair
Mirror that resolution here so MaxAvailable RPC routes
`tradeQuoteCcy=USDC` instead of leaving the param off (fallback
to "USDT" or "USD" by the backend).
Sibling Rust path:
`spot_limit_interactor.rs:1120-1138` (constructor seed) +
`:2193-2223` (InstrumentChanged handler).

name: validate_oco_tpsl_for_submit
doc:
FFI-exposed OCO TP/SL submit gate. Runs the SAME directional TP/SL
validation the order-attach path uses (buy-SL-trigger-too-high /
sell-SL-trigger-too-low / TP-direction checks → CDKeys
`pr_trade_function_input_sl_higher_value` / `_lower_value` etc.) so the
Kotlin modify (amend) submit gate can block a bad order BEFORE it reaches
the backend — matching online iOS, which validates here.

This is a thin UniFFI twin of the internal
[`validate_oco_tpsl`][Self::validate_oco_tpsl]: it forwards the exact same
7 inputs and returns the same [`OKTTpslValidationResult`]. It adds ZERO
validation logic of its own — `validate_oco_tpsl` reads `side` /
`order_price` / `is_amend` / trigger-px-type from the kernel state (seeded
by `apply_side` / `update_context_pricing` / `set_amend_mode` /
`set_trigger_px_type`) and the market price via `resolve_market_price`
(session ticker → `seed_amend_market_price` override). Additive surface;
no other Interactor contract changes.

The returned record carries `is_valid` plus the per-leg error CDKeys
(`tp_error_code` / `sl_error_code`) and the missing-field markers; the
Kotlin binder resolves those CDKeys through the canonical resolver and
blocks the submit when `is_valid == false`.

fields.name: input_revision_internal
fields.doc:
Monotonic counter bumped on EVERY chase-value / max-chase-value input action.

Kernel-internal, no Kotlin reader (the `_internal` suffix is on the R-MIG-284
default whitelist). It exists so clamping an over-bound input back onto the SAME
bound still changes the state and therefore still notifies: without it
`modify_state`'s equality dedup swallows the notification, no render runs, and the
controlled input keeps the raw over-bound text -- the failure mode hit by
AdjustLeverage (2026-05-30) and attached-TPSL trailing (2026-07-19).

Deliberately NOT reset by lifecycle orchestration: a monotonic counter must never
go backwards, or a post-reset value can collide with a pre-reset one and re-arm the
very dedup hole it exists to close.

name: is_show_inst_id_by_search
doc:
Check if an instrument should be shown in search results

An instrument is shown in search if both currencies are either:
- Not in the hidden list, OR
- In the hidden list but not search-limited

USD quote currency is always considered visible.

# Arguments
* `inst_id` - Instrument ID (e.g., "BTC-USDT")
* `amount_sign` - Base currency symbol (e.g., "BTC")
* `quote_sign` - Quote currency symbol (e.g., "USDT")

# Returns
* `true` - Instrument should be shown in search
* `false` - Instrument is search-limited

# Example (Kotlin)
```kotlin
val searchResults = allInstruments.filter { inst ->
facade.isShowInstIdBySearch(inst.instId, inst.baseCcy, inst.quoteCcy)
}
```

name: query_dual_pnl_for_rate_leg
doc:
ByRate dual-side bubble: compute trigger prices for both long and short
directions given the user-entered profit rate, plus the profit amount.

`is_tp`: true = TP leg rate input, false = SL leg rate input. Determines
which rate field (`tp_rate_raw` / `sl_rate_raw`) is read and which
direction functions are called (calc_tp_trigger / calc_sl_trigger).

Returns `PureAttachedTpslDualPnl` with:
- `long_trigger_px_display` / `short_trigger_px_display` — trigger prices
for long and short directions (new ByRate-only fields).
- `long_pnl_rate_display` / `short_pnl_rate_display` — profit amount
(same for both directions since ByRate is symmetric).
- `long_pnl_display` / `short_pnl_display` remain None.

For a non-ByRate leg, returns that leg's OWN by-price dual PnL via
`recompute_dual_pnl(Some(is_tp))` (per-leg TP row / SL row; device
2026-07-22 #7) — Kotlin still calls this for all cases without branching.

doc:
R1a — render-ready projection of the SINGLE take-profit leg currently being
EDITED in the V1 `MultipleTpSettingFragment` "set multiple TP" dialog.

# Why this is separate from `PureContractMultiProjection`
`PureContractMultiProjection.tp_legs` is the LIST of already-CONFIRMED legs
(V1 `multiplePriview` preview recycler). This struct is the EDIT FORM above
it (V1 `tpView` + `estimateAmountLl` + the progress row) — the not-yet-added
leg the user is typing, plus the "set-pct / remaining-pct" progress. Splitting the
two mirrors the V1 layout (one editable form + one confirmed list) and lets
the Kotlin pure sheet stop computing `calcEstimateAmount` itself (V1
`MultipleTpSettingFragment.calcEstimateAmount:374` uses the Kotlin
`TradeAvailableManager` + `TradeUnitUtils` — an A1 violation). Every numeric
value here is produced by the clean `OKTTpslMultiManager` /
`attach_facade` calculator, never recomputed in Kotlin.

# V1 source map (MultipleTpSettingFragment.kt / UniSetTpSlView.kt)
- `estimate_amount`  ← `calcEstimateAmount:374` (`estimateAmountTv`)
- `estimate_profit`  ← per-leg `profit` (`profitTip.result` / ByPrice PnL
bubble) — `UniSetTpSlView.getMultipleTpPriceInfo:1836`
- `set_percent`      ← `priceSettingInfo.totalPercent` (set-pct)
- `left_percent`     ← `getLeftPercent():449` = `1F.subS(totalPercent)` (remaining-pct)
- `is_full`          ← `isFull():441` = `totalPercent.gte(1)`
- `is_estimate_visible` ← `estimateAmountLl.isVisible:358`
- `is_limit_kind` / `trigger_px_type` ← shared `isTPLimit()` /
`tpTriggerPriceType` (V1 keeps ONE type for the whole multi-tp session —
`showTpTriggerPriceTypeDialog` writes it, `getCallbackResult` applies it to
ALL items).

doc:
Typed capability for the order-detail header's "go to trade" entry.

One value answers both questions the hosts used to answer separately: should
the entry be visible, and where would a tap go. `Unavailable` means "no entry
AND no action", so a host cannot render a dead affordance; `Available` carries
a target that is ready by construction.

Both shells used to decide this in the native layer by comparing
`header.instType` against `"CONVERT"` (Android `PureOrderDetailUtils`
`isConvert`, iOS `showsGoToTrade`), and then assembled the destination from the
loaded VO with a launch-argument fallback. That left two real gaps:

* a blank or unrecognised `instType` passed the CONVERT test, so the entry
rendered and the tap silently did nothing;
* "which identity wins" was a per-host convention rather than a contract.

Rust now decides: the entry exists only for a recognised, tradable business
line on a HYDRATED order, and the identity is always the hydrated order's own.
The launch argument is deliberately NOT a fallback — the header this entry
lives in is itself built from the hydrated VO, so "no VO" already means "no
entry", and preferring the launch value could only ever navigate somewhere the
detail is not about.

A host may still AND-suppress the entry when it has no local navigation
capability; it must never re-enable what this says is unavailable.

NOT modelled yet, pending the product answers the report calls out: whether
`SPOT` + full/partial liquidation offers the entry (today's Android behaviour
is kept: it does), whether buy/sell side changes the landing, instrument
availability, the expired FUTURES/EVENTS same-series fallback, the EVENTS
outcome, and a typed unavailable reason.

name: clip_quantity_for_click
doc:
Clip a clicked depth quantity by the current max-available via the
shared `ClipDepthClickQuantityUseCase`. Returns the clipped quantity (or
empty when not applicable). The instrument context is resolved from the
parent session.

# Known limitation — `max_avail` is `None` for non-PM accounts

`ClipDepthClickQuantityUseCase` short-circuits to an empty string for
every non-portfolio-margin account when `max_avail` is `None` (it needs
the live `MaxAvailResponse` to know the clip ceiling — see the
`let Some(..) = max_avail else { return String::new() }` arms in
`clip_depth_click_quantity_use_case.rs`). Today this interactor cannot
reach a live max-available value **synchronously**:

- `MaxAvailableManager` is stateless — its `fetch()` is `async` and does
a network round-trip; it caches no "latest" snapshot.
- `TradeSessionContext` exposes no max-available accessor / cached value.
- `PureDepthInteractor` owns no `MaxAvailableManager` subscription and
has no max-available state field of its own (unlike the sibling
spot-limit pure interactor, which subscribes + caches the response in
its own state via `fetch_max_available`).

Because this is a **synchronous** FFI getter (`-> String`), it cannot
`.await` a fetch. Feeding the real value therefore requires net-new
infrastructure (a depth-owned max-available subscription that caches the
latest `MaxAvailResponse` into the interactor's state, or a
session-level cached snapshot), not a one-line wiring change. Until that
lands, `max_avail` stays `None` — PM accounts clip correctly (the use
case returns the raw qty directly for PM), non-PM accounts get the
empty-string fallback that already shipped. Tracked for follow-up; do
not fabricate a sync max-available source here.

doc:
Check whether the DEX trade tab should be shown.

Logic (mirrors Kotlin `TradeCeDefiManager.isShowDexTrade()`):
- Not logged in → show (return true)
- Logged in → show only when ALL of:
- CeDefi feature is NOT hidden (isSupportDex)
- App is in Pro mode (isPro)
- User is on main account (isMainAccount)
- Not in demo trading mode (notDemoTrading)

# Parameters
- `is_pro`: Whether the app is in Pro mode.
Caller must provide this because Pro mode detection lives in the lifecycle/app layer,
not in core-trading (same pattern as `is_pro_app_mode` in `AvailableAccountSelectInput`).

`#[uniffi::export]`: consumed Pure-side by the batch-cancel dialog (and any
other Pure surface that needs the DEX-note gate) so Kotlin/Swift do not
reimplement the support/main-account/demo checks. Caller passes `is_pro`
(host-input); Rust reads the rest from its own globals.

fields.name: markers
fields.doc:
Tooltip rows for EVERY sampled x, ascending, aligned with the sampled positions the
series are built from.

The chart library snaps a highlight to an actual plotted vertex, so the native side
looks the tooltip up by that x and renders it in the SAME frame. Reporting the touch
back to Rust and waiting for a new frame instead left the tooltip one async hop behind
the finger — blank on first touch, and showing the previous x throughout a drag —
where native computes it inline (`markerValuesAt`, `MmrImrVariablesFragment.kt:1509`).

The xs are already lot-aligned by the sampler, so this needs no separate snapping step:
looking up a plotted x IS native's snap-down-to-lotSz result.

fields.name: x_tick_precision
fields.doc:
Precision the native side formats axis ticks at: the decimal places of the
instrument's `lotSz`, which is the position-size step.

# Why no tick positions or labels

Tick PLACEMENT belongs to the chart library, not here. Native leaves the x
positions to MPAndroidChart on purpose - the Figma's 0 / 10,000 / 50,000 / 100,000
are laid out space-between and carry no positional meaning, so reproducing them
would invent a precision the design does not have - and caps only the density
(`setLabelCount(5, false)`, deliberately unforced, because forcing divides the
range evenly and yields 20.4 / 40.8 instead of the intended 20 / 40).

Since the library decides WHICH values to label, Rust cannot pre-format them. What
it can own is the unit and the precision, which is exactly what crosses here: the
native formatter renders whatever value it is handed, as a percent or a bare
multiple per [`Self::axis_is_percent`], at this precision.

name: recompute_spot_per_leg_pnl
doc:
Per-leg (TP / SL) by-price PnL for the estimated-profit rows. Bug fix
(2026-06-23): the binder used to render the single merged `pnl_display`
under BOTH the TP and SL rows, so they always matched. This getter
returns each leg's own earn (TP from the TP trigger, SL from the SL
trigger). Only `ByPriceStrategy` overrides the strategy method; other TP
kinds return `has_per_leg = false`, and the binder then keeps the single
`pnl_display`. Purely additive — `compute()` is untouched.

Bug (a) fix (2026-06-24): when the user enters ONLY the change-rate
(percent) box — not the trigger box — `s.input.tp_trigger_raw` /
`sl_trigger_raw` are empty, so `compute_spot_per_leg_pnl` produced `None`
for both legs and BOTH estimated-profit rows were hidden ("enter the
change-rate first -> neither leg shows"). The merged `pnl_display` path already handled this (see the
BUG-A fix at the end of `apply_by_price_rate_linkage`: it derives the
trigger px from the percent and re-runs the PnL), but this per-leg getter
reads `s.input` directly and bypasses the linkage. Mirror that here: run
the rate→trigger linkage to obtain the derived `tp_trigger_px` /
`sl_trigger_px`, then feed a `derived_input` (with the derived triggers
back-filled into `tp_trigger_raw` / `sl_trigger_raw`) into the strategy so
each leg shows its own earn whether the user entered the trigger directly
OR derived it from a change-rate. V1 parity: `ByPriceSpPresent` always
runs `setCalculate*TriggerPx` (percent → trigger) THEN
`showProfitAndLoss()`, so the tip uses the derived trigger.

PRIVATE (spec/interactor.md §D): the math/linkage is unchanged but this
is no longer an FFI compute-verb getter. It is the worker behind the
`update_spot_per_leg_pnl` action — the result is projected into State
and read by the UI via [`state`][Self::state]. Math is 1:1 with the
former `compute_spot_per_leg_pnl()` getter; only the trigger site
(action) and result sink (State) moved.

name: MarginHeaderNativeContext
doc:
Resolved inputs for the projection. Populated by `MarginLeverHeaderManager`
Native-fed inputs (class B) that core-trading cannot self-source. The 7a
self-source migration moved the 10 account/instrument business reads
(can-show-cross / spot-support-margin / pre-market / double-pos /
margin-iso-auto-trans / side-support-loan / need-show-level / trade & quote
symbols) into `build_ctx` (Rust SSoT). Only these 5 remain native inputs:
- `is_lite`: lite/onshore app mode. No core-trading Rust producer — the lite
signal lives in the `account` crate's `AppModeProvider` (not a core-trading
dependency); native feeds it from OKApp `OKAppService.isLite()` (non-OKTradeCore).
- `is_manual_trade` / `is_quick_order`: caller panel context (which host fed it).
- `is_quick_margin_isolated`: Lite multi-currency isolated edge case; the View VM
owns the real check, so the header treats the default `false`.
- `cached_margin_coin_is_base`: SP `"$CROSS_MARGIN_COIN-{instId}"` == MARGIN_BASE,
a plain `SPUtils` read (core, not OKTradeCore).
State-read inputs only (§A); the UI *decisions* run in Rust `project()`.

(FSP-9744). Native-owned for the same reason as the flags above: the host

name: bind_instrument
doc:
Bind the instrument. DEVICE-FIX (2026-07-07 coin-switch stale unit/ccy):
re-project the FULL instrument snapshot from the session synchronously
(base/quote ccy, input-box units, precision, quote-ccy list) + re-fetch
max-available — mirroring spot-limit's `bind_instrument` and this
interactor's own `update_instrument_snapshot` / InstrumentChanged
self-drive path. Without this, switching pair while the panel stays open
left base_ccy / unit / button stuck on the OLD coin (buy button + max-buy
still showed BTC on an ETH panel), because the native full-snapshot push
was removed and the
async session event was the SOLE re-projection path (it can miss this
panel on host-attach/timing). Also restamps `balance_inst == inst_id` via
the re-fetch so the percent seekbar's `compute_amount_by_percent` stops
returning empty (that was the slider-not-linked downstream symptom).

name: on_hidden
doc:
Order-type-switch hide hook (`onHidden()` in UniFFI camelCase).

Distinct from `pause`: the Pure host swaps spot order-type panels via
show/hide keep-alive (NOT re-inflate), so a hidden panel does NOT get
Activity-level `onPause`. Native, by contrast, re-inflates a fresh
Fragment per order-type, so it shows a blank draft on every order-type
switch. The typed amount lives in Rust state and survives hide/show, so
to mirror native we clear the input draft (amount + probably/total +
seekbar) ONLY on this hide transition — NOT on `pause` (which also fires
on app backgrounding, where native preserves the typed amount).

Kotlin routing: `PureSpotLimitFragment.onHiddenChanged(hidden=true)`
calls `pause()` (subscription cancel) AND `on_hidden()` (draft clear);
`Fragment.onPause()` (backgrounding) calls only `pause()`.

Keeps `price` intact — native `SpotLimitTradePanelPresenter.cleanInputContent`
(:909-913) clears only amount + seekbar and keeps the limit price, and
the sibling `spot_advanced_limit_interactor::on_hidden` (#48, device
verified) makes the same choice. Additive action — forward-compatible;
existing bindings that never call it are unaffected.

name: current_tpsl_trigger_or_limit_type_sp_key
doc:
SP-storage key for the "TP limit vs trigger type" preference toggle.

Native source (behavior contract — mirror EXACTLY):
`TpslViewUtil.getTPSLTriggerOrLimitTypeSpKey` (TpslViewUtil.kt:32-35) /
`RustTpslViewUtil.getTPSLTriggerOrLimitTypeSpKey` (RustTpslViewUtil.kt:31-34):
```kotlin
"${TradeUIExtraKeys.TP_LIMIT_TRIGGER_TYPE}-${TradeCoreProxy.isSimulateLine()}-$uuid"
```
where `TradeUIExtraKeys.TP_LIMIT_TRIGGER_TYPE == "tp_limit_trigger_type"`
(TradeUIExtraKeys.kt:180) and `isSimulateLine` renders via Kotlin
`Boolean.toString()` → `"true"` / `"false"`, and a null uuid renders as the
literal `"null"` (Kotlin string-interpolation of `String?`).

This builds the whole key in Rust from [`CTTradeAccountManager`] so the
Kotlin caller reads zero `TradeCoreProxy` state. Both the sim-line bool and
the uuid come from the same `CoreUserManager` session the native path reads.

Parity note on the uuid `null` case: native interpolates
`TradeCoreProxy.getTrade()?.getLoginUuid()` (a `String?`), so when not logged
in the suffix is the literal `"null"`. [`CTTradeAccountManager::uuid`]
returns `""` when not logged in, so to keep byte-for-byte parity we emit the
literal `"null"` for the empty case.

doc:
Delivers the outcome of a `LoadFundingTypeCatalog` request.

`request_id` must be the token echoed back from that event. `entries` is `Some` when the
platform's fetch resolved — possibly to an empty catalog, which is a successful load with
no categories — and `None` when it failed.

`failure_message` carries the API's already-scrubbed message and is read ONLY on the
`entries: None` path; a resolved fetch cannot reach it, because the `Some` arms are matched
first. The host passes the message through verbatim and still interprets nothing: whether a
failure is user-visible, and what is shown when the API supplied no usable text, is decided
here. `None` or a blank message is therefore legitimate input, not a host-side omission.

Cancellation must NOT be reported through this action at all. Leaving the screen bumps the
generation, so a cancelled request simply never lands and never shows an error.

doc:
Account-tier / feature-restriction flags the position-list shell reads to
gate the repay icon, demo-account guard, etc. Produced by
`PositionAssetManager::build_position_config_flags` and echoed into
`OKTPositionAssetListState::config_flags`.

Native source mapping (so Kotlin drops the `TradeCoreProxy` reads):
- `is_equal_or_greater_single_account` → `getTradeDataSettings().isEqualOrGreaterSingleAccount()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:343-344`)
- `support_all_instruments` → `getTradeConfig().isSupportAllInstruments()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:345`)
- `support_one_click_repay` → `getTradeConfig().isSupportOneClickRepay()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:346`)
- `is_demo` → `getCurrentSystemStatus() == DEMO_TRADING.headerValue`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:1118`; same demo session predicate)
- `is_auto_transfer` → `getTradeDataSettings().isFutureOpenPositionTrans()`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:1061`, gates the adjust-margin auto-transfer
path). Mirrors the existing manager derive at
`position_asset_manager.rs:718` (`get_future_iso_transfer_mode() ==
TRADE_ISO_MODE_OPEN_POSITION`).
- `is_pro` → `OKAppService.isPro()` / `TradeConfig.isPro()`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:386,603`, gates the last-price dialog
"Learn more" button). There is NO Rust producer for pro-app-mode yet
(`is_pro_compliant()` is a hardcoded TODO, and `config_factory.rs:166`
still TODOs `OKTradeCoreBridge.isProAppMode()`). Across every spot order
interactor the value is *pushed in* by Native via `update_is_pro(bool)` —
core-trading has no native getter for it (see `dex_visibility.rs:31`).
So this field defaults to `false`; until a real native bridge
(`register_pro_mode` / feature-restriction) is wired, Native must push the
live value through `PurePositionAssetListInteractor::update_is_pro`. The field
is NOT hardcoded `true` — fabricating a value would violate the contract.

name: set_margin_switch_open_trading
doc:
Bug V-d (Round 22 · 2026-05-21) — Bridge pushes live
`MarginSwitchView.marginSwitchMode` toggle into the Rust state for
the simple-account / TRADING-level switch.

V1 reference: `MarginSwitchView.kt:231-234` holds the live toggle in
`_marginSwitchMode` MutableStateFlow. The Rust `MarginSwitchManager`
for TRADING level (`account_level == "1"`) always returns `false`
from storage (`margin_switch_manager.rs:263-280`) because the
TRADING-level switch is not persisted — it is held in-memory only.
Without this setter, Round 20 NF-10 (commit `39d67ca5bb`) wired
the flow subscriber but only called `fetchMaxAvailable()` —
downstream derives (`can_borrow`, `is_available_help_tips_visible`,
`is_fund_source_chevron_visible`) never flipped because their
upstream Rust state mirror (`is_margin_mode_on` /
`is_margin_switch_open_trading`) was never written.

This setter is the single-writer rail for the live toggle:
1. Writes `is_margin_mode_on` (Path-2 input of `derive_can_borrow`).
2. Writes `is_margin_switch_open_trading` (chevron-derive input).
3. Runs `recompute_borrow_derives` so `can_borrow` +
`is_available_help_tips_visible` + downstream borrow-family
derives flip in one tick.
4. Re-runs `account::derive_is_fund_source_chevron_visible` so the
chevron hides in lockstep with the help-tips becoming visible
(V1 invariant — see audit report §1.3).

name: get_cost_price_type

`PureCostPriceBottomSheet` opens to pre-select the correct card, so the
Kotlin shell no longer reads `TradeCoreProxy.getTradeDataSettings()
.getCostPrice()` (A1/B1 native-layer violation). Consistent with the
`get_account_level` / `get_coin_id` / `get_spot_inst_id` navigation query
helpers already on this surface (one-shot, not subscribable state).

doc:
Rust-computed tracking payload for a common-function item click, carried out
with the `Navigate` event so native fires the exact same telemetry as legacy
`topItemOnClick` WITHOUT re-deriving `instrument_type` / `is_demo` (both are
Rust session-owned). Two native tracking systems are covered:

`instrument_type` = `biz_type`, `is_demo`, and (analysis only) `tab`.

fires none).
Empty strings mean "param absent" (avoids `Option` in the FFI record per the
binary-size guidance). `is_demo` is carried as a bool; native formats it to
the string the tracking call expects (legacy uses `"true"` / `"false"`).

Source parity: `CommonFunctionFragment.topItemOnClick` +
`addTrackEvent` (`CommonFunctionFragment.kt:593-793`); per-item mapping owned
by `business::more_tools::click_telemetry`.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc:
Monotonic tick bumped by `on_visible` so a page re-entry ALWAYS re-delivers
the current projection to the observer, even when the projected VO is
unchanged. modify_state dedups equal states (PartialEq); without this, a
header that settled to content_visible=false while the shell was invisible
(the true→false hide never reached the view) would never re-notify on return
→ the view stayed visibly stale ("Cross Nx" on a simple account). Cross-
platform: both Kotlin and iOS observers pick this up (the raw setStateObserver
has no StateFlow-style replay-on-resubscribe). Native reads state() and never
renders this field.

name: compute_amount_by_percent
doc:
R13 — V1 `getAmountCal` percent branch port (Double). Returns
the percent-derived amount string. When `state.balance` is
`None` returns empty string (V1 fall-back — no balance loaded).

V1 ref: `SpotStopDoubleFragment.kt:700-748`. The full V1 body
has TWO branches per (side × symbol_type) combo; this Rust port
covers the 4 main combos exactly:

- BUY + BASE:
* tp_market_limit==true (i.e. TP=market) → `getNewMarketMaxSize`
(which itself returns `available / (max_trigger * 1.05)`)
* else canBorrow → `maxSize`; !canBorrow → `maxSize -
loanMaxSize`
- BUY + QUOTE:
* canBorrow → `available`; !canBorrow → `available -
loanAvailable`
- SELL + BASE:
* canBorrow → `available`; !canBorrow → `available -
loanAvailable`
- SELL + QUOTE:
* canBorrow → `maxSize`; !canBorrow → `maxSize -
loanMaxSize`

The percent × amount multiply is performed via plain f64 (V1
uses `BigDecimal.divide(100).multiply(amt)` — fastnum-free
approach is acceptable for the percent-derived hint; the
authoritative submit-side numeric is recomputed on the RPC).

doc:
Projection for the position-history risk (liquidation / partial-liquidation / ADL)
**detail page** — Native `HisPosDetailsActivity` (HisPosDetailsActivity.kt:71) and its
Pure counterpart `PureHisPosDetailsActivity`.

# This is the PAGE contract, not the list-row contract

The three key/value rows on that page use their OWN labels and embed the unit INSIDE the
value, unlike the history list where the unit lives in the column header:

| Row | Native page label (HisPosDetailsActivity.kt:208,211,214) | Native page value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pr_demotrade_text_order_liquidation_trigger_price` | `"{fmtPrice(triggerPx, HALF_UP).first} {.second}"` |
| 2 | `pr_trade_input_amt` (NOT the list's "liquidation amount") | `"{fmtAmt.first} {fmtAmt.second}"` |
| 3 | `pr_trade_calculator_tab_gross_profit` (NOT the list's "realized PnL") | `"{fmtPlInfo(riskProfit).first} {.second}"` |

so `trigger_price` / `amount` carry their unit and `amount_label` / `pnl_label` are the
page keys. Do not "align" them back to the list-row labels.

variants.name: SubmitFailed
variants.doc:
Emitted ONLY when BOTH consent writes failed (`recorded_any == false`).

This is an OBSERVABLE CONTRACT — do not widen it. A PARTIAL success (exactly one mechanism
recorded) emits [`Self::Acknowledged`] instead, because the failed mechanism's store still
reads unsigned, so the show-condition re-presents the disclosure on the next Buy/Sell, which
is the established fail-safe outcome. Native's handling depends on that split: routing a
partial success here would surface a failure for an acceptance that DID record.

Note also what this event does NOT imply: the presentation is not terminated. The `submit()`
failure branch leaves `finished` unset and does not `unregister`, and restores
`is_confirm_enabled` from `is_checked`, so a retry after a total failure is genuinely live.

doc:
Adjust margin details view object

Contains all formatted data for UI display.
All fields use DisplayString for direct UI consumption.

# Field Mapping

| VO Field | iOS UI Component | Display Format |
|----------|------------------|----------------|
| `max_adjustable_amount` | `self.maxAdd` | "500.5 USDT" |
| `liquidation_price` | `self.liquidationPrice` | "45001 USDT" (buy round up / sell round down) |
| `leverage` | `self.lever` | "10.5x" |
| `warning` | `self.alertLabel` | "Leverage will increase due to margin reduction" |
| `should_block` | `self.confirmBtn.enabled` | !should_block |

# Usage in iOS/Android

```swift
// Swift
let vo = manager.queryPreview(position: position, type: .add, amt: "100")
maxAddLabel.text = vo.maxAdjustableAmount.value.toString()
liqPxLabel.text = vo.liquidationPrice?.value.toString() ?? "--"
leverLabel.text = vo.leverage?.value.toString() ?? "--"
confirmButton.isEnabled = !vo.shouldBlock
warningLabel.text = vo.warning?.toString() ?? ""
warningLabel.isHidden = vo.warning == nil
```

doc:
One UI-ready ladder-level option for the level selector (precision-ladder) bottom sheet.

V1 source: `DepthLevelView.kt:44-47` built a `TradeMenuItemBean(title =
OKTNumberF.formatLocalized(level), selected = currentLevel == level, data =
level)` PER level, where `OKTNumberF.formatLocalized(...)` applied thousands
grouping to the ladder string. In the Pure path the BizInstrument is null, so
the kernel produces this record instead: the thin `PureDepthLevelView` maps
each option 1:1 to a `TradeMenuItemBean` with NO OKTNumberF / biz read.

- `raw`: the level key for dispatch (e.g. "0.01" / "10") — round-trips back
into `on_level_changed(raw)`. This is the exact string the books-WS
grouping channel expects (V1 `data = depthLevel`). It is ALSO the
un-grouped canonical value the Native side locale-formats.
- `selected`: `raw == level_str` (V1 `currentLevel == depthLevel`).

A2.1: the locale display label is NOT carried here. Native
(`PureDepthFragmentRenderExt` / `PureOrderBookBottomFragment`) formats `raw`
via `String.formatRustNumber()` (locale thousands separator + decimal point)
for the chip / menu label — the kernel emits the un-grouped canonical value
only (no `format_with_thousands`).

`state.leverage` stays 0 and the confirm sheet renders "0x"
(`confirm_lever_text` reads `state.leverage`); the b007 best-leverage
request reads it too. Accepts the panel's String form (e.g. "5") and
parses to the u32 `state.leverage` (margin-limit state stores u32, unlike
margin-MP which stores the raw String).

doc:
Round 3.3 stub — returns the BBO-adjusted allowed price the user may

when no BBO violation applies (the user-entered price is already safe).

Round 3.3: returns `None` always (stub) because the session
`inst_context` ticker read isn't wired for advanced-limit yet.
Round 4 wires the real computation:
- BUY  → min(user_px, ask1 × 1.05, stable_max)
- SELL → max(user_px, bid1 × 0.95, stable_min)

EMIT_PENDING(T-ADV-BBO-ALLOWED-PRICE-COMPUTE):
deadline_round: round-4
blocker_reason: session.inst_context() ticker / stable-limit read
not yet ported for advanced (mirror sibling Round 4 ticker pipe).

name: price_valuation
doc:
REQUEST 3 (Image 21) — iOS-requested SYNC query for the price-valuation
bubble. Computes the "≈ {symbol}{value} ({ccy})" valuation from the
CURRENT price (passed by the caller) × the Rust-held quote-ticker last ×
the Rust-held USD→local fiat rate, then formats / rounds / groups /
prefixes it exactly like the state-driven producer.

The rate (`state.usd_to_local_rate`), fiat symbol (`state.local_fiat_symbol`)
and ticker last (`state.quote_ticker_last`) are read from Rust state — NOT
from params, per the contract. The only param is the live price string.
Empty price falls back to the InstContext ticker.last (same as the
producer) so the bubble can preview against the current ticker before
the user types.

ADDITIVE: as of 2026-06-11 (Image #6 problem 1) the rate / symbol /
quote-ticker this query reads are now PRIMARILY self-fetched in Rust —
the fiat rate + symbol from `CurrencyRateManager`
(`populate_fiat_rate_from_rust`, driven by on_visible / start / resume)
and the quote-ticker last from the session's cup-tickers-3s stream
(`QuoteTickerSubscription`). The native-push producers (`update_fiat_rate`
/ `update_price_bubble`) are retained for Android compatibility and act
as a secondary writer of the same state fields. `has_focus` remains a
native-only signal (UI focus Rust cannot observe). Pure read — no state
mutation.

NOTE: a new `#[uniffi::export]` method requires UniFFI binding regen
before Kotlin / iOS can call it; the Rust side compiling is the gate here.

name: create_trade_filter_interactor
doc:
Create a `TradeFilterInteractor` (V2 Pure) that shares this session.

Sessioned-kernel factory for the orders/positions instrument filter
sheet (mirrors `create_pure_order_list_interactor`). The filter
interactor is a child node of the trade-session tree: it subscribes to
`TradeUpdate` so the supported-type set / charge
groups rebuild on a biz-type switch. It sources its tab/chip/row business
from the Rust biz layer (`OkBizTrait` + inst-group data), replacing the
native `TradeInstEntryLoader` + `TradeInstFilterSheetDataSource`
OKTradeCore reads (R-MIG-370). The OKMarket cross-tab search stays
Kotlin-side (migration brief §4); P3 wires its results back in.

doc:
Set a state observer (UniFFI export).

DEPRECATED: callback-based observer. Use `state_stream()` —
the callback observer pins the foreign object in UniFFI's
static handleMap and produces a cross-language retain cycle
(Android GC + iOS ARC).

name: release
doc:
Stop-gap teardown (TEMPORARY — target state is the stream APIs,
which need no teardown call).

One idempotent call at host lifecycle end that breaks the
UniFFI handleMap cycle for any registered callback observers,
ends active streams, and stops effects. On Kotlin call BEFORE
`destroy()`. Includes `stop()`.

name: stop
doc:
Stop the interactor and cancel all effects.

Calls the user's `InteractorLifecycle::stop()` implementation first,
then cancels all effects as a framework guarantee.

prices at the trigger px, limit-family at the order px) so it re-fetches.

doc:

to reflect it into the Kotlin-owned master TP/SL checkbox, keeping the
OCO/MULTI/None decision Rust-owned (Kotlin does no classification). §C pure
query, zero side effect.

name: reload_trade_setting_data
doc:
Reload trade setting data from server (cancellable)

This method forces a refresh of the account trade configuration data
by setting `is_force_refresh` to true. Supports cancellation via OKCancellationToken.

# Arguments
* `cancel_token` - Cancellation token to allow cancelling the operation

# Returns
* `Ok(Success)`: Data reloaded successfully
* `Err(FFITradingError)`: Failed to reload data
